The free event is open to all area educators, including teachers, homeschoolers, and youth group leaders, and will feature door prizes, goodie bags, and refreshments. There is a registration link on the website www.shelbycoiamuseum.org. One lucky person who registers will receive a special door prize.
Londo said for more information about what is happening at the museum, follow on Facebook and 'Please feel free to stop by the museum sometime.'

title: Cyclones have big goals for upcoming season
author: Alex Martin
description: 'We are looking forward to this season after a very successful season a year ago with the most wins and the fewest losses in school history.' Some of the Cyclones wins last season came against Creston, Carroll, St. Albert, Denison, Underwood, and a first round tournament victory against Treynor winning 2-1. 'It was a tough way to finish, losing to St. Albert for the second straight year, but the girls are focused and have high expectations for this year with a relatively young, but experienced team returning from last year,' Boysen added.
content:
After its 2023 campaign in which the HCHS Cyclones girls soccer team finished with a 14-5 record, they are back to practicing preparing for a new season.
'It has been great to be practicing outside this first week with nice weather for the beginning of March, as we are usually practicing indoors the first couple weeks,' said Cyclone Head Coach Jared Boysen. 'We are looking forward to this season after a very successful season a year ago with the most wins and the fewest losses in school history.'
Some of the Cyclones wins last season came against Creston, Carroll, St. Albert, Denison, Underwood, and a first round tournament victory against Treynor winning 2-1. They lost the second round tournament game against St. Albert 2-0.
'It was a tough way to finish, losing to St. Albert for the second straight year, but the girls are focused and have high expectations for this year with a relatively young, but experienced team returning from last year,' Boysen added.
The Cyclones lost three seniors from a year ago, including two defenders, but have a majority of the team back.
'Losing Madison Kjergaard and Ava Miller will be tough to replace on defense and their leadership will be missed as well,' Boysen said. 'Our returning defenders will be sophomores this year, and they gained a lot of experience last season that we hope will carry over to this season as well.'
Some of the Cyclone stars on offense were Aubrey Schwieso, who led the team with 30 goals, followed by Ivy Stevens with 13 goals, Carly Torneten with seven, Kayla Anderson with six, and Hailey Good with five.
Grace Albertsen was the main goalkeeper was for the Cyclones, coming away with 70 saves. Anderson led the team in assists with 10, while Stevens had seven, Schwieso had five, and Torneten had four.
The Cyclones will open this season starting with a Jamboree March, followed by a scrimmage against the AHSTW Vikings March 22, before they open the regular season against Panorama March 25. Boysen talked about what will be key to start the season off on the right foot.
'We are looking to be more creative and less predictable on offense with our experience and hopefully find more scoring opportunities against our tougher opponents with those adjustments this year,' he said.
The Cyclones will have some tough opponents this season, some of which they have not been able to defeat. However with a majority returners and high scorers, Boysen is confident his team can pull off victories.
'Underwood will be tough again this year, and I think they will be the team to beat again in our region in class 1A,' he added. 'It is always our goal to battle against conference rivals Glenwood and Lewis Central, as they are the two teams we have not been able to defeat on our schedule, and I think we have a great chance to do that this year if we can keep those games close. Both of those games are scheduled to be played at Creighton's Morrison Stadium, which is a great opportunity for the girls.'

content:
HARLAN — Students from Harlan Community High School's Business Professionals of America (BPA) Chapter have qualified to attend the 2024 BPA National Leadership Conference in Chicago May 10-14.
Those attending the National Conference advanced from the State Leadership Competition held in Des Moines February 18 - 20.
Chad Swanson and Mark Kohorst sponsor the Harlan Community BPA. Swanson, who is in his 28th year of sponsoring the Harlan Community group said, 'The results of the state competition really highlight the high quality of students we have and the strong curriculum we offer at Harlan Community.'

title: Cyclones to tee-off at home against Titans
author: Alex Martin
description: With a small roster, the HCHS Cyclones girls golf team has big plans for the upcoming season. The Cyclones lost two seniors from the previous season in Timber Svendsen and Tela Schwery. Svendsen led the team with a 9-hole low of 44 strokes, averaging 58.90 per 9-hole courses.
content:
With a small roster, the HCHS Cyclones girls golf team has big plans for the upcoming season.
'It's really exciting,' said Junior Cyclone Macy Mueller. 'We have me returning, Ella Freund, and Kara Kenkel.'
The Cyclones lost two seniors from the previous season in Timber Svendsen and Tela Schwery. Svendsen led the team with a 9-hole low of 44 strokes, averaging 58.90 per 9-hole courses. On an 18-hole course, she led with 90 strokes, averaging 96.50.
'Timber was a heck of a player,' said Cyclone Head Coach Todd Bladt. 'She was really mentally focused, a hard-nosed golfer.'
With Svendsen and Schwery graduated, Bladt is looking to some of his upperclassmen to lead the way.
'We have a senior in Ella Freund,' he said. 'She's looking to have a good year this year. She was right there on the cusp last year and is looking to make a name for herself. We have Macy Mueller back as well. I have aspirations for her, and I think she has some high expectations herself.'
During its 2023 campaign, some of the wins the Cyclones got came against Kuemper Catholic winning 209-217, Glenwood 206-221, and Clarinda 190-200.
The Cyclones also took home first place during a triangular at Shenandoah Golf Course that featured them, Shenandoah, and Red Oak, and the IKM-Manning Invitational that featured them, IKM-Manning, and Boyer Valley.
'We're trying to improve our short game,' Mueller said. 'I know that hurt us a lot last season with putting and getting on the green, so hopefully we can improve that area and cut down some strokes from there.'
The Cyclones will open up their season at home April 8 against Lewis Central at 3:30 p.m. Last season, the Titans finished 12-29 overall and were led by Junior Sydney Thien with 47 strokes on a 9-hole course, and Sophomore Brooke Larsen with 98 strokes on an 18-hole course.
'It's always a big rivalry with Lewis Central no matter what sport it is,' Mueller added. 'We went there last year, and won by just a couple of strokes and I feel like we can beat them this year, especially on our home course.'

title: Cyclones drop season opener to Monarchs
author: Alex Martin
description: Despite the Cyclones struggling as a team, a few Cyclones stood out throughout the day, including one of the top varsity golfers last season. Loudy finished his day with 47 strokes, getting par on hole #8, while Leinen finished with 50 strokes, going just one stroke over par on a majority of the holes. Other Cyclone golfers included Owen Neve finishing with 52, taking a par on hole #3, Gabe Arkfeld finishing his day with 55 strokes, and Jason Erlemeier with 52 strokes, with par on the 9 th hole.
content:
The Denison Monarchs boys varsity golf team set the tone against the HCHS Cyclones Thursday at the Harlan Golf & Country Club as they beat the Cyclones 173-189.
'Denison-Schleswig had an excellent day with all 6 of their varsity players scoring in the 40s,' said Cyclone Head Coach Chad Swanson. 'Their balance was the key as we struggled to avoid trouble all day long.'
Despite the Cyclones struggling as a team, a few Cyclones stood out throughout the day, including one of the top varsity golfers last season.
'Jonas Reynolds had a solid start to the season with a medalist score of 40,' Swanson said. 'His round was highlighted by a birdie on hole 6, the toughest hole on the course. Brock Loudy and Kiron Leinen also impressed me in their career varsity rounds.'
Loudy finished his day with 47 strokes, getting par on hole #8, while Leinen finished with 50 strokes, going just one stroke over par on a majority of the holes.
Other Cyclone golfers included Owen Neve finishing with 52, taking a par on hole #3, Gabe Arkfeld finishing his day with 55 strokes, and Jason Erlemeier with 52 strokes, with par on the 9 th hole.
'We have 7 or 8 guys battling to fill four varsity spots going forward,' Swanson added. 'As the weather breaks and we get some matches and tournaments under our belt it will be interesting to see how they guys step up and improve.'
The Cyclones next event will be Monday at 3:30 p.m. at the Fox Run Golf Course where they will be up against Heartland Christian and Lewis Central. For Lewis Central, their top golfer is Ethan Peterson with 39 strokes on a 9-hole course.

title: Cyclones finish 2nd at Koos Invitational
author: Alex Martin
description: The HCHS Cyclones girls track and field team took a second place finish overall at the Koos Invitational with 121.5 points, just half a point behind Atlantic who won the event. In field events, multiple Cyclones took top 10 finishes, including Aubree Wegner who got 4 th place in high jump with 4'6' and Kenzley Bruck who finished 9 th with 4'6'. Hamilton was impressed with the distance medley team as they managed to take a first place finish with Camryn Goshorn, Van Baale, Schwieso, and Sonderman with a time of 4:38.42, edging out Atlantic by almost five seconds, who finished with 4:43.35.
content:
The HCHS Cyclones girls track and field team took a second place finish overall at the Koos Invitational with 121.5 points, just half a point behind Atlantic who won the event.
'This was our first meet of the year that kept team score, and what a brawl it was,' said Cyclone Head Coach Jenny Hamilton. 'We knew we would have to fight and claw for every point possible. The girls competed hard, finishing top-3 in eleven events and scoring twice in five events.'
In field events, multiple Cyclones took top 10 finishes, including Aubree Wegner who got 4 th place in high jump with 4'6' and Kenzley Bruck who finished 9 th with 4'6'. In long jump, Aubrey Schwieso placed 6 th with 14' 6.5', with Brinley Van Baale right on her tail in 7 th place with 14' 5.75'.
On the track, Lindsey Sonderman took a 1 st place finish in the 3000m run with 10:50.67, beating Anne Miller of Treynor by over a minute with 11:56.91.
The 800 sprint medley team which featured Jaylee Schmitz, Dani Smith, Samantha Ineson, and Abby Broeckelman finished 3 rd with a time of 2:00.19, just three seconds behind Lewis Central who won with 1:57.03.
Hamilton was impressed with the distance medley team as they managed to take a first place finish with Camryn Goshorn, Van Baale, Schwieso, and Sonderman with a time of 4:38.42, edging out Atlantic by almost five seconds, who finished with 4:43.35.
'We were not necessarily expecting to win the distance medley, but each leg did a great job of keeping us in the race and giving the baton to Lindsey in a position where she could compete and win,' she said.
Other highlights included Schmitz and Ari Daniels during hurdle events. In the 100m hurdles, Schmitz took 3 rd place with 16.93 and Daniels came in 9 th with 18.46. In the shuttle hurdle relay which included Schmitz and Daniels, along with Kami Stork and Ainsley Mages helped lead that team to a 2 nd place finish with 1:12.39, right on the tails of Treynor who won with 1:12.02.
Towards the end of the event, it was senior night where Taylor Bieker, Ineson, Smith, Stork, and Lauren Wingert were honored for their contributions to the program.
'They are a good representation of the variety of strengths and personalities that make up a track team,' Hamilton said. 'We will continue to depend on each one of them to use their unique strengths to lead our team and keep the standard high for both how we carry ourselves as people and how we compete on the track and field.'

title: ‘Adopt a Dispatcher' for Telecommunicator Week
description: SHELBY COUNTY — Shelby County Emergency Management will be celebrating Telecommunicator Week Sunday, April 14 through Saturday, April 20. 'During this week, we acknowledge our employees who serve the county by answering emergency calls, dispatching first responders, rendering life-saving assistance to those in need, and countless other things on a day-to-day basis,' said Shelby County EMA Coordinator Alex Londo. However, this year, Londo would like the residents of Shelby County to show their appreciation to those who provide a lifeline during emergency situations.
content:
SHELBY COUNTY — Shelby County Emergency Management will be celebrating Telecommunicator Week Sunday, April 14 through Saturday, April 20.
'During this week, we acknowledge our employees who serve the county by answering emergency calls, dispatching first responders, rendering life-saving assistance to those in need, and countless other things on a day-to-day basis,' said Shelby County EMA Coordinator Alex Londo.
Londo said these 'heroes with headsets' are celebrated every year during Telecommunicator Week, usually with small gifts, snacks, and a meal provided by EMA administration and other agencies. However, this year, Londo would like the residents of Shelby County to show their appreciation to those who provide a lifeline during emergency situations.
This year, Shelby Countians have the opportunity to Adopt a Dispatcher. 'This would be a unique way for the County to show their appreciation for those who are on the other end of the phone 24 hours a day, 365 days a year,' Londo said. Appreciation may be shown by handwritten notes, cards, colored pictures or drawings from children. 'Any way you can think of to say thank you.'
Londo said 'Adopting a Dispatcher' is ideal for individual families, work or office professionals, church groups, or anyone else who would like to participate and show appreciation.
Anyone interested in participating may email alondo@shco.org and request to Adopt a Dispatcher, and more details will be sent in response.

title: Schwieso goes for hat trick in Cyclones victory
author: Alex Martin
description: Cyclone Junior Aubrey Schwieso set the tone Monday at Merrill Field, going for three goals against the Kuemper Catholic Knights, helping lead her team to a 5-1 victory for their second win of the season. The Cyclones struck first and struck early when they got their first goal less than 10 minutes into the action from Junior Kayla Anderson, who scored via a header. Following Anderson's header, both teams went quiet on offense until Schwieso scored her first goal of the game approaching the 10-minute mark of the first half.
content:
Cyclone Junior Aubrey Schwieso set the tone Monday at Merrill Field, going for three goals against the Kuemper Catholic Knights, helping lead her team to a 5-1 victory for their second win of the season.
'Kayla [Anderson] did a great job of getting the ball to her [Schwieso],' said Cyclone Head Coach Jared Boysen. 'Getting it across was something that we were really trying to work on, and she was there to finish on those three.'
The Cyclones struck first and struck early when they got their first goal less than 10 minutes into the action from Junior Kayla Anderson, who scored via a header.
'We don't really practice head-butting it into the goal, but that was probably the first one we've seen in a while,' Schwieso said. 'She was in the right spot. She said her head hurt a little bit after, but it went in.'
Following Anderson's header, both teams went quiet on offense until Schwieso scored her first goal of the game approaching the 10-minute mark of the first half. The first half concluded with the Cyclones leading 2-0.
Not long into the second half, Schwieso got in on the action again with her second goal, putting the Cyclones up 3-0.
Coming into the match, the Knights had yet to score a goal after getting shutout 2-0 by Lewis Central and 1-0 by Panorama, but that changed when Sophomore Cierra Pudenz made a goal, putting her team on the board with 13+ minutes remaining in the game, but still trailing 3-1.
A few minutes later, Schwieso scored her third goal of the night making it a 4-1 game.
'I think our midfielders did a great job keeping the ball forward and our strikers too,' Schwieso said. 'Kayla and I work really well with each other and when she gives me that cross, I'm there a lot of times to finish it, but I wouldn't be finishing those goals if the ball didn't get to me, so I think our midfielders and strikers did an amazing job.'
With less than a minute remaining in the game, one of the Cyclones top scorers from a year ago, Junior Ivy Stevens scored a goal, her first of the season, which would be final goal of the game giving the Cyclones a 5-1 win.
'It was good to get her confident,' Boysen said of Stevens. 'I think at the end of last year she was kind of struggling. Even though it was at the end, they kept playing and wanted to keep scoring, so that was good to see for her.'
The Cyclones move to 2-2 on the season and will be back in action Friday at 5 p.m. against the 3-2 Tri-Center Trojans, who are coming off a 9-0 win over Sergeant Bluff-Luton. The Trojans are led by Quincey Schneckloth with eight goals, Cassidy Cunningham with three assists, and goalkeeper Macie Schneckloth with 34 saves.
'I think there's a lot of things we can clean up, first touches for me especially,' Schwieso said. 'We'll hopefully get a chance to rest our legs in these next couple of days, but we'll be ready to go.'

title: Lady Vikings finish 7th at TC Invitational
author: Alex Martin
description: In the 100m hurdles event, Senior Graycen Partlow earned a 6 th place finish with a time of 19.66, just 1.58 seconds behind Quincey Schneckloth of Tri-Center who won the event. Partlow also helped the shuttle hurdle relay team that featured her, Bella Lamp, Makenzie Pauley, and Adaline McIntosh to a 5 th place finish with a time of 1:20.57, five seconds behind Carroll who won the event. Other Viking highlights included multiple top five finishes in relay races included a first place finish in the distance medley with a time of 4:38.44, edging out Treynor who came in second with 4:46.81.
content:
The AHSTW Vikings girls track and field team earned a 7 th place finish out of 11 teams with 50 points, tied with Woodbine, and 57 points behind the winner St. Albert.
'I thought that the girls competed very well yesterday in adverse conditions,' said Viking Head Coach Traye Pelzer. ' Our middle distance groups had to really face the brunt of the windy day, and I think they handled it well.'
In the 100m hurdles event, Senior Graycen Partlow earned a 6 th place finish with a time of 19.66, just 1.58 seconds behind Quincey Schneckloth of Tri-Center who won the event.
'Graycen has had a great start to the season,' Pelzer said. 'Yesterday was a tough day to hurdle, but she is a competitor through and through. She is one of the hardest workers that I have gotten to coach and I am excited to see that translating to success this season. More yet to come.'
Partlow also helped the shuttle hurdle relay team that featured her, Bella Lamp, Makenzie Pauley, and Adaline McIntosh to a 5 th place finish with a time of 1:20.57, five seconds behind Carroll who won the event.
Other Viking highlights included multiple top five finishes in relay races included a first place finish in the distance medley with a time of 4:38.44, edging out Treynor who came in second with 4:46.81.
The 4x100 relay team and 800 sprint medley finished in second place, with times of 54.27 and 2:04.71, along with the 4x400 relay team finishing in third place with 4:37.59.
'Buy-in has been huge for us this year,' Pelzer added. 'The girls have done a great job attacking each relay and each leg. Our success this year is because everyone on the team is willing to give there all no matter what relay or leg they are in.'
Lamp competed in four events during the invitational. Pelzer is impressed with the tone she's setting as a freshman.
'Lamp has had a great start to the season and her performances definitely speak for themselves,' he said. 'I also believe that her success is indicative of her work ethic outside of competition. Her ceiling will be high if we can stay focused on continuing to do the right things.'
The Vikings next event will be Tuesday at 4:30 p.m. at the CAM Classic Track Meet featuring 10 other schools.
'The CAM meet offers a nice opportunity to keep getting better and to see some different competition,' Pelzer said. 'We are excited to keep growing and keep improving each meet.'

title: Cyclones earn eighth win of the season over Vikings
author: Alex Martin
description: After missing a few games, Cyclone Junior Aubrey Schwieso returned to the lineup Tuesday at home against the AHSTW Vikings, scoring three goals to help lead the HCHS Cyclones girls soccer team to a 7-1 victory. Schwieso scored the first goal just over five minutes into the game, putting the Cyclones up 1-0, followed by another goal less than 10 minutes later, making it 2-0. Two more Cyclones got in on the action minutes later, when Sophomore Kassie Anderson scored her first goal of the game, and second of the season, followed by a goal from Junior Kayla Anderson, putting the Cyclones up 4-0.
content:
After missing a few games, Cyclone Junior Aubrey Schwieso returned to the lineup Tuesday at home against the AHSTW Vikings, scoring three goals to help lead the HCHS Cyclones girls soccer team to a 7-1 victory.
'It was exciting to get back out there,' Schwieso said. 'I was itching to get back out there after watching the past couple of games. I think we put a lot of really good passes together which we haven't done in a while and we needed to get our spirits up, and I think this one helped. We had a lot of fun.'
Schwieso scored the first goal just over five minutes into the game, putting the Cyclones up 1-0, followed by another goal less than 10 minutes later, making it 2-0.
Two more Cyclones got in on the action minutes later, when Sophomore Kassie Anderson scored her first goal of the game, and second of the season, followed by a goal from Junior Kayla Anderson, putting the Cyclones up 4-0.
'It's nice to have multiple people that can score,' said Cyclone Head Coach Jared Boysen. 'It was good to see Kassie score. She was in the right spot at the right time. We tried to get it at the top of the box there. She found that spot, we got it to her, and she was able to finish on that.'
The remainder of the first half was quiet on both sides offensively with the Cyclones taking a 4-0 lead into halftime.
'We needed to not get complacent, and to keep doing what we were doing,' Boysen said. 'I thought we did a great job of passing. We had more time, but we were working together well and we were with the wind. Just come out and do the same thing the second half and not let up. I think we did that for the most part.'
The Cyclone offense continued to dominate in the second half with Schwieso scoring her third goal of the night less than a minute into the action. A few minutes later, after playing goalkeeper the entire first half, Senior Hailey Good scored her first goal of the night and seventh of the season.
Not long after Good's goal, Sophomore Carly Torneten found the net, putting the Cyclones up 7-0, which would be their final goal of the game. Sophomore Viking Halle Goodman got her team on the board approaching the halfway mark of the second half, but the Cyclones won easily 7-1, moving their record to 8-7 on the season. The Vikings fall to 1-11.
The Cyclones next game will be on the road Monday at 5 p.m. against the 2-7 Creston Panthers for their regular season finale.
'At the end of the season, we've got to have some confidence,' Schwieso said. 'Any win it matters a lot to keep us going and keep our spirits up. I think it's a good little break for us because we have a big week next week and we're excited to keep going.'
For the Vikings, their regular season has concluded. They will open up Regional play in the Class 1A – Region 6 Game starting at home Monday at 7 p.m. against the 0-10 Greene County Rams. The Rams are led by Esther Van Horn with one goal and Lucy Vander Linden with 137 saves.

title: Lady Vikings advance to next round with OT victory
author: Alex Martin
description: With just over two minutes remaining in regulation, it looked like the AHSTW Vikings girls soccer team may be headed home early, but Junior Viking Claire Mertz saved the day when she kicked the ball from over 20 feet out, as it just barely went out of reach of Sophomore Rams goalkeeper Lucy Vander Linden to tie the game at three goals apiece. The game started off with an early goal from Senior Ram Esther Van Horn just a little over two minutes into the action, which was followed by a game tying goal by Goodman less than a minute later. Within 10 minutes of Goodman's second goal, Van Horn added another two goals to turn the tables on the Vikings, giving the Rams a 3-2 lead at halftime.
content:
With just over two minutes remaining in regulation, it looked like the AHSTW Vikings girls soccer team may be headed home early, but Junior Viking Claire Mertz saved the day when she kicked the ball from over 20 feet out, as it just barely went out of reach of Sophomore Rams goalkeeper Lucy Vander Linden to tie the game at three goals apiece. The Vikings would later win in overtime 4-3 for their second win of the season.
'Oh gosh, that was good,' said Viking Sophomore Halle Goodman of Mertz's goal. 'Everyone's been yelling at her to shoot it from far, and her finally getting it in the back of the net, it was cool to see.'
The game started off with an early goal from Senior Ram Esther Van Horn just a little over two minutes into the action, which was followed by a game tying goal by Goodman less than a minute later.
Both sides went quiet on offense until Goodman added her second goal of the game, giving her team their first lead of the night at 2-1.
'She has one heck of a left leg, so she could definitely shoot from afar on those corners,' Mertz said of Goodman. 'We're very lucky to have her on our team. She's only a sophomore and she has so many years ahead of her to go, so she'll continue to keep going and get better.'
Within 10 minutes of Goodman's second goal, Van Horn added another two goals to turn the tables on the Vikings, giving the Rams a 3-2 lead at halftime.
'Beth [Herbst] has definitely said to us the whole season to never give up, and our bodies can do amazing things,' Mertz said. 'We definitely showed that I think by never giving up, and we pushed through for sure.'
When the second half began, both teams continued to exchange passes, but nothing came of it until Mertz saved the Vikings season with her game tying goal to force the game into overtime.
The Vikings went through a quiet first overtime period, and it looked like they were headed for a second scoreless overtime until Sophomore Alondra Vargas connected for a goal giving the Vikings the victory, and punching their ticket to the next round of the playoffs.
'I was thinking one of these has to go in,' Mertz added. 'Keep crashing, we got it, and the ball went in, it was a great feeling all around.'
They will be taking on the 13-2 Underwood Eagles Wednesday on the road at 7 p.m. in the Class 1A – Region 6 Tournament Game. The Eagles are led by Tieler Hull with 20 goals, Raegan Ward with nine assists, and goalkeeper Avery Honan with 34 assists.
'We just need to keep our heads up,' Goodman said. 'We can't go in thinking we're going to lose. We've just got to believe in ourselves and I think we can compete with them.'

title: Cyclones mauled by Tigers at home
author: Alex Martin
description: It didn't take long for the ADM Tigers to put away the HCHS Cyclones softball team as they opened the game dropping an 8-spot with contributions from Kaylee Smith, who had two triples and Aleah Johnson who had a home run with six runs batted in throughout the night leading them to a 15-2 victory. The Cyclones were able to answer back on offense in the bottom of the 1 st inning when Freshman Taylor Heese came up and connected for a home run that bounced off the top of the fence and went over. 'It was exciting to watch and seeing how all the girls reacted to it, and I think it helped the girls gain more confidence that things are possible, and as long as we keep our bats going, we can get some good hits and some runs brought in.'
content:
It didn't take long for the ADM Tigers to put away the HCHS Cyclones softball team as they opened the game dropping an 8-spot with contributions from Kaylee Smith, who had two triples and Aleah Johnson who had a home run with six runs batted in throughout the night leading them to a 15-2 victory.
'I think the struggle right now is we are playing some really, really good teams,' said Cyclone Head Coach Tarah Devlin Lawler. 'They're state ranked and we knew going into it, it was tough competition. We just ask that the girls compete and they did well.'
The Cyclones were able to answer back on offense in the bottom of the 1 st inning when Freshman Taylor Heese came up and connected for a home run that bounced off the top of the fence and went over.
'It was a huge hit,' Devlin-Lawler said of Heese's home run. 'It was exciting to watch and seeing how all the girls reacted to it, and I think it helped the girls gain more confidence that things are possible, and as long as we keep our bats going, we can get some good hits and some runs brought in.'
The Tiger offense came alive once again in the top of the 4 th inning scoring another six runs. When the Cyclones came to bat in the bottom half of the inning, they were unable score, dropping the game via the mercy rule.
The Cyclones returned to action Saturday in a tournament at MVAOCOU High School, playing the 0-2 Hinton Blackhawks. Offensively, the Blackhawks are led by Ashlyn Kovarna with three hits and two runs batted in. In pitching, Kayla Sypersma has five strikeouts with a 2.76 earned average.
'We're excited for the tournament just to get some reps and looks at the ball and kind of get us going before we start playing in the conference,' Devlin-Lawler said.

title: First inning proves costly for Vikings
author: Alex Martin
description: AHSTW Vikings eighth grader Etta Partlow struggled out of the gate Friday night allowing seven runs to the Riverside Bulldogs, which proved to be the difference in the game as the Vikings would lose their first game of the season 10-4. The inning finally came to an end when Freshman Viking Bella Lamp made a diving catch in center field to end the half inning. Following the top of the 1 st inning, both sides went quiet with their bats until the top of the fifth inning when Etta Partlow walked, followed by Addison Carrol with a sacrifice fly to advance Etta to second base.
content:
AHSTW Vikings eighth grader Etta Partlow struggled out of the gate Friday night allowing seven runs to the Riverside Bulldogs, which proved to be the difference in the game as the Vikings would lose their first game of the season 10-4.
'It was a tough inning there, but after that she seemed to be able to pick it up,' said Vikings Head Coach Katie Pace. 'She's coming back. We haven't had her and didn't think that we were going to have her at the first part of the season, so we're just coming back. She's doing a great job as an eighth grader. We have a young team.'
The inning finally came to an end when Freshman Viking Bella Lamp made a diving catch in center field to end the half inning.
Following the top of the 1 st inning, both sides went quiet with their bats until the top of the fifth inning when Etta Partlow walked, followed by Addison Carrol with a sacrifice fly to advance Etta to second base. Then came the future Kansas Wesleyan softball player in Graycen Partlow who connected at the plate for an RBI single scoring her sister to get the Vikings on the board, followed by an RBI double by Lorelai Wahling to make it 7-2.
'It just takes one,' Pace said. 'We talk about strength. It just takes one person to get going and then they believe in themselves and believe that they can do it.'
Etta Partlow got into some minor trouble in the bottom of the fifth inning when Bulldog eighth grader Peyton Schafer started the inning with a double, which was followed by an RBI single by Junior Ayla Richardson who knocked in Ashley Kelley, who came in to courtesy run for Schafer, making it an 8-2 game. Freshman Kayden Schnack connected for an RBI single at the plate, which would widen the Bulldog lead.
Wahling came in the bottom of the sixth inning to shutdown the Bulldog offense keeping the game at an 8-run deficit entering the final inning.
'Lorelai does a fantastic job and steps up whenever we need her to,' Pace said. 'She came in, she did what we she was supposed to do, and did a great job.'
In the top of the seventh inning, the Vikings proved they weren't going to go down without a fight when Wahling connected at the plate for a 2-run double, bringing the Vikings within six runs of the Bulldogs, but unfortunately came up empty after that for the loss.
'I'm very proud of them,' Pace added. 'We had a conversation out there in regards to the scoreboard might not show what we wanted it to show, but that's okay. Our focus all year has been growth. We only have a couple of upperclassmen, but our focus this year is been getting better every and everyday, each and every practice, each and every game.'
The Vikings return home Tuesday at 7:15 p.m. to play the Treynor Cardinals. The Cardinals during their 2023 campaign went 16-10 and were led by Jadyn Huisman with 36 hits and 42 runs batted in, along with Delaney Mathews on the mound with 13 wins and 107 strikeouts in 115 2/3 innings pitched.
'We're going to reset here,' Pace said. 'We'll just go back to the basics and fundamentals of things.'

title: Bieker's faith gets tested during surgery
author: Alex Martin
description: With a sense of fear moments before surgery, but knowing she had a great doctor and her mother by her side, 2022 HCHS graduate and current Harding University student Kaia Bieker anxiously awaited entering the operating room for a knee surgery. content:
With a sense of fear moments before surgery, but knowing she had a great doctor and her mother by her side, 2022 HCHS graduate and current Harding University student Kaia Bieker anxiously awaited entering the operating room for a knee surgery.
'I was kind of afraid, but I was praying to God that everything would go well,' Bieker said. 'I was a little bit in fear, but also very much trusting that this was the right thing to do and comforted by my doctor.'
Bieker missed out on her sophomore season of track and field due to having a knee problem, a problem that's been with her since birth.
'I've kind of dealt with this knee problem off and on, but have never gone to a doctor who could tell me what it really was,' Bieker said. 'I was born with an extra tissue, extra tendon in my knee. It's kind of like if a duck has webbed feet, I had some extra webbing in my knee, and the doctor said I don't know how you've been training, but you're about to feel a lot better if we do a surgery on this, and clean it up, and sure enough we went ahead and had the surgery.'
Bieker has spent the last two years of her life at Harding University, a private university in Searcy, Arkansas where she's a member of the cross country and track team.
Bieker was also a member of the cross country and track team at HCHS, where she was coached by Doug Renkly and Jenny Hamilton, both of whom she gives a lot of credit to for her success in her college athletic endeavors.
'All the coaches that I've had along the way, including Coach Renkly, Coach Hamilton,' Bieker said. 'He [Renkly] kind of became a father figure for me and in so many ways, he built me up and made me ready for college running, not just physically, but also mentally, and I would not be the college runner I am today if it wasn't for him. I will always appreciate him. Coach Hamilton, I remember my last year of track I had her, and I still remember saying a prayer with her before the Drake Relays, which I was very fortunate to get to go to in the open 800.'
Outside of her athletics, Bieker has enjoyed the college life and being around a college setting.
'I think my favorite part about being in college the last two years so far is the people I've met and the connections I've made,' she said. 'Our track team is very international heavy. We have a lot of people from different states in the U.S., so we have so many different personalities to become friends with and learn from. I have a lot of teachers who bring a lot of expertise to the college of business and my college is a little bit different because it's a little bit smaller, so my teachers are very personable. They invite us to our house for bible studies. As far as my academics go, I've been enjoying being part of a lot of different organizations and clubs.'
Following her surgery, the road to recovery hasn't been an easy one, but Bieker has taken steps through physical therapy, along with a bible verse, Isaiah 40:31, which according to her, has made a huge impact on her faith.
Bieker's new season of cross country is not far down the road. She hopes to be ready to go and be stronger than ever.
'I'm so excited just to compete again,' she said. 'Track is definitely my priority. I will be running cross country, but I'll be training a lot with the sprinters this season, so I'm ready for that 800. My goal is to go to Nationals and place well at that, but I'm just excited to compete again.'

title: Cyclones take back end of doubleheader
author: Alex Martin
description: In the bottom of the ninth inning during game two of Monday's home softball doubleheader, Senior Cyclone Lilyana Albertsen was up to bat when she connected at the plate, dumping a base hit into shallow left field scoring Freshman Aubree Wegner from second base to earn a 6-5 victory, their third win of the season. In the first game of their doubleheader, Freshman Cyclone Camryn Goshorn got the ball to start the night in the circle pitching 2.1 innings, giving up six runs on two hits and walking six batters, while striking out five. In the bottom of the 5 th inning, Frohlich was at the plate and connected for an RBI double, putting her team down 6-4, and later in the bottom of the sixth inning, the Cyclones added two more runs when Tatum Lacy came in to pinch hit and knocked in a run on an RBI groundout scoring Kaitlynn Schmitz who came in to courtesy run for Suzy Kenkel, followed by Heese knocking in Tobi Bachman making it a 9-6 game after she came in to run for Schmitz.
content:
In the bottom of the ninth inning during game two of Monday's home softball doubleheader, Senior Cyclone Lilyana Albertsen was up to bat when she connected at the plate, dumping a base hit into shallow left field scoring Freshman Aubree Wegner from second base to earn a 6-5 victory, their third win of the season.
'Truthfully, I was pretty nervous going up,' Albertsen said. 'I not only had to be confident at the plate, but I had to put that ball in play, I had to get it down so we could get a run. Aubree was the perfect person to have out there. She's aggressive and she's fast.'
In the first game of their doubleheader, Freshman Cyclone Camryn Goshorn got the ball to start the night in the circle pitching 2.1 innings, giving up six runs on two hits and walking six batters, while striking out five. Following Goshorn's outing, Lauren Schmitz took over in the circle and pitched the remainder of the game, giving up three runs on five hits, striking out three hitters.
However, the Cyclone offense as of late has been coming together more and was able to get contributions up and down the lineup, including three hits from Taylor Heese and Teya Frohlich, and two each from Wegner and Albertsen.
In the bottom of the 5 th inning, Frohlich was at the plate and connected for an RBI double, putting her team down 6-4, and later in the bottom of the sixth inning, the Cyclones added two more runs when Tatum Lacy came in to pinch hit and knocked in a run on an RBI groundout scoring Kaitlynn Schmitz who came in to courtesy run for Suzy Kenkel, followed by Heese knocking in Tobi Bachman making it a 9-6 game after she came in to run for Schmitz. The Cyclones couldn't score anymore dropping game one of their doubleheader, but head coach Tarah Devlin-Lawler was pleased with the adjustments the girls have made as of late in the batters box.
'Being able to be patient and have some discipline in the batters box and be able to wait for a pitch that's in the strike zone,' Devlin-Lawler said. 'Making sure they are swinging at pitches that are good and hittable.'
In game two of their doubleheader, Schmitz returned to the circle and went the distance pitching all nine innings, allowing five runs on seven hits, walking three, and striking out two batters.
'She's done a really great job,' Devlin-Lawler said of Schmitz. 'Just being able to keep up with everybody out there and she's been throwing really well.'
A big moment came in the bottom of the fifth inning with the game tied at three and Heese stepped to the plate and hammered a ball that went over the left field fence and behind the batting cages for her third home run of the season to put her team in front at 4-3.
'I was so excited for her,' Albertsen said of Heese. 'She was due. She's hit two this season. Not only did that score a run, but it got the whole dugout up and it changed the whole atmosphere of the game. It changed it for the positive.'
The Cyclones were able to add another run following Heese's home run, but Shenandoah came right back with two runs of their own in the top of the sixth inning to tie the game at five runs apiece.
The next few innings went quiet until Albertsen connected for a walk-off single in the bottom of the ninth scoring Wegner to give her team the victory after dropping game one of their doubleheader.
'It was amazing to see and just watching Aubree make that read and be able to see Lily's face when I told that ball was dropping,' Devlin-Lawler said. 'I'll remember that face on Lily for a while, but it was just amazing to see these girls come together and be able to make a play here at the end.'
The Cyclones move at 3-23 overall and return to action Wednesday on the road at 7 p.m. against the 16-12 Sioux Cith East Black Raiders. Offensively, the Black Raiders are led by Leah Conlon batting .515 with 52 hits and 30 runs batted in. In pitching, Brooklyn Johns has seven wins with 39 strikeouts, while Olivia Mentzer leads the team in earned run average with 4.00.
'We're going in and striving to compete with teams, and that's what's key for us,' Albertsen said. 'Sometimes we catch ourselves getting down a little bit knowing teams are big and good, but just like this game, we come in and we put runs on the board.'

title: Cyclones get both games of doubleheader
author: Alex Martin
description: In game one, Senior Cyclone Caleb Schleis took the mound and went six innings, throwing 94 pitches and left the game with an 8-2 lead. In the bottom of the third, the Cyclones took their first lead when Koesters walked to start the inning, Schneider singled to move Koesters into scoring position, Hayden Soma walked to load the bases, and Jozef Reisz walked to bring Koesters in as the Cyclones led 2-1 after three innings. Schleis returned to the mound for a 12-pitch top of the fourth inning, but in the bottom half, the Cyclones busted the game wide open dropping five runs on the Mustang defense.
content:
The phrase 'next man up' is commonly uttered in sports, and during Monday's home doubleheader for the HCHS Cyclones baseball team, Freshman Colton Schneider came out of the bullpen in both games, helping lead his team to victories of 8-5 and 5-4.
'I was just trying to put it over the middle and make my defense make plays,' Schneider said. 'Just throwing the fastball and a few curveballs.'
In game one, Senior Cyclone Caleb Schleis took the mound and went six innings, throwing 94 pitches and left the game with an 8-2 lead.
'Schleis battled out of some jams early on in the first game,' said Cyclone Head Coach Heath Stein.
Schleis gave up a run in the top of the first inning when Senior Mustang Hunter Dukes hit an RBI double to give his team an early 1-0 lead. The Cyclones answered back right away in the bottom of the first when Matthew Sorfonden and Quinn Koesters opened the inning with back-to-back singles. Those were was followed by a sacrifice fly to right field by Schneider, moving Sorfonden to third base, allowing him to score due to a subsequent overthrow, tying the game at one.
In the bottom of the third, the Cyclones took their first lead when Koesters walked to start the inning, Schneider singled to move Koesters into scoring position, Hayden Soma walked to load the bases, and Jozef Reisz walked to bring Koesters in as the Cyclones led 2-1 after three innings.
Schleis returned to the mound for a 12-pitch top of the fourth inning, but in the bottom half, the Cyclones busted the game wide open dropping five runs on the Mustang defense. It all started with back-to-back walks by Foxx Argotsinger and Weston Reisz, and another set of back-to-back walks with the bases loaded by Koesters and Schneider, making it a 4-1 game. Brett Heese hit into a fielders choice to score Sorfonden, followed by an RBI groundout from Soma, and an RBI single by Jozef Reisz as the Cyclones led 7-1 at the end of four.
'We definitely should have put up a few more crooked numbers early,' Stein said. 'We kind of took what they gave us in that inning, so good approaches making their guy work and putting a lot of runs up in that inning.'
The Cyclones were able to score another run in the bottom of the fifth when Schneider hit a sacrifice fly, and Sorfonden scored to make it an 8-1 game. The Mustangs offense got that run right back in the top of the sixth when Senior Camden Lorimor connected for an RBI single, bringing his team back within six runs at 8-2.
In the top of the seventh inning, Koesters took over out of the bullpen, allowing two runs. Stein replaced him with Schneider, who got the final two outs and the game one victory 8-4.
'It was pretty uncharacteristic for Quinn to struggle in those moments,' Stein added. 'It's nice to have a couple guys in the bullpen like Quinn and Colton, so if one doesn't have it, the other one should.'
In game two, Weston Reisz got the ball to start the game for the Cyclones and pitched five innings and threw over 100 pitches. He still managed to exit the mound with his team leading.
'His pitch count climbed up,' Stein said of Reisz. 'Some of those misses were quite a bit out of the zone, which is not like him. But tough elements, tough day to go out there and get on the mound. He did a great job getting us where we needed to be.'
The Cyclones were able to take an early lead on the Mustangs in the bottom of the first when Schneider knocked in Sorfonden on an RBI groundout to make it a 1-0 game.
The Cyclones offense added a few more runs in the bottom of the second when Weston helped his own cause with an RBI groundout, followed by Argotsinger reaching safely at first base due to the fielder coming off the bag, allowing Jozef Reisz to score making it 3-0.
'We're trying to stay on top of the ball and not do too much,' Schneider said.
The Mustang offense was able to get themselves right back in the game in the top of the third. A groundball was hit to Heese at first base who stepped on the bag for the out. He then threw over to Kaufman at third, but the ball sailed out of reach scoring Senior Jade Spangler, who cut the Cyclone lead to 3-2.
However, the Cyclones were able to answer back in the bottom of the third when Soma hit an RBI groundout to score Koesters, which was followed by an RBI groundout by Kaufman to score Heese to make it 5-2.
Nobody scored again until the top of the fifth when another overthrow occurred at third base by the Cyclones allowing Spangler to score making it 5-3.
The Mustangs were able to get one more run in the top of the sixth on a mis-played groundball by Kaufman. Junior Dalton Athen was later hit by a pitch with the bases loaded, forcing home a run. However, Schneider once again was brilliant out of the bullpen, pitching the final two innings of the game, including a 1-2-3 top of the seventh inning, which featured a swinging strikeout of Lorimor to end the game, giving the Cyclones two wins on the night.
'We knew it was going to be a long night,' Stein said. 'Colton did a really nice job closing out both of those games.'
With these wins, the Cyclones move to 21-6 on the season. They return to action at 7:30 p.m. against the 17-3 Clarinda Cardinals, whom they beat at home June 14 by a score of 7-5. Offensively, the Cardinals are led by Cole Baumgart with 29 hits and Creighton Tuzzio with a .439 batting average and 34 runs batted in. In pitching, Tuzzio has seven wins, 72 strikeouts, and a 1.01 earned run average.
'Keeping the sticks hot, and keeping our defense hot,' Schneider said. 'Our pitching has been phenomenal these past few games, and we've got to keep that up.'

title: Schmitz one of 75 selected to top gun showcase
author: Alex Martin
description: Max Schmitz, an incoming freshman at Ankeny Centennial High School recently went to Naples, FL for a football camp called the ESPN 300 top gun showcase where he was just one of 75 people across the country to represent. Schmitz is the son of David Schmitz and grandson of Janice Schmitz of Harlan, and the late Cletus Schmitz. Despite his mother not longer with him, Schmitz has others in his life that have supported him and helped him along the way, including his dad.
content:
Max Schmitz, an incoming freshman at Ankeny Centennial High School recently went to Naples, FL for a football camp called the ESPN 300 top gun showcase where he was just one of 75 people across the country to represent.
'It definitely means a lot,' Schmitz said. 'I've put a lot of work in, and it's definitely starting to pay off.'
Schmitz is the son of David Schmitz and grandson of Janice Schmitz of Harlan, and the late Cletus Schmitz.
While Schmitz is going to Naples for sports related reasons, this will not be his first time in Florida. The last time he was there, his mother's ashes were spread. She had died a year earlier due to ovarian cancer.
Despite his mother not longer with him, Schmitz has others in his life that have supported him and helped him along the way, including his dad.
'My dad is a huge supporter,' he said. 'He's definitely helped me and pushed me every day with all I do in football, and having my friends down there going with me, it's definitely going to be fun.'
The love for football started for Schmitz at a young age, including cheering on a college football team.
'I probably started playing flag football when I was about 4-5 years old, but when I was in second grade, I started playing tackle football,' Schmitz said. 'What really drew me to football was being an Oregon Ducks fan as a little kid and watching them was what made me want to play football.'
Schmitz also talked about an athlete on the Ducks who he admires and looks up to.
'His name is Bucky Irving,' he said. 'He plays for Oregon. He's really elusive, he's short, he's quick kind of like me, and I put my game towards him.'
Still being so young, Schmitz has already learned life lessons that have helped him be successful in the game of football.
'Just keep going,' he added. 'I went through a lot with football, especially the last couple of years, and it's taught me to keep going. You can't ever quit. It's just my mentality.'
With his high school journey starting in just a few months, Schmitz will not only play football, but play other sports as well.
'I'm going to play basketball and run track,' Schmitz said.

title: Cyclones bats go quiet in road loss
author: Alex Martin
description: In the bottom of the second inning with the bases loaded, a comebacker was hit to HCHS Senior Cyclone pitcher Braydon Ernst who turned and threw to shortstop Colton Schneider who was unable to field the ball cleanly causing Senior Clarinda Cardinals Caden Butt and Ayden Sunderman to score, which would be all the Cardinals would need winning 2-0, and handing the Cyclones their eighth loss. The Cyclones did not get their first hit until the top of the fourth inning and it came off the bat of Senior Matthew Sorfonden. Stein removed him after the fourth inning, replacing him with Koesters, who pitched two scoreless innings to keep his team within striking distance of the Cardinals.
content:
In the bottom of the second inning with the bases loaded, a comebacker was hit to HCHS Senior Cyclone pitcher Braydon Ernst who turned and threw to shortstop Colton Schneider who was unable to field the ball cleanly causing Senior Clarinda Cardinals Caden Butt and Ayden Sunderman to score, which would be all the Cardinals would need winning 2-0, and handing the Cyclones their eighth loss.
'That one mental lapse,' said Cyclone Head Coach Heath Stein. 'I guess we assumed that with corners in and bases loaded, pitchers know that they're going to the plate, but we need to do a better job of pre-pitch communication on that one.'
Senior Cardinal Creighton Tuzzio got the ball for Clarinda and dominated the Cyclones batting order. The Cyclones did not get their first hit until the top of the fourth inning and it came off the bat of Senior Matthew Sorfonden. Following Sorfonden's hit, Senior Quinn Koesters was able to draw a walk to put a little bit of pressure on Tuzzio. However, Tuzzio was able to work his way out of the inning with back-to-back strikeouts of Juniors Brett Heese and Hayden Soma to get out of the inning.
Ernst pitched four innings giving up just those two runs. Stein removed him after the fourth inning, replacing him with Koesters, who pitched two scoreless innings to keep his team within striking distance of the Cardinals.
'He's executing pitches,' Stein said of Koesters. 'He did a good job. He hadn't had some work in a while, so that was our plan was to get him a little bit of work after Braydon.'
When Tuzzio returned to the mound in the top of the seventh inning, he got through the first two outs quickly, then surrendered a base hit to Soma, but was able to record the final out of the game going the distance and handing the Cyclones the loss.
'That's the best arm we've seen,' Stein said of Tuzzio. 'We haven't seen high 80s pretty much all year. It took a while for us to adjust. Some guys made adjustments, and it's good to see just in case we run into that down the road. Hopefully we learn from it and find ways to compete better in the box.'
The Cyclones return home Monday night at 7:30 p.m. against the 4-32 Council Bluffs Jefferson Yellow Jackets. Offensively, the Yellow Jackets are led by Garrett Denman with 32 hits and Jordan Steinspring with 15 runs batted in. On the mound, Peyton Steinspring has one win, while Kendall Bell leads his team in earned run average with 3.50, and Aiden Moore leads in strikeouts with 28.
'We just need to continue to work on some things,' Stein said. 'Fine tune some things, and get things as cleaned up as possible before Friday.'

title: Area athletes excited for senior season
author: Alex Martin
description: Whether it's AHSTW's Claire Mertz, Exira-EHK's Harlee Fahn, HCHS's Aubrey Schwieso, or IKM-Manning's Raegan Garrison, each student athlete is excited and looking forward to their senior season. Despite graduating eight seniors from the 2023-2024 school year, Mertz is optimistic about what the team could be capable of this season. Mertz also plays soccer during spring, when this past season she scored the game tying goal in the Class 1A – Region 6 First Round Tournament Game from over 20 feet away only minutes before it looked like their season was all but over.
content:
Whether it's AHSTW's Claire Mertz, Exira-EHK's Harlee Fahn, HCHS's Aubrey Schwieso, or IKM-Manning's Raegan Garrison, each student athlete is excited and looking forward to their senior season.
Mertz will open her season with volleyball. Last season, Mertz had eight assists, two kills, 146 digs, and a serve efficiency rate of 77.1%. Despite graduating eight seniors from the 2023-2024 school year, Mertz is optimistic about what the team could be capable of this season.
'Volleyball will miss the talents of the graduating seniors, but I hope we can rise to the challenges and continue to support each other through the change in positions,' she said. 'As one of the seniors, I hope that our group will lead and take a positive approach to each game.'
Mertz also plays soccer during spring, when this past season she scored the game tying goal in the Class 1A – Region 6 First Round Tournament Game from over 20 feet away only minutes before it looked like their season was all but over.
Fahn plans to be ready for basketball in the winter. She helped her team reach the Regional Championship game the previous two seasons.
Last season, she scored 151 points, with 163 rebounds, 14 assists, 32 steals, and two blocks in 23 games played, 10 of which she started.
'It's been fun the past three years,' Fahn said. 'With working throughout this past summer, we've been working a lot and hoping to get over that hump at the Regional Final.'
Fahn remains close with her coaches, including Tom Petersen, who has coached her in basketball, and has known him for quite some time.
'I've known Coach Petersen my whole life,' she said. 'He coached my older brothers. He's a good coach. He's a role model to me.'
Schwieso will start with volleyball in the fall, then move to basketball in the winter, and conclude her senior season with soccer and track and field.
During this past volleyball season Schwieso led the Cyclones with 139 kills. She had the second most points in basketball with 325, just two behind Erica Rust with 327, and led the Cyclones in assists with 102 during their state tournament run season. In soccer, she led the team in goals with 18, and had the fastest time in the 200m dash with 27.62.
Schwieso is coached by Elle Crees, Zach Klaassen, Jared Boysen, and Jenny Hamilton, and credits them for the help they've given her.
'I credit them for helping me grow as a person, not only in sports, but outside of it,' she added.
With so many impressive statistics, Schwieso hopes that her numbers aren't what people remember her for, but other characteristics she had while competing for the Cyclones.
'I don't want it to be about my numbers,' Schwieso said. 'I just want to leave a good impact and good sportsmanship, being a really good teammate, and helping out the younger kids and always being good role models for the little ones.'
Garrison is known for running, as she dominated cross country and track and field this past season. She is known for the longer distance events, including leading her team in the 1500 and 3000m events with times of 5:25.11 and 11:34.38.
'I'm hoping to make it to state and more,' Garrison said. 'Last year I was very disappointed with my 2-mile because I ran terrible at districts, but I'm hoping to continue to workout a lot, get better, and go to state in more than one event.'

title: Cyclones head back to state tournament with dominant victory
author: Alex Martin
description: In the top of the fifth inning of Wednesday's 3A-8 Regional Championship Game leading 10-0, Lewis Central Senior Luke Woltmann hammered a flyball to center field, but Senior Cyclone Matthew Sorfonden was there to make the catch securing the final out, followed by his team rushing the field to jump on the back of Senior Braydon Ernst, as the team punched their ticket to the state tournament for the second consecutive season. Ernst opened the game walking Senior Titan Gaven Goldsberry, but following that walk he recorded back-to-back strikeouts of Woltmann and Junior Brady Hetzel, getting out of the first inning with just 18 pitches thrown. Junior Gavin Harrington reached base via a 2-out single, but Ernst got out of the inning once again when Schneider caught the final out on a line drive off the bat of Freshman Liam Anderson.
content:
In the top of the fifth inning of Wednesday's 3A-8 Regional Championship Game leading 10-0, Lewis Central Senior Luke Woltmann hammered a flyball to center field, but Senior Cyclone Matthew Sorfonden was there to make the catch securing the final out, followed by his team rushing the field to jump on the back of Senior Braydon Ernst, as the team punched their ticket to the state tournament for the second consecutive season.
'That was awesome,' Sorfonden said. 'When it came to me, I was like 'this is perfect. This is exactly what I wanted, and it's exactly what I got to do.''
Ernst opened the game walking Senior Titan Gaven Goldsberry, but following that walk he recorded back-to-back strikeouts of Woltmann and Junior Brady Hetzel, getting out of the first inning with just 18 pitches thrown.
In the bottom of the first, the Cyclones got their first hit courtesy of a double from Freshman Colton Schneider, but left him stranded on second base keeping the game scoreless after one inning.
Ernst continued to work through the Titan lineup starting with a line drive to Senior Quinn Koesters at second base, followed by a strikeout of Sophomore Brody Applegate for the second out. Junior Gavin Harrington reached base via a 2-out single, but Ernst got out of the inning once again when Schneider caught the final out on a line drive off the bat of Freshman Liam Anderson.
'Ernst is having a heck of a career,' said Cyclone Head Coach Heath Stein. 'For him to get in this big game like this and perform how we did was just fantastic. He was a little erratic to start the game with that first batter, but he settled in so dang nice and just executed pitches and never wavered and never gave them any hope at all.'
In the bottom of the second, the Cyclones got their first run of the game when the bottom of the batting order got going with Junior Weston Reisz stepping to the plate and connecting for an RBI single scoring Jozef Reisz, followed by eighth-grader Foxx Argotsinger hitting an RBI single to score Landen Kaufman, which was later capped off by a sacrifice fly from Koesters to score Weston Reisz giving the Cyclones a 3-0 lead after two innings.
'I was having some really tough quality at bats,' Weston Reisz said. 'Today, I kind of switched things up and my mom did some stuff with me that I used to do when I was younger, and it helped me tremendously.'
The Titans bats continued to stay quiet in the top of the third starting with a strikeout of Junior Landon Kammrad to open the inning. Ernst got the next two outs exiting the inning with 51 pitches.
In the bottom of the third, with one out, Junior Cyclone Hayden Soma launched a solo home run that went over the left field fence to the right of the scoreboard putting his team up 4-0 and getting his teammates pumped up as they exited the dugout to greet him when he crossed home plate.
'It was just an energy boost for the fellas,' Soma said. 'The bats were rolling all night, especially the bottom of the order. I think we had seven hits. When you can get the whole lineup rolling, it's hard for the defense to make stops and plays to get us out.'
Following Soma's home run, Weston Reisz knocked in his second run of the night expanding the lead to 5-0, which forced Junior Titan pitcher Aaron Kreps to exit the game, replacing him with Applegate.
However, the Cyclones weren't fazed by a new arm on the mound as they continued to pile runs on the Titan defense with Sorfonden drawing a bases loaded walk, followed by Koesters getting hit by a pitch, and then a balk from Applegate scoring Argotsinger to make it 8-0, chasing him from the game as he was unable to record an out.
Hetzel came in and managed to strike out Colton Schneider, but the third strike was dropped which allowed Sorfonden to score. Junior Brett Heese got in on the action adding an RBI single to score Koesters, putting his team up 10-0.
'Top to bottom, our lineup was outstanding tonight,' Stein said. 'Our bottom of the order guys were absolutely nails and when they get on, we're so tough. Their approaches were fantastic and the swings they got off were great. I can't say enough about these guys.'
When Ernst returned to the mound in the top of the fifth, he only needed to throw 13 pitches, getting the final three outs, sending his team back to the state tournament for the second consecutive year.
'I just knew if I threw strikes they'd hit the ball, and I let my defense do some work,' Ernst said. 'Some of them got by more hitters than I thought, and it worked good.'
The Cyclones will play Monday at 11:30 a.m. in Cedar Rapids in the 3A – Quarterfinal Game against the 26-6 North Polk Comets. Offensively, the Comets are led by Drew Owen with 41 hits, batting .373, and Isaac Zoske with 25 runs batted in. On the mound, Reece Wrage has 10 wins, with a 1.05 earned run average and 85 strikeouts in 66.2 innings pitched.
'It's going to be good to go out with these boys no matter what happens,' Sorfonden said. 'Our goal is just to make a good run.'

title: Cyclones eliminated by Comets at state
author: Alex Martin
description: Sometimes a game can come down to just one pitch to define your season, and that certainly proved to be case for the HCHS baseball team Monday in Cedar Rapids in the Class 3A – Quarterfinal Game when North Polk Comet Sophomore Chase Fjelland launched a 2-out, 2-run walk-off single off Freshman Cyclone Colton Schneider over the head of Junior Cyclone Jozef Reisz winning the game 5-4 ending the Cyclones season. Cyclone Senior Braydon Ernst took the mound in the bottom half of the inning allowing a leadoff single from Junior Comet Drew Owen, but his time on base was short-lived with Cyclone Junior Hayden Soma throwing him out just a few pitches later for the first out. Junior Cyclone Brett Heese connected for a base hit to open the top of the second for the Cyclones, but Wrage shut them down once again on offense striking out the rest of the batters.
content:
Sometimes a game can come down to just one pitch to define your season, and that certainly proved to be case for the HCHS baseball team Monday in Cedar Rapids in the Class 3A – Quarterfinal Game when North Polk Comet Sophomore Chase Fjelland launched a 2-out, 2-run walk-off single off Freshman Cyclone Colton Schneider over the head of Junior Cyclone Jozef Reisz winning the game 5-4 ending the Cyclones season.
'Way to compete and stay gritty,' said Junior Cyclone Weston Reisz. 'We had a hell of a season and it came down to the wire there, but we didn't go down without a fight.'
The game opened with Senior Comet Reece Wrage striking out the side in the top of the first. Cyclone Senior Braydon Ernst took the mound in the bottom half of the inning allowing a leadoff single from Junior Comet Drew Owen, but his time on base was short-lived with Cyclone Junior Hayden Soma throwing him out just a few pitches later for the first out. Ernst continued to battle and got out of the inning with a strikeout of Senior Comet Hunter Cook.
Junior Cyclone Brett Heese connected for a base hit to open the top of the second for the Cyclones, but Wrage shut them down once again on offense striking out the rest of the batters. Ernst returned to the mound and had to battle through the Comets offense, but was able to get the final out of the inning on a groundball to Schneider at shortstop, who flipped to second baseman Quinn Koesters for the final out of the inning.
'Ernst pitched out of some jams and did a great job with that,' said Cyclone Head Coach Heath Stein. 'We battled and got in tough spots, but the kids persevered in those spots.'
The next few innings were quiet until the bottom of the fifth. Senior Comet Brayden Foster opened the inning with a leadoff single. Ernst then made a fielding error attempting to throw Foster out going to third base, but the throw went past third base allowing him to score giving the Comets a 1-0 lead. Stein removed Ernst for Brock Lemrick.
The Comets weren't fazed by the pitching change as Wrage helped his own cause connecting for an RBI single to score Owen making it 2-0, followed by an RBI single from Cook scoring Sophomore Bryce Burke, who came in to courtesy run for Wrage giving his team a 3-0 lead after five.
Reisz got his team back in the game in the top of the sixth inning when he smashed a 2-run double down the right field line bringing his team back within one run at 3-2, chasing Wrage from the game.
'I was really stoked,' Reisz said. 'We struggled at the beginning of the game, but once we started finding barrels, things started falling in place. It just didn't hold up.'
When Lemrick returned to the mound in the bottom of the sixth, he got through the Comets offense with a 1-2-3 inning, keeping his team down by one entering the top of the seventh.
When the top of the seventh began, Matthew Sorfonden was hit by a pitch, followed by Koesters getting hit by a pitch. Comets head coach Wyatt Zoske then made a pitching change that worked when Schneider struck out for the first out, but then Heese walked to load the bases with just one out. Hayden Soma popped out to the first baseman for the second out, and it looked like the Cyclones season was over until Jozef Reisz hammered a pitch that went past the third baseman down the left field line scoring two runs, putting the Cyclones up 4-3, making their fan base erupt with applause and cheers.
'That was huge,' Weston said of Jozef. 'Joining us halfway through the season off of surgery. He's done a heck of a job and it's awesome to see.'
When the Cyclones returned to defense in the bottom of the seventh, Lemrick was on the mound, but got removed for Schneider after getting just one out. Schneider got into a jam when Wrage came up and hit a single to load the bases with one out, but following Wrage's single, Jozef Reisz made a season saving catch in left field for the second out of the inning. However, following his catch, Fjelland ended the game with a walk-off single.
'Our guys showed their toughness, showed their fight,' Stein said. 'We could have rolled over. We were down 3-0, and we found a way to scrap into it, take the lead and we were one out, one pitch away, and I couldn't be prouder of the guys.'
The Cyclones wrap up their 2024 campaign finishing with an overall record of 27-9. Offensively, they were led by Koesters with 38 hits and Soma with 31 runs batted in. On the mound, Ernst had eight wins, with 52 strikeouts in 65.1 innings pitched with a 1.71 earned run average.
Sorfonden, Koesters, Ernst, Lemrick, Caleb Schleis, Keegan King, Gavin Bruck, Franz Reisz, and Cade Sears won't return due to graduating. However, despite losing nine talented seniors, the future of Cyclone baseball looks bright.
'I'm really looking forward to it,' Reisz said. 'We have some good young guys coming up, and hopefully seeing this can feed into them and get them ready for next season.'

title: Guest speaker presents powerful data on digital media
description: HCSD and Myrtue Medical Center partnered up to bring Douglas Gentile, Ph.D., a psychology professor and researcher from ISU who brought in a collection of data from his and other studies, to speak to the schools and community on Wednesday, August 28. Gentile's message highlighted how powerful digital media is in the development of children and culture as a whole, while also emphasizing the importance of parental action in mitigating problems and using digital media positively. Screen use creates a vicious cycle: screen time is used to cope with problems, but it only exacerbates them—loneliness drives more 'social' media use, and children are handed screens to 'keep' their attention, leading to further issues.
content:
99% of American households have TV sets. The average household in America has 25 internet connected devices in it. When we look at children's bedrooms, 40% of preschoolers have TVs in their bedrooms.' - Douglas Gentile, Ph.D.
The world is at a turning point, where screens, much like addictive substances throughout history, have rapidly spread across society until their negative consequences came to light. The effects of digital media are starting to become more understood by data and research. HCSD and Myrtue Medical Center partnered up to bring Douglas Gentile, Ph.D., a psychology professor and researcher from ISU who brought in a collection of data from his and other studies, to speak to the schools and community on Wednesday, August 28. Gentile's message highlighted how powerful digital media is in the development of children and culture as a whole, while also emphasizing the importance of parental action in mitigating problems and using digital media positively.
Confronting the data and hard evidence reveals that, even if not outright addictive, excessive screen use still leads to lower grades, increased aggression, impulsiveness, and worsened mental health conditions like depression, anxiety, ADHD, and overall unhappiness. While most research over the past 20 years has focused on gaming, emerging studies on general screen time show similar negative effects. Screen use creates a vicious cycle: screen time is used to cope with problems, but it only exacerbates them—loneliness drives more 'social' media use, and children are handed screens to 'keep' their attention, leading to further issues.
'When does it become a disorder? It's not about how much you do it, it's about- Is it disrupting other areas of your life? That's true for any addiction. When does it start damaging family life? When does it start damaging kids' social life because they stop being interested in clubs, sports, or music, or other things they used to be interested in? Addictions are defined by being dysfunctional,' Gentile stated.
Where recently the World Health Organization declared Gaming Disorder as a mental health disorder, Gentile shared the U.S. is lagging in having a diagnosis, treatment, and help. Being on a committee advising those revising the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM), he hopes the DSM 6 will address screen addictions in the next few years.
In a study of 3,000 kids across 3 years, Gentile and his colleagues measured addiction symptoms. Though the study suggested gaming is leading mental health problems, Gentile emphasized, ' Mental health disorders beget other mental health disorders. It's called comorbidity. The question of which started the process is not what's most important. Therapists have to treat the whole package.'
Gentile showed a study of a classroom of children ages 3-5 years-old who watched a Barney show and then a Power Ranger show the next day. He demonstrated that just 20 minutes can have a powerful influence and change the whole environment of a classroom. His research and studies, however, looked at exposures over time and across a range of ages. His studies on aggression, attention, grades, and mental health have implications on the development of the brain in how it becomes wired to respond in certain ways. When a child is subdued by a screen, their brains are being wired to rely on that constant stimulation. When a person grows up playing video games, their brain gets constant rewards for reacting in quick, impulsive ways.
While studies are complex, involving many factors and comorbid disorders, one thing is clear- there simply isn't enough time in a week. Surveys reveal that the average American school-age child spends just 2.5 hours per week interacting with their mother and a staggering 0.5 hours weekly with non-school reading. In contrast, they spent an overwhelming amount of time on screens for entertainment purposes, taking away from the quality time of social interactions and developmental activities like reading.
'I have no doubt parents matter,' Gentille addressed the audience. 'You're not getting equal time. You're not getting anything close to equal time. You add it up; it is an average of 54 hours a week the average American school-age child is in front of the screen not for school purposes. That's a full-time job with 14 hours of overtime.'
Gentile suggests a collective effort and partnership to combat this huge issue we face. It takes a shift in what we have become comfortable with and normalized as a culture over the years.
'Here's the good news. This is my favorite study I ever did. We studied 1,300 3rd-5th graders in Iowa and Minnesota. We measured them multiple times through the school year, looking at parents who do have rules, and their kids are consuming lower amounts of screen time. We followed them out to the end of the school year. Those kids with more limits are getting better sleep, which lowers their BMI and risk for obesity. They are getting better grades in school. They show more prosocial behaviors as rated by the teachers. The teachers don't know the rules at home for media, but they can see the behaviors. They are less aggressive as rated by the teacher,' Gentile shared.
Gentile offered three tips that have been shown to make huge impacts against the negative effects of screens:
Restrictions on time
Restrictions on the content
Co-viewing with critical discussion
The fourth suggestion is one of the most powerful things parents can do. Parents can watch with their kids and have discussions to ask questions about the media's points of view, the good, the bad, the wrong, and the right.
'When you sit and watch with your kids and you talk to them about what they are seeing and hearing, it mitigates almost all of the negative effects and enhances the positive effects,' Gentile emphasized twice. 'Here's the caveat. If you sit and watch with them and you don't discuss it, it enhances the negative effects.'
There needs to be partnerships and a community standard to protect children from addiction and growing up with a normalized presence of constant screens. Parents can work with the school and other parents to normalize having no phones at school. Schools have tried many measures, like phones left at the door before entering classrooms. Expectations held by teachers and parents need to extend into partnerships, teams, and the community.
Before answering questions, Gentile made a last point, 'You will never know you are having an effect. You'll never know if your child gained less weight than they would have or have better grades than they would have had. You only see what your child is. You don't know what your child would have been if you relaxed the rules. What do you see? You see the fight over the rules, and this is why parents feel powerless. They see the fighting, but they cannot see the beneficial effect of those rules. You are in a much more powerful position than you realize.'

title: Southwest Iowa Art Tour has Harlan stop featuring Seven Artists
author: Tami Schechinger
description: This year, Market Street Gifts, located at 608 Market St. on the north side of the square in downtown Harlan, is one of the 20 stops in Southwest Iowa to see work from local artists in painting, sculpture, fabric art, photography, pottery, wood carving, jewelry and mixed media.
