author: Alex Martin
description: After trailing 3-0 a majority of the Thursday's road game against the Kuemper Catholic Knights, the HCHS Cyclones baseball team found the scoreboard late in the game coming away with a 6-spot, which would be enough to win the game 6-3. Senior Cyclone Brock Lemrick got the ball to start the night going 6.2 innings with seven strikeouts, allowing three runs on six hits with three walks and 111 pitches thrown, but was able to come away with the win. 'He was on really early, but his pitch count climbed up there due to a couple plays not being made behind him, so that made him throw more pitches early, and he was at about 60 pitches threw three innings.
content:
After trailing 3-0 a majority of the Thursday's road game against the Kuemper Catholic Knights, the HCHS Cyclones baseball team found the scoreboard late in the game coming away with a 6-spot, which would be enough to win the game 6-3.
'We put together a bunch of good at bats and took what they gave us,' said Cyclone Head Coach Heath Stein. 'They ended up giving us quite a few runs and ultimately the ballgame.'
Senior Cyclone Brock Lemrick got the ball to start the night going 6.2 innings with seven strikeouts, allowing three runs on six hits with three walks and 111 pitches thrown, but was able to come away with the win.
'Brock threw the ball really well,' Stein said. 'He was on really early, but his pitch count climbed up there due to a couple plays not being made behind him, so that made him throw more pitches early, and he was at about 60 pitches threw three innings. Him being able to stay in the game as long as he did, he got really tough and very efficient in those middle innings, so that allowed him to get one out away from finishing that ballgame, so great job by Brock.'
Junior Knight Mason Knerl provided the biggest spark for the Kuemper Catholic offense with two hits, including driving in one run for his team that helped them jump out to an early 3-0 lead.
Ethan Loew got the ball for the Knights, pitching 6.1 innings, taking a shutout into the top of the seventh, but the Cyclone offense came alive.
'They gave us a few,' Stein said. 'They walked us a couple of times and a couple of hit batters. Loew was giving up fits all night. We weren't squaring as many balls up, and then he kind of hit a wall and walked a couple. Weston Reisz had a great at bat and hit a single through the right side. Next thing you know Landen [Kaufman] gets hit, [Matthew] Sorfonden gets hit.'
Cyclones close out week with win over Cardinals at home
In the bottom of the fifth inning of Friday's home game against the Clarinda Cardinals, the HCHS Cyclones baseball team trailed 4-1 with Junior Cyclone Landen Kaufman opening the inning and got on base via an error by the Cardinal defense, which was followed by a double by Matthew Sorfonden to put him and Kaufman in scoring position. Brett Heese stepped to the plate to knock both of them in and a few batters following Heese, Hayden Soma put his team back in front for the first time since the opening inning.
Braydon Ernst got the ball to start the night on the mound for the Cyclones pitching five innings, striking out four batters, while giving up four runs on four hits, walking seven batters, but he got through five innings of work.
'Braydon was sharp early,' said Cyclone Head Coach Heath Stein. 'He had a little lapse where he walked the 8-hole, and got a little erratic in his pitch count which climbed up to 92. That's usually not his M.O., usually he fills it up and attacks, but for some reason tonight, he had a couple of lapses that got him into trouble, but he fought through it and got through five, and it was a good spot when we put up those runs.'
The Cyclones struck first in the bottom of the first inning when Freshman Colton Schneider connected at the plate for an RBI single giving his team a 1-0 lead after Brett Heese and Quinn Koesters reached back with back-to-back singles.
'He's in a good spot,' Stein said of Schneider. 'He's getting good pitches to hit and putting good swings on him. He's done that all year and it's starting to click, starting to find holes, and we just need a couple of more guys to get on base in front of him, and when he's on base, drive them in.'
The game went quiet for the next few innings until the Cardinals tied the game at one run apiece in the top of the fourth inning on a sacrifice fly by Kort Neal. The Cyclones opened the bottom half of that inning with a leadoff single from Schneider, but were unable to answer back in that inning.
The Cardinals offense took the lead, their first of the game in the top of the fifth inning when Karsten Beckel drew a walk with the bases loaded, followed by a 2-run single from Andrew Jones to score Kaiden Roop and Cole Baumgart to put his team up 4-1.
The Cyclone offense answered back right away with a 4-spot retaking the lead at 5-4. Multiple Cyclones contributed to the offense, including Schneider who got a hit, his third of the night to load the bases, which set the stage for Soma who gave his team the lead back with a 2-run single.
'It was actually really easy to see,' Schneider said. 'The first pitcher wasn't throwing very hard, and I was trying to stay on top of the ball.'
Schneider took over on the mound in the top of the sixth for Ernst and got a quick inning with an unassisted 6-3 double play that was made by Weston Reisz.
'Huge play out of Weston,' Stein said. 'They had the 7-8-9 coming up in the sixth, and we really wanted to get through that clean. First guy got a hit, and next thing you know we get the double play by Weston, which was huge.'
When the bottom of the sixth inning rolled around, the Cyclones got some insurance runs to extend their lead to 7-4 when Heese put the ball in play, reaching on an error, followed by a fielders choice from the Cardinal defense during an at bat by Kaufman, giving them a 7-4 lead entering the final inning.
Schneider returned to the mound in the top of the seventh and allowed an RBI single from Creighton Tuzzio to score Caden Butt, which would be followed by him loading the bases, but after a mound visit from Stein, Schneider struck out Sam Kline looking to end the game, giving the Cyclones their third win in a row and 15 th on the season.
'I was pumped,' Schneider said. 'I worked from an 0-2 count, and then a full count, and wasn't too good of a start, but I finished it.'
The Cyclones return to action Monday on the road for a doubleheader starting at 5:30 against the 4-15 Red Oak Tigers. Offensively, the Tigers are led by Brett Erickson with 17 hits and Brody Bond with 12 runs batted in. In pitching, Reese Montgomery has two wins, while Erickson leads the team in strikeouts with 36.
'We just need to keep hitting,' Schneider added. 'We had over 10 hits this game. We need good pitching just like Ernst tonight, and I think we'll do good.'

title: Schaben-Lansman reflects on first professional season
author: Alex Martin
description: Former HCHS Cyclone and ISU Cyclone Jess Schaben-Lansman recently wrapped up her first professional season of volleyball with the Omaha Supernovas, which resulted in the first ever championship in the Professional Volleyball Federation. During the season, the Supernovas finished with a record of 18-8 with some of their wins coming against the San Diego Mojo, Grand Rapids Rise, Vegas Thrill, Orlando Valkyries, and Atlanta Vibe. Schaben-Lansman's first match was at the CHI Health Center in Omaha where she and her team faced off against Atlanta, dropping the match 3-2.
content:
Former HCHS Cyclone and ISU Cyclone Jess Schaben-Lansman recently wrapped up her first professional season of volleyball with the Omaha Supernovas, which resulted in the first ever championship in the Professional Volleyball Federation.
'It was definitely a season I'll never forget,' Schaben-Lansman said. 'It was full of so many new experiences. Competing at the highest level was such an amazing experience. It was quite a whirlwind of a year from finding out about the season last May, to now wrapping it up as PVF championships. Overall, an amazing experience.'
During the season, the Supernovas finished with a record of 18-8 with some of their wins coming against the San Diego Mojo, Grand Rapids Rise, Vegas Thrill, Orlando Valkyries, and Atlanta Vibe. She played 18 matches and in 59 sets played, scored 190 points, and had 36 blocks.
Schaben-Lansman's first match was at the CHI Health Center in Omaha where she and her team faced off against Atlanta, dropping the match 3-2. Even though the match resulted in a loss, she talked about how electric the atmosphere was with a record setting 11,624 fans in attendance.
'The first game of the year against Atlanta was a really special game with a record breaking crowd and all the hype that surrounded professional volleyball in the United States,' she said. 'For it to be hosted in Omaha, and to have that crowd who had never seen us play before, but they all came and wore Supernovas gear. It was very special for women and volleyball.'
During the season, Schaben-Lansman talked about the challenge of traveling to other cities, while having a family whom she was away from for days at a time, including her son.
'My husband [Will] was an absolute trooper through all of this,' she added. 'He really took on a huge role. When I was gone, he was the only parent here. He took care of our son and he was working also. It was a really busy time for him, but he was so supportive through it all and he was my biggest fan. It's all because of him that I was able to do this.'
Even with her first professional season behind her and while it's hard to top a championship, Schaben-Lansman is looking forward the future of Supernova volleyball.
'I think the future of the Supernovas is super bright,' she said. 'I think that it's only going to keep building and the hype around women's volleyball is continuing to grow. It was an amazing start, and I think it's only going to go up from here.'

title: Six Vikings bring home softball awards
author: Alex Martin
description: Etta Partlow and Graycen Partlow made 1 st Team, Bella Lamp got 2 nd Team, and Loralei Wahling, Clara Pace, and Kennedy Wyman received honorable mention in the Western Iowa All Conference list. During the season, Graycen Partlow had the most hits on the team with 27, knocking in 12 runs with a .278 batting average. Lamp was the lone player who took home second team honors finishing her season with a .260 batting average with one home run and 10 runs batted in.
content:
Recently, six members of the AHSTW Vikings softball team were recognized for their efforts. Etta Partlow and Graycen Partlow made 1 st Team, Bella Lamp got 2 nd Team, and Loralei Wahling, Clara Pace, and Kennedy Wyman received honorable mention in the Western Iowa All Conference list.
'It was great to see that,' Graycen Partlow said. 'It was a great showing of the hard work I've put in, and all five years that I've played, and a great way to end it, a great way to wrap it up with my sister on there too.'
During the season, Graycen Partlow had the most hits on the team with 27, knocking in 12 runs with a .278 batting average. Etta Partlow was known for pitching leading her team in the circle with 116 strikeouts, a 1.85 earned run average in 102 innings pitched.
Lamp was the lone player who took home second team honors finishing her season with a .260 batting average with one home run and 10 runs batted in. She had 25 hits, eight of which were doubles and two triples. She also scored 24 runs and stole 11 bases.
'We definitely were competing a lot throughout practice, and we were struggling and we knew that was because we couldn't put the bat on the ball,' Lamp said. 'I feel like we all just worked really hard with coach [Katie] Pace and coach [Brock] Partlow.'
Wahling, Pace, and Wyman were all acknowledged for their efforts in honorable mention. Wahling batted .302 with 12 runs batted in and 26 hits, Pace led the team in runs batted in with 15, while collecting 27 hits and batting .333, and Wyman batted .369 with 10 runs batted in and 24 hits.
The Vikings finished their season as a team with a 16-9 record, including an 8-game winning streak to close out the regular season before taking a first round exit in Regionals to the Logan-Magnolia Panthers at home 9-1.
'We definitely had a rougher start to our season than what we would've liked,' Lamp added. 'Our team chemistry helped me and our team throughout this entire thing. Our group of girls got really close throughout the entire season. I think our team chemistry is what powered us through those hard times, and made us able to have that 8-game winning streak.'
During the prior offseason, the Vikings made a coaching change replacing Trevor Gipple with Pace as the head coach and adding Sydney Zimmerman as an assistant coach. But despite the changes, the Vikings weren't fazed by it and played strong throughout the course of the season.
'Our coaching staff was really supportive throughout the whole year,' Lamp said. 'If we had a problem, we brought it to them, they understood and talked to us about it. They helped us through those times with losing a coach, but we powered back and did what we had to do.'
Graycen Partlow will not be returning due to graduating, but her softball career will continue onward at Kansas Weslayan. Despite not being with the Vikings anymore, Partlow plans to be close by and sees a bright future with this team.
'I will definitely be back either as a coach or watching them,' she said. 'I'm so excited to see them grow. They are very young and have lots of years ahead of them, and this year was a terrific start to that, and I can't wait to watch them succeed more in the future.'

title: Vikings look to dig deep in new volleyball season
author: Alex Martin
description: After a 2023 campaign in which the AHSTW Vikings volleyball team finished 11-22, including losing their final two matches of the season, they are ready to dig deep and play strong this season. Despite losing Scott, Goshorn, Saydi Paulsen, Ellie Hoffmann, Miranda Akers, Maegan Akers, Lauren Yates, and Lydia Pace due to graduation, Fraher is looking to other girls to step up in those roles. 'It is still early in the season, but we do have some girls who had a little bit of varsity experience last season that we look to fill those roles; Loralei Wahling, Addison Carroll, Sienna Christian and some underclassmen,' she said.
content:
After a 2023 campaign in which the AHSTW Vikings volleyball team finished 11-22, including losing their final two matches of the season, they are ready to dig deep and play strong this season.
'We are extremely excited to get things started this year,' said Vikings Head Coach Kelsey Fraher. 'We have a solid group of hard working girls, and are looking forward to seeing what we can do this season.'
During the 2023 season, the Vikings were led by Kendra Hansen with 188 assists, Delaney Goshorn with 242 kills and 50 blocks, Grayson Gettler with 271 digs, and Lillian Scott with 29 serve aces.
Some of their wins came against Atlantic, Denison, ACGC, Southwest Valley, Coon Rapids-Bayard, Panorama, and others. Despite losing Scott, Goshorn, Saydi Paulsen, Ellie Hoffmann, Miranda Akers, Maegan Akers, Lauren Yates, and Lydia Pace due to graduation, Fraher is looking to other girls to step up in those roles.
'It is still early in the season, but we do have some girls who had a little bit of varsity experience last season that we look to fill those roles; Loralei Wahling, Addison Carroll, Sienna Christian and some underclassmen,' she said.
The Vikings play in a tough Western Iowa Conference against Treynor, Tri-Center, Riverside, Missouri Valley, Underwood, Logan-Magnolia, and IKM-Manning, some of which they had struggles with in prior years.
'The entire WIC is competitive,' Fraher said. 'It doesn't matter who we are facing, we need to be playing our best volleyball. Some teams we hope to be more competitive against are Riverside, Treynor, and Tri-Center.'
With the season set to begin in a few weeks, Fraher and the rest of the coaching staff have been working with the girls during practice to make sure they are at their best.
'We are really focusing on effort and attitude,' she added. 'Another focus for us is increasing our offensive production. We are working on finding open spots on the court and just being more aggressive offensively in general.'
The Vikings will begin their season with a scrimmage at Atlantic High School Aug. 24 where they will be one of 16 schools in attendance. Not knowing what the team will look like on the court, Fraher is looking forward to seeing how the girls compete.
'Ultimately, we are excited to see what we have,' Fraher said. 'We will be a young and relatively inexperienced team. However, we have some very talented athletes and we can't wait to see how they continue to improve this season.'

title: Wolves host triangular to open season
author: Alex Martin
description: It was a struggle for the IKM-Manning Wolves volleyball team last season with just four wins, but with a new season right around the corner, the team is excited for a new journey. When Regionals began, the lost the Class 1A – Region 1 First Round Tournament Game in five sets to the Glidden-Ralston Wildcats. Last season, Ar-We-Va finished 2-24, losing in three sets in the Class 1A – Region 1 First Round Tournament Game to the River Valley Wolverines.
content:
It was a struggle for the IKM-Manning Wolves volleyball team last season with just four wins, but with a new season right around the corner, the team is excited for a new journey.
'I've been looking forward to this season for a while now,' said Junior Karlee Arp. 'I'm excited to play with the people on our team. I think we're all good friends and we can all work good together. I think we have a lot of potential in these first few games to compete.'
During the 2023 season, the Wolves were led by Ella Richards with 195 assists and 31 serve aces, Megan Williams with 146 kills and 40 blocks, and Grace Carroll with 242 digs.
The Wolves four wins came against Coon Rapids-Bayard, Ar-We-Va, Lawton-Bronson, and Logan-Magnolia. When Regionals began, the lost the Class 1A – Region 1 First Round Tournament Game in five sets to the Glidden-Ralston Wildcats.
The Wolves will open this season with a triangular they will host against Ar-We-Va and Exira-EHK. Last season, Ar-We-Va finished 2-24, losing in three sets in the Class 1A – Region 1 First Round Tournament Game to the River Valley Wolverines. Exira-EHK finished 10-13, making it to the Class 1A – Region 4 Quarterfinal Game losing in four sets to the CAM Cougars.
'We just need to work on consistency and controlling our side of the court,' said Wolves Head Coach McKaylie Croghan. 'We have talked a lot about communication already this year. We have a great group of girls who are out, and they all have great attitudes and are fun to be around.'
Before the season begins, the Wolves will have a chance to see some game action when they scrimmage Aug. 24 at Atlantic High School where they will be one of 16 teams in attendance.
'I think that'll be good for us,' Arp said. 'We went to the Central Camp a couple of weeks ago, and that was the first time playing with each other since open gym, so that was our first time in a real rotation, and I think since we've put together a lot of work in these practices. I'm looking forward to that scrimmage because now we know how the other one likes to play, so that'll be good to prepare us for our real games.
Following its season opener, the Wolves will face tough opponents, including Western Iowa Conference rivals Underwood, Tri-Center, Treynor, and others.
'I think we can compete with anybody in our conference this year,' Arp added. 'We have a lot of potential on our team, and as long as we keep working towards it, we just need to take it one game at a time, and keep pushing ourselves and doing what we know we can do.'

title: Harlan Lions Club will offer free vision screening for children
description: lowa KidSight, a vision screening program of the Lions Clubs of lowa and the University of lowa Stead Family Children's Hospital Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences, will be offering free vision screening for children 6-months of age through kindergarten. The screening wil be held at Harlan Primary Building September 9 and 10, Shelby County Catholic School September 11, Harlan Head Start September 17, and AHSTW Elementary September 18. Starting with the 2015-2016 school year, parents of children entering kindergarten and the third grade were required to provide proof their child has completed an approved vision screening.
content:
HARLAN —As adults, we know how we see and if we don't see things clearly. But do we really know how children see? Can a child tell us that a straight line doesn't have a sharp, straight edge? lowa KidSight, a vision screening program of the Lions Clubs of lowa and the University of lowa Stead Family Children's Hospital Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences, will be offering free vision screening for children 6-months of age through kindergarten. The screening wil be held at Harlan Primary Building September 9 and 10, Shelby County Catholic School September 11, Harlan Head Start September 17, and AHSTW Elementary September 18. Home schooled students are welcome to attend at any location.
Starting with the 2015-2016 school year, parents of children entering kindergarten and the third grade were required to provide proof their child has completed an approved vision screening. This requirement, part of a law passed by the lowa Legislation in 2013 (Senate File 419), is an important step to ensuring al children are seeing properly. Parents will need to supply proof their child has completed a vision screening, similar to providing the school with copies of up-to- date immunization records. An lowa KidSight screening is one approved option to meet the requirements of this law.
lowa KidSight is dedicated to enhancing the early detection and treatment of vision impairments in lowa's young children through screening and public education. Free screenings are offered across the state of lowa. After screenings are complete, the results are interpreted by specialists with the Ul Department of parents or guardians receive a letter of referral as well as a list of local ophthalmologists and optometrists. To ensure there are no obstacles in getting to an eye care professional and to ensure the screening program is referring appropriately, follow-up wil be conducted for any child being referred.
lowa KidSight is a community service project of the Lions Clubs of lowa. For more information about the screening process or the program, please contact a the Harlan Lions Club volunteer.

After a weekend tournament in which the AHSTW Vikings volleyball team took just one of six, they returned to action Monday at home for a triangular which also featured the Nodaway Valley Wolverines and Griswold Tigers.
During their match with Nodaway Valley, the Vikings made quick work of them taking the first two sets by scores of 25-6 and 25-8.
'It felt good to get another win,' said Viking Head Coach Kelsey Fraher. 'I know the girls really needed it, as well. However, despite our record, I have seen a lot of positives things out of our young squad.'
Fraher was proud of the way her defense for preventing more points from the Wolverines, which included a block each from Seniors Loralei Wahling and Sienna Christian.
Sophomore Kendra Hansen also came away with nine assists during their matches against the Wolverines, and currently leads the team with 87 on the season.
'Kendra is one of the hardest workers on the court,' Fraher said. 'She does a great job of getting to the ball and giving our hitters something to work with. I thought our passers did a great job of giving her good passes to work with.'
The path to a potential victory against the Tigers was not so easy, as the Tigers managed to earn two wins against the Vikings (25-18 and 25-19), after coming away with two quick wins against the Wolverines.
During set one against the Tigers, Fraher pulled the team together during a timeout when trailing 18-13.
'I just gave them a reminder to play our game,' she said. 'We got away from the way we want to play with effort and energy, so it was just a quick reminder to play AHSTW volleyball.'
Following Fraher's timeout, the Tigers wrapped up set one going on a 7-5 run. During set two, the Tigers got off to a strong start once again going up 11-7 at one point. The Vikings managed to claw their way back into the game, but still lost for their sixth loss of the season.
'Even though our record doesn't show it, we have really played some competitive ball so far this season,' Fraher said. 'I attribute that to their effort and attitude. The girls have worked hard on staying positive and giving 100% effort at all times.'
The Vikings will have some time off before their next match Sept. 12 at home against the 6-0 Riverside Bulldogs. The Bulldogs are led by Junior Bentley Rone with 51 assists, Senior Elly Henderson with 40 kills, Sophomore Lilli Reed with seven blocks, Senior Ayla Richardson with 30 digs, and Sophomore Sophia Fenner with 11 serve aces.
'Riverside is a great team,' Fraher added. 'They do the little things right, they have great hitters who move the ball around and they are scrappy defensively. We know we have to limit our errors, be aggressive and work to find the holes in their defense. We are looking forward to the challenge.'

title: Shelby-Tennant Alumni Association is searching for yearbook
author: Renée Brich
description: AREA ­— The Shelby-Tennant Alumni Association is asking former students and classmates to help preserve the memory of the school by donating Shelby-Tennant yearbooks. Chuck Martens, member of the Alumni Association said it is uncertain what happened to the school library's yearbooks when the school consolidated with what was AvoHa in 1996 to form the A-H-S-T (now AHSTW) School District. Anyone who attended school at Shelby-Tennant, or the individual Shelby or Tennant schools, is welcome to join the Alumni Association, even those who did not graduate from there.
content:
AREA ­— The Shelby-Tennant Alumni Association is asking former students and classmates to help preserve the memory of the school by donating Shelby-Tennant yearbooks.
Chuck Martens, member of the Alumni Association said it is uncertain what happened to the school library's yearbooks when the school consolidated with what was AvoHa in 1996 to form the A-H-S-T (now AHSTW) School District.
'Schools are a mainstay in a community. We lost our school, so there's nothing to bring people together. We are trying to revive that spirit of community,' Martens said.
The Alumni Association will be have a booth at Carstens Farm Days Saturday, September 7 and Sunday, September 8, where yearbooks may be dropped off. Copies of current and past newsletters will be available to read, and anyone who attended Shelby-Tennant will be able to signup to become a paid member of the Alumni Association. There is no charge to become a member, however, those paying $5 for annual dues will receive a copy of the current newsletter.
Anyone who attended school at Shelby-Tennant, or the individual Shelby or Tennant schools, is welcome to join the Alumni Association, even those who did not graduate from there. Alumni banquets are held annually on the Saturday of Memorial Day weekend.
Shelby City Hall will also accept donated yearbooks. The Shelby County Historical Museum in Harlan has agreed to store and display the donated yearbooks, which Martens said would be a great resource for former Cardinals.
'Many of us feel as if the identity of the school is fading away,' Martens said. 'We don't want that to happen. We are reaching out to the community to help us.
For more information about donating yearbooks, or about the Shelby-Tennant Alumni Association, please email S-T_Alumni@outlook.com

title: Enjoying good food while ‘gallivanting' around Shelby County
description: SHELBY COUNTY — Jay Goodvin, known as 'The Iowa Gallivant', recently made two stops in Shelby County for his popular travel blog. Goodvin stopped at the Norse Horse in Elk Horn, which represented Shelby County in his 'Burgers and Backroads' tour throughout Western Iowa. Jay selects places to visit based on recommendations within his platform and Troy's in Earling was often suggested for both burgers and tenderloin.
content:
SHELBY COUNTY — Jay Goodvin, known as 'The Iowa Gallivant', recently made two stops in Shelby County for his popular travel blog.
Goodvin travels Iowa, promoting tourism and dining throughout the state for his 50,000 followers. When not creating content, he works as a paradeucator for the Iowa City Community School District, allowing him to travel during school breaks.
Goodvin stopped at the Norse Horse in Elk Horn, which represented Shelby County in his 'Burgers and Backroads' tour throughout Western Iowa.
Doug Thompson and the staff impressed Jay and company with the quality burgers and sides and great service.
Saturday, August 31 he visited Troy's Bar & Grill in Earling during his 99 Tenderloins quest. His goal is to help small businesses reach customers they otherwise may not have the opportunity to reach. Jay selects places to visit based on recommendations within his platform and Troy's in Earling was often suggested for both burgers and tenderloin.
The owner suggested Jay try the 'Joe Gross' version of the tenderloin which features pepperjack cheese, grilled onions, and bacon. Jay went with the local favorite and said, 'Wow! This one is a true contender on my best of the 99! Fantastic!' Jay also admired the fries and was told by a local Troy's may be one of the only dining establishments in Shelby County to serve hand cut fries.
Jay has been to Earling before, and he featured the sausage made by Earling Locker in his book 'Rural Iowa Sausage: History & Tradition of Brats on the Backroads.'
Jay said, 'You know, pound for pound, Shelby County has some of the best dining establishments in all of Iowa.'

title: Bottled Water Advisory for the City of Shelby
description: September 9th, the City of Shelby, notified the DNR Atlantic Field Office that it received a complaint about pink drinking water. Due to the continuation of the discolored water, the City of Shelby is under a bottled water advisory until sample results become available.Tap water can be used for bathing and other uses, but bottled water should be used for drinking, tooth washing, food preparation and similar uses. The wells are back online and potassium permanganate is no longer being overfed, but pink water is still observed in the clearwell.
content:
September 9th, the City of Shelby, notified the DNR Atlantic Field Office that it received a complaint about pink drinking water. City staff arrived at the plant to discover that two of the four well pumps did not turn on. Since the flow decreased drastically, potassium permanganate was overfed, causing the water to turn pink. The City immediately began working to remedy the issue.
Due to the continuation of the discolored water, the City of Shelby is under a bottled water advisory until sample results become available.Tap water can be used for bathing and other uses, but bottled water should be used for drinking, tooth washing, food preparation and similar uses.
The wells are back online and potassium permanganate is no longer being overfed, but pink water is still observed in the clearwell. The clearwell will be pumped out and replaced with treated water. According to the City, the system's failure alarm did not go off.
Potassium permanganate is used as an oxidizing agent in drinking water and wastewater treatment to help with iron and manganese removal.
Manganese levels in the city's raw water have ranged between 0.62 mg/L to 1.3 mg/L. After treatment with potassium permanganate, the manganese levels in the city's finished water is 0.2 mg/L. The United States Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA) has developed a health advisory level (HAL) for manganese in drinking water of 0.3 mg/L for infants and 1.0 mg/L for adults, respectively.

title: Wolves struggle at home against Eagles
author: Alex Martin
description: After opening the season with two strong wins, the IKM-Manning Wolves volleyball team was back in action Thursday against the 7-9 Underwood Eagles as they struggled to defeat them losing sets one, two, and four (25-17, 25-17, and 25-20). Set two began with Wolves Freshman Keagan Eischeid spiking the ball for a 1-0 Wolves lead. The final point of the set came when the ball was knocked into the backcourt and Wolves Junior Anna Stangl tried to save the ball and keep it in play, but it deflected out of bounds giving the Eagles another 25-17 win.
content:
After opening the season with two strong wins, the IKM-Manning Wolves volleyball team was back in action Thursday against the 7-9 Underwood Eagles as they struggled to defeat them losing sets one, two, and four (25-17, 25-17, and 25-20).
'I thought they did a good job,' said Wolves Head Coach McKaylie Croghan. 'We started off a little slow, so I think we could've picked that up a little bit. I think it was good for them to see with conference play where we can be this year. Underwood has always been really strong.'
The first point of the night came when Addisyn Bandow knocked the ball out of bounds giving the Eagles a 1-0. The Eagles took command of the set leading a majority of the night, finishing off set one with a 25-17 victory.
Set two began with Wolves Freshman Keagan Eischeid spiking the ball for a 1-0 Wolves lead. However, the Eagles once again took over. The final point of the set came when the ball was knocked into the backcourt and Wolves Junior Anna Stangl tried to save the ball and keep it in play, but it deflected out of bounds giving the Eagles another 25-17 win.
Even with an 0-2 deficit at that point, Croghan stayed positive and gave her team some words of encouragement.
'We made a lineup change, and that helped us throwing out something different,' she said.
In set three, the Wolves got off to a slow start, at one point trailing the Eagles 12-8. Croghan called a timeout, and when play resumed, the Wolves offense came alive taking leads of 19-18 and 23-20. The team showed strong defense at the net, as Junior Grace Carroll had three blocks and Sophomore Ella Langel had two.
'I think they do a good job getting a lot of touches,' Croghan said of the defense. 'We've had a couple of net violations, so we need to work on controlling that part of it. But, overall they did a good job with the defense.'
The Wolves got the first point in set four when Carroll spiked a shot that deflected out of bounds, which lead to a 4-0 start. However, the Eagles turned the tables on the Wolves, and the final point of the game came when Senior Eagle Ruby Patomson spiked the ball giving them their eighth win the season, and handing the Wolves their first loss.
The Wolves return to action Tuesday at home at 7:30 p.m. against the 8-3 Treynor Cardinals, who are coming off three consecutive victories. The Cardinals are led by Zoey Zadalis with 120 assists, Nora Konz with 83 kills and nine serve aces, Channing Reed with seven blocks, and Shaylee Smith with 83 digs. Croghan thinks making adjustments when needed will be key during the Treynor match.
'I think we can rally hard with them,' she said.

title: Martin takes oath as Harlan Postmaster
author: Renée Brich
description: HARLAN — Vanessa Martin, Harlan's new Postmaster, was sworn in Tuesday, September 10. Rich Foust, Manager of Post Office Operations, issued the oath of office to Martin. Foust and Martin worked together in Des Moines, and Martin said it was an honor to have him issue the oath.
content:
HARLAN — Vanessa Martin, Harlan's new Postmaster, was sworn in Tuesday, September 10.
Martin transferred to the Harlan Post Office in January and accepted the Postmaster in April. Rich Foust, Manager of Post Office Operations, issued the oath of office to Martin. Foust and Martin worked together in Des Moines, and Martin said it was an honor to have him issue the oath. 'With our history, it was an honor to receive the certificate from him.'
Martin is a native of Glenwood and has 19 years of service with the U.S. Postal Service. Prior to moving to Harlan, she was a supervisor in Bellevue for three years. 'It's good to be back in Southwest Iowa,' Martin said.
She said she appreciates the diversity her job offers. 'It's never the same two days in a row. I can be doing payroll one day, then customer service or one of the rural routes. It's just a vast variety of things.'
In addition to the Harlan office, Martin oversees the post offices in Defiance, Earling, Panama, Elk Horn, and Kimballton. She said she gives a lot of credit to her 23 staff members.
'They are good. They are local and know the area and the community. It's nice to have that knowledge base. They helped me a lot when I came here.'

title: Multiple runners medal at AHSTW Invitational
author: Alex Martin
description: For the Wolves, two girls medaled, including Raegan Garrison, who finished 10 th with 22:38m and Emily Albertsen, who finished 13 th with 23:05. For the boys, Camden Morris was the top finisher, taking an overall finish of 19:04. However, Ava Paulsen has been setting the tone, finishing first among the Vikings with 23:24 at 16 th overall.
content:
Whether it was Exira-EHK, AHSTW, or IKM-Manning, multiple runners performed strong at the AHSTW Invitational in Avoca Tuesday afternoon. For the Wolves, two girls medaled, including Raegan Garrison, who finished 10 th with 22:38m and Emily Albertsen, who finished 13 th with 23:05.
'I thought Raegan and Emily had solid races tonight,' said Wolves Head Coach Robert Cast.
For the boys, Camden Morris was the top finisher, taking an overall finish of 19:04. Kasche Huehn was the second fastest finishing 25 th overall with 19:44.
For the Vikings, one of their top runners, Bella Lamp, continues to remain sidelined. However, Ava Paulsen has been setting the tone, finishing first among the Vikings with 23:24 at 16 th overall. Her sister, Kenna Paulsen was not far behind her finishing 21 st with 24:06.
'I was very proud of both the Paulsen sisters,' said Viking Head Coach Jackson Renberg. 'Ava had a great start and really did a great job picking off runners throughout the race. She beat some very good runners from the area and was close to some very good runners as well. She has really had a strong start to the season and we look forward to seeing her get better as the season progresses. Kenna did a great job of setting in on a good pace and she looked very good on the hills both going up and down them. I was a little bummed out for her that she didn't get a medal as she has been close this year to breaking through. However, she ran really good and as long as she keeps doing that I think she will break the top 20 soon.'
The other two runners for the Vikings were Emery Brockhoff and Yana Lander taking 34 th and 38 th finishes with times of 27:04 and 27:30.
'Emery ran sick yesterday, but she has a really good work ethic and she will eventually have a good race,' Renberg said. 'We're really looking forward to next week where we can get some good courses that are flatter and hopefully we can see on paper how much she has improved. Yana has come a long way since the start of the season and hopefully she can improve her times next week. The last few meets have been tough courses the gauge there times as they were very hilly.'
For the Spartans, their top finisher on the boys side was Austin Rasmussen, who took 10 th overall with 18:20, finishing just a little over a minute behind the winner, Gunner Wagner of Woodbine with 17:03.
'Austin ran a very consistent race against some of the best 1A runners in the area,' said Spartan Head Coach Kevin Brown. 'He seems to run his best races when he runs even, or negative splits for each mile. What really stood out to me was his finishing kick. He caught another runner with 50 meters to go which shows he never gave up.'
On the girls' side, Brown's top runner in Michelle Wilson did not run, but Brown is excited to see her compete in their next event. With Wilson not runner, Leah Boysen was the top finisher with a time of 29:07 coming in at 47 th overall.
'Sitting out Michelle is tough, because she is a state quality type of runner, but we are thinking of playing a long game with her and not over racing her,' he said. 'Michelle did a great job being a leader, even without racing. Leah ran hard the first mile and set the tone of the race. The girls team competed hard throughout the race.'
The Wolves and Vikings will run next Tuesday at 5 p.m. at the Quail Run Golf Course where they will be two of 16 schools competing. The Spartans returned to action Tuesday for an event at Panorama Elementary School where they were one of 18 to compete. According to Brown, Wilson will return for this event.
'Thursday will be a fun race to see unfold,' he added. 'Some of the best schools in the area will be there to compete. We have to concentrate on what we can control. Austin has a goal of qualifying for state this year, and it's another opportunity to run against a lot of good competition. Michelle will be back in action and will be ready to compete.'

title: Cyclone girls win Denison meet
author: Alex Martin
description: It was another strong showing for the HCHS Cyclones girls cross country team taking a first place finish as a team with 41 points, 89 points ahead of Denison who finished in second place. Yesterday wasn't that close, but you've got to stay focused no matter who you are racing each and every meet.' Senior Lindsey Sonderman won the race with a time of 18:47.
content:
It was another strong showing for the HCHS Cyclones girls cross country team taking a first place finish as a team with 41 points, 89 points ahead of Denison who finished in second place.
'I think we've ran really well,' said Cyclone Head Coach Zach Klaassen. 'It takes a lot of focus to make sure that happens. We've won a couple of really close ones. Yesterday wasn't that close, but you've got to stay focused no matter who you are racing each and every meet.'
Senior Lindsey Sonderman won the race with a time of 18:47. Freshman teammate Ashlyn Rau came in second at 19:34.64.
'It was great,' Sonderman said. 'Usually I'm not a big fan of the Denison course, but today I actually kind of enjoyed it. I think the cool weather helped and just more experience.'
Klaassen spoke on how impressed he is with the times Rau is putting up in her first season of high school cross country.
'I think she's getting more confident,' Klaassen said. 'I thought she got out and really attacked that first mile yesterday and just held on from there. I think she's becoming a better hill runner than she was at the beginning of the season, and that just comes with strength and repetition and getting after it in practice.'
Other Cyclone girls who performed strong and finished in the top 30 were Senior Brylee Schechinger in 11 th with 21:09.64, Sophomore Allie Anderson in 12 th with 21:14.61, Freshman Aspen Bieker in 15 th with 21:38.40, Sophomore Ava Freund in 20 th with 22:17.55, along with Freshman Josie Sonderman and Sophomore Sadie Alberti taking 27 th and 28 th with times of 22:51.95 and 22:52.27.
The boys finished 10 th overall with 215 points, with Woodbine taking a first place finish as a team with 60 points. Individually, Sophomore Erik Heslink finished 16 th overall with 17:53.00, almost two minutes behind Gunner Wagner of Woodbine, who won with 16:02.21. Sophomores Elijah Cox and Jeffrey Gross finished 39 th and 40 th overall with times of 19:05.74 and 19:06.07.
'I thought they ran pretty well for the most part,' Klaassen said. 'It's good to see Erik feeling like himself again, get under 18, and it was nice to see him get a medal. Elijah, that was probably one of his better races this season. He attacked two really big downhills, really just opened up, and let gravity take him down and help him. Jeffrey is running gutsy. He's in a lot of pain right now, and fighting a cold, as well. He isn't slowing down, he's fighting through it, but he's going to continue to grind it out.'
Other Cyclone boys who put up some strong times included Sophomore Nathan Sandquist with 19:50.36 finishing 62 nd overall, Sophomore Kobe Kimmen finishing 80 th with 20:24.02, Senior Jeb Sonderman in 95 th with 21:04.76, and Freshman Ramsey Gottsch with 21:17.85 in 100 th.
The Cyclones will have some time off before they return to action Oct. 10 at the Nishna Hills Golf Club in Atlantic, where they will be one of 23 schools competing. With a nine day layoff, Sonderman talked about how she plans to prepare for that race.
'Staying healthy and getting some good workouts in,' she said. 'The season is far from over, so we've got to stay in it and keep the focus.'

title: Former baton twirlers perform at Homecoming
description: Vicki Strissel's daughter, Emeri, is the HCHS Marching Band's lone baton twirler this year, and Emeri has hosted baton camps for the past few years in hope to draw more interest in the activity. She reached out to Judy Nelson, who taught baton for several years in Harlan, as well as coached baton for the Harlan Community School District for 22 years. The two contacted as many former twirlers as they could, and last Friday a group of twirlers and coaches from graduating years of 1955 - 2023 showed up to perform, including Judy Nelson, Shirley Nollen, Roseanne Larson, Cathy Murray, Vicki Petsche, Andrea Nielsen, Jana Daberkow Rieker, Nicki Petersen Ranney, Kaitlin Murray, Hope Miller, Jessie Saunders, Dori Pethoud, Jayden Gessert, and Emily Hansen.
content:
HARLAN — A group of former Harlan Community High School baton twirlers dusted off their batons to perform during the Homecoming parade and pregame show last Friday.
Vicki Strissel's daughter, Emeri, is the HCHS Marching Band's lone baton twirler this year, and Emeri has hosted baton camps for the past few years in hope to draw more interest in the activity. 'It's been a great thing for her,' Strissel said.
Strissel came up with the idea to have a reunion of sorts for the former twirlers. She reached out to Judy Nelson, who taught baton for several years in Harlan, as well as coached baton for the Harlan Community School District for 22 years. 'I thought it sounded fun, but there wasn't a lot of time for it to come together,' Nelson said.
The two contacted as many former twirlers as they could, and last Friday a group of twirlers and coaches from graduating years of 1955 - 2023 showed up to perform, including Judy Nelson, Shirley Nollen, Roseanne Larson, Cathy Murray, Vicki Petsche, Andrea Nielsen, Jana Daberkow Rieker, Nicki Petersen Ranney, Kaitlin Murray, Hope Miller, Jessie Saunders, Dori Pethoud, Jayden Gessert, and Emily Hansen. Emeri designed shirts for the group to wear during their performances.
Strissel said there wasn't a set routine. 'We made it easy, and just told them to do what they could remember.'
Nelson admitted it had been almost 25 years since she had twirled a baton. She said it was similar to riding a bike. 'You are a little wobbly at first, but then it starts to come back.'
'It takes a lot more skill than most people realize.
She enjoyed seeing some of her former students. 'Some of them have contacted me over the years. I taught a lot of kids, it's always fun to see them again.'
'It's probably one of the things I enjoyed most in my life,' she said of her years teaching.
Both said the group received a lot of positive feedback.
'It was so neat to watch their family and friends' reaction,' Strissel said. 'To see them doing something they enjoyed doing when they were younger was great.'
'It was a surprise to many, but everyone seemed to enjoy it,' Nelson said. '
Strissel said she would like to see the group reunite every year, and to add more former twirlers.

content:

According to Tufts University 4-H Study of Positive Youth Development indicate that, when compared to their peers, young people in 4-H are:

·Two times more likely to pursue healthy behaviors.
·Two times more likely to engage in Science, Technology, Engineering and Math (STEM) programs during out-of-school time.
