HMU celebrates 30 years of providing cable TV and internet
By:
HARLAN — In the early 1990's, the Harlan Municipal Utilities (HMU) Board of Trustees began discussing a municipal telecommunications system. However, at the time, several hurdles stood in the way. In May 1995, residents of Harlan voted on two measures to establish broadband cable communications as a municipal utility, which passed, setting the stage for HMU to offer broadband cable and internet service. Design and construction took place in 1995 and 1996, and both cable TV and internet services were available in early fall 1996. Shortly after, discussions regarding telephone service were held, and a decision was made to add telephone as the third telecom service, which was offered in 2001.
Over two decades later, HMU continues to provide the most up-to-date telecom services to the residents of Harlan. HMU's telephone service is locally owned, operated and supported. HMU prides itself as being one-call service for telephone, cable TV, and high-speed internet needs for Harlan residents, which is combined into one bill for customers. 'More of your money stays right here in Harlan working for you,' said Joe Rueschenberg, CEO.
In 2019, almost all of Harlan was serviced by a direct fiber connection, making it virtually 'future proof', meaning it will be almost impossible to exceed the technical capabilities of the fiber connection. Fiber allows for more data over a smaller physical connection, meaning a greater amount of material or items passing through a system or process. This allows HMU to offer enhanced data services now and in the future. At about 1/11th the size of a human hair, fiber allows for more data over a smaller physical connection allowing greater throughput for more HD video channels and almost unlimited Internet capacity. A fiber connection means HMU is poised to offer enhanced data services now and in the future.
'In 2024 HMU upgraded our internet carriers. We have multiple carriers we get internet from. This diversifies our connection, giving us better reliability,' said Brian Dotzler, Telecommunications Superintendent. The change, was completed in April, which allows HMU to double the speed to all internet customers. In addition, HMU's email platform was upgraded to a cloud-based system. This allowed increased accessibility from any device, cost savings by eliminating the need for on-premise hardware, enhanced data security through centralized backups, scalability to meet fluctuating demands, improved collaboration capabilities, disaster recovery options, and greater flexibility in deploying applications. 'It's no longer hosted on servers at HMU which provides better reliability for our customers with multiple backups,' said Dotzler.
HMU also introduced a new wireless router to internet customers called a GigaSpire. 'It's a great new addition,' said Dotzler. The router allows customers to install an app on their phone to control their home's wireless network (wifi). 'They can kick a device off, change the wifi password, make a guest account, basically control the router through the app. It's good to allow customers to make those changes. It gives them the flexibility to control their own items,' said Dotzler.
New applications, such as smart home services, remote thermostat control, smart appliances, and accessing camera systems, are available to consumers by manufacturers. HMU believes they are ready for whatever the future may bring.
HMU's cable line-up includes two local school and community event programming channels. These channels were recently upgraded to high definition. 'We aired every football game and most of the many other sporting and community events. We updated the equipment so we can put a scoreboard on the live broadcast,' said Dotzler. 'We've received a good response.' The live events are shown on the local channels and also broadcast on YouTube at www.youtube.com/ @HarlanUtilities
Editor's Note: This article is the fourth and final in a series of articles highlighting each of HMU's departments and recent improvements.

title: Cyclones lose close battle to Falcons
author: Alex Martin
description: In the fourth quarter with 4.1 seconds remaining in regulation with the St. Albert Falcons leading by two, the HCHS Cyclones boys basketball team inbounded the ball, got it to Senior Jozef Reisz, who went up for a layup, but couldn't sink the shot and the Cyclones lost 56-54. Following Reisz' shot, both teams exchanged buckets with the final shot of the quarter coming from 3-pointer range from Freshman Falcon Cooper Hamilton putting his team up 10-7. Shots continued to get exchanged when a scary moment for the Cyclones occurred when Senior Ben Leinen went up for a shot, landed awkwardly on his foot, left the game, and didn't return.
content:
In the fourth quarter with 4.1 seconds remaining in regulation with the St. Albert Falcons leading by two, the HCHS Cyclones boys basketball team inbounded the ball, got it to Senior Jozef Reisz, who went up for a layup, but couldn't sink the shot and the Cyclones lost 56-54.
'He [Reisz] got fouled by three different guys,' said Cyclone Head Coach Mitch Osborn. 'He got held and hacked on the shot, so it's disappointing on your home floor. You've got to fight through it.'
Junior Falcon Noah Narmi opened the game with the first shot, but Reisz immediately responded with a shot at the basket to tie the game at two. Following Reisz' shot, both teams exchanged buckets with the final shot of the quarter coming from 3-pointer range from Freshman Falcon Cooper Hamilton putting his team up 10-7.
Sophomore Cyclone Kobe Klaassen got his team back in the game only seconds into the second quarter with a 3-pointer tying the game at 10.
Shots continued to get exchanged when a scary moment for the Cyclones occurred when Senior Ben Leinen went up for a shot, landed awkwardly on his foot, left the game, and didn't return.
'He's got to get it x-rayed,' Osborn said of Leinen. 'It's not good. Hopefully nothing is broken, but right now it doesn't look good.'
Following Leinen's exit, both teams continued to match each other until Hamilton and Senior Falcon Joe Hughes made back-to-back buckets. However, Klaassen made a shot, was fouled in the act of shooting, and made the extra point to keep his team within striking distance as they trailed 23-20 at halftime.
'We felt like defensively we played great,' Osborn said. 'Offensively, we weren't executing very well. Give St. Albert credit. We can't have those scoring droughts.'
Cyclones Junior Dallas McDowell got going in the second half with a 3-point shot, followed later by a shot at the basket to cut the Falcons lead to two. Hughes made a 3-pointer to force a timeout from Osborn. Following Osborn's timeout, the Cyclone offense answered with back-to-back baskets from Senior Bryce Van Baale and Klaassen, but the Cyclones still trailed 39-35 entering the fourth quarter.
Junior Cyclone Gabe Arkfeld stepped up for his team on the offense end of the floor in the fourth quarter contributing with six points, which was followed by a bucket from McDowell tying the game at 46, forcing a timeout from St. Albert.
'Dallas came up big,' Osborn said. 'Gabe Arkfeld did a great job. We're so short-handed and we really can't play man-to-man.'
The Cyclones got their first lead of the game when Reisz was sent to the free throw line making one of two buckets, putting his team up 49-48. Junior Falcon Nick Ballenger made a 3-point shot to get his team back in front, but Reisz tied the game immediately at 51 with a shot at the basket.
Unfortunately, the Cyclones couldn't get over the hump dropping the game for their fourth loss of the season. They will be back in action Tuesday on the road against the 9-2 Glenwood Rams. The Rams are led by Senior Ayden Gibson averaging 19.6 points and 9.3 rebounds per game, along with Junior Jack Johnson averaging 3.6 assists.
'It's going to be extremely tough at their place,' Osborn said. 'They're loaded. They're 9-2, and we probably won't have Ben [Leinen], and we'll just have to go out and do our best.'

title: Spartans struggle on the road against the Tigers
author: Alex Martin
description: The struggles continue for the Exira-EHK Spartans boys basketball team as they've dropped their fifth consecutive game, most recently losing 78-44 Tuesday night to the Woodbine Tigers. The Tiger offense came out of the gate aggressively opening the quarter with a 7-0 run before Senior Spartan Josh Nelson made a 3-pointer to get his team on the board, which would be followed shortly after by another 3-point shot, to keep his team within striking distance. The Tigers continued to put offensive runs together going on another 6-0 run, but just before the quarter Nelson made his third 3-pointer of the game to have nine of the 11 Spartans points trailing 24-11.
content:
The struggles continue for the Exira-EHK Spartans boys basketball team as they've dropped their fifth consecutive game, most recently losing 78-44 Tuesday night to the Woodbine Tigers.
'What I keep telling them is that we've got to play with energy, with passion, and working our tails off, and making sure we're doing the right things,' said Spartan Head Coach Tony Santisteban. 'I like what I've seen the last week and a half, where the scoreboard isn't always what we want it to be. Woodbine is a great team.'
The Tiger offense came out of the gate aggressively opening the quarter with a 7-0 run before Senior Spartan Josh Nelson made a 3-pointer to get his team on the board, which would be followed shortly after by another 3-point shot, to keep his team within striking distance.
The Tigers continued to put offensive runs together going on another 6-0 run, but just before the quarter Nelson made his third 3-pointer of the game to have nine of the 11 Spartans points trailing 24-11.
'If he [Nelson] hits his first shot, he normally is feeling pretty good for the rest of the game,' Santisteban said. 'He's in aggressive mode and he's ready to go. He's got a good shot. If they leave him any space, he can knock it down.'
Nelson continued his dominance from 3-point territory with another shot to open the second quarter, but the Tiger offense continued to get shots from Brody Pryor, Carter Gruver, and Landon Blum. Nelson responded with a mid-range jumper giving himself 14 points on the night.
Santisteban called a timeout shortly after Nelson's shot. When play resumed, Nelson made another 3-pointer, his fifth of the game. Junior Spartan Owen Juhl got in on the action sinking a 3-pointer, followed by a mid-range basket from Nelson, but the Tiger offense continued to make shots, taking a 48-31 lead into halftime.
'We needed to take care of the ball, and we ended up not doing that,' Santisteban said. 'When that's the case, they spread the lead, because they get layups or we have too many turnovers and that swings the game more wide open than what it was.'
The third quarter was dominated by the Tiger offense, outscoring the Spartans 20-2 with the only shot of the quarter coming from Nelson after the Tigers opened the quarter with a 15-0 run.
However, in the fourth quarter, the Spartan offense turned the tables on the Tigers for a moment with the first four buckets coming from Junior Austin Rasmussen, Nelson, and Juhl, but it wasn't enough as the Spartans lost their eighth game of the season.
The Spartans returned home Thursday night for a showdown with the 8-3 Ar-We-Va Rockets. The Rockets are led by Senior Blayne Smith averaging 15.3 points, 9.9 rebounds, and 2.8 assists per game.
'Coach [Matt] Wilken is going to have Ar-We-Va ready,' Santisteban said. 'They play hard for him. They have been going on a little bit of a winning streak themselves. We've just got to play some good sound fundamental basketball. If we can do that, then we'll be able to make it a game hopefully and just go from there.'

title: Shelby County Extension Council elects officers
description: SHELBY COUNTY — Four officers were elected during the Iowa State University Extension and Outreach Shelby County extension council organizational meeting January 7, 2025. Kathy Fara will preside at all meetings of the county extension council, have authority to call special meetings and perform duties as performed and exercised by a chairperson of a board of directors of a corporation. Kristina Larsen, Harlan, was elected secretary and has the responsibility of keeping the minutes of all county extension council meetings and signing required papers for the council.
content:
SHELBY COUNTY — Four officers were elected during the Iowa State University Extension and Outreach Shelby County extension council organizational meeting January 7, 2025. The nine-member county extension council annually elects officers to comply with federal and state laws to aid in disseminating useful and practical information from the state's land grant university to the people of Iowa.
Kathy Fara, Irwin, is the newly-elected chairperson. Kathy Fara will preside at all meetings of the county extension council, have authority to call special meetings and perform duties as performed and exercised by a chairperson of a board of directors of a corporation. Brenda Arkfeld, Portsmouth, elected vice chairperson.
Kristina Larsen, Harlan, was elected secretary and has the responsibility of keeping the minutes of all county extension council meetings and signing required papers for the council.
The council elected Elaine Baughman, Kirkman, to the treasurer position. The treasurer has charge of all of the funds of the county extension council; receives, deposits, pays and disburses. The treasurer ensures an accurate record of receipts and disbursements and submits reports to the county extension council.
As elected officials, the county extension council is the local governing body of ISU Extension and Outreach. The county extension council hires county staff, manages the county extension budget of approximately $ 330,000, and helps determine programming. In partnership with Iowa State University, the council provides educational opportunities that bring university resources to the needs of the county and region.
ISU Extension and Outreach is part of the federal Cooperative Extension Service — a network of more than 100 land-grant institutions, including Iowa State University, and the U.S. Department of Agriculture serving communities and counties across the United States. Every county in Iowa has an elected extension council that decides how to support ISU Extension and Outreach educational programs at the county level.
The county extension office is located at 906 6th Street in Harlan. To learn more about ISU Extension and Outreach in Shelby County, visit www.extension.iastate.edu/shelby. For more information about ISU Extension and Outreach, visit www.extension.iastate.

title: Books & Beyond: Harlan Community Library kicks off fundraising for outdoor revitalization project
author: Renée Brich
description: HARLAN — Learn about the Harlan Community Library's outdoor revitalization project at a family friendly event,' Books & Beyond Kick-Off', Thursday, January 23 at 5 p.m. Plans for the outdoor renovation project include white washing the building, new signage, an outdoor learning space, continuous access to wireless internet and outdoor charging stations, a musical garden, and accessible seating areas. Most of our outdoor seating now is in rock beds around the buildings, which prohibits people with ambulatory issues from using our outdoor facilities,' Brewer said.
content:
HARLAN — Learn about the Harlan Community Library's outdoor revitalization project at a family friendly event,' Books & Beyond Kick-Off', Thursday, January 23 at 5 p.m. The event will feature a kids' activity and refreshments will be served.
'The library has become so very active the last eight years. We want to make the outside of building more visible,' said Library Director Amanda Brewer.
Plans for the outdoor renovation project include white washing the building, new signage, an outdoor learning space, continuous access to wireless internet and outdoor charging stations, a musical garden, and accessible seating areas.
Murals will also be featured on the outside of the building. 'The City is trying to expand the presence of art in the community, so the murals will reflect both the community and the library,' Brewer said.
The sidewalks will be replaced, and seating will be on concrete, making it accessible for everyone. 'We have accessibility issues. Most of our outdoor seating now is in rock beds around the buildings, which prohibits people with ambulatory issues from using our outdoor facilities,' Brewer said.
Brewer said in 2021, the library received a grant for lighted outdoor charging stations. 'One of the biggest issues facing our community is the high cost of internet,' she said. 'On any given month the library has about 2,800 hits on our wifi. We have people who sit outside, even in the cold, to use our wifi.' The outdoor charging stations and seating will be accessible when the library is closed.
An outdoor storytime area will be located on the westside of the building, and will feature sensory friendly music equipment. Brewer said the popularity of the library's storytime hour has grown, and with the new space, attendees will be able to enjoy the event outside when weather permits.
The renovation will also include a landscaping update and an additional safety exit will be installed for library staff to use if needed.
Brewer said the goal is to fundraise throughout 2025, and break ground on the project spring of 2026. The cost of the project is $200,000, and the Harlan Community Library Foundation will match funds up to $100,000.
For more information about donating to the project, please contact the library or visit the website at www.harlan.lib.ia.us
Brewer said in-kind donations will also be appreciated if any area businesses would like to volunteer their services.
'We are excited about it,' Brewer said. 'It's time to enhance the outdoor area and improve safety and accessibility.'

title: Cyclones struggle against Knights
author: Alex Martin
description: Facing the #2 ranked Kuemper Catholic Knights on the road, the HCHS Cyclones boys basketball team knew they had a challenge ahead of them. 'We actually played pretty good the first half,' said Cyclone Head Coach Mitch Osborn. The Cyclones trailed by eight at the end of the first quarter, and continued to trail in the second quarter being down by 18 at halftime.
content:
Facing the #2 ranked Kuemper Catholic Knights on the road, the HCHS Cyclones boys basketball team knew they had a challenge ahead of them. Despite a strong first half, the Cyclones lost 83-51.
'We actually played pretty good the first half,' said Cyclone Head Coach Mitch Osborn. 'We had 13 turnovers at halftime. That was the backbreaker. We said taking care of the ball was going to the point of emphasis. You could say it, talk about it, but doing it are two different things because Kuemper is so good.'
The Cyclones trailed by eight at the end of the first quarter, and continued to trail in the second quarter being down by 18 at halftime.
'We just said we've got to try and put a run together and get some stops,' Osborn said. 'You can't get it all back at once. You try to get the game to single digits. You can't trade baskets.'
Offensively, the Cyclones were led by Jozef Reisz with 16 points, eight rebounds, and two steals. Kobe Klaassen and Dallas McDowell were also in double figures as Klaassen came away with 12 points, and McDowell at 11. Senior Bryce Van Baale had five points off the bench, including nine rebounds and one steal.
'Dallas and Kobe struggled,' Osborn added. 'Dallas was 3-for-12 and Kobe was 3-for-13. Jozef did a nice job inside and Bryce played well.'
In the second half, the Knights continued to score with the Cyclones playing catch-up trailing 25 at the end of the third quarter and finishing 32 points behind the Knights at the end of regulation.
'The third quarter we scored, but the problem was we didn't play good defensively, and they got hot from 3's,' Osborn said. 'We knew we were up against a lot, but our kids played hard. We've just got to do a little bit better of a job taking care of the ball.'
The Cyclones return home Friday night to take on the 1-2 Blair Bears. The Bears one win came against Lincoln Northwest, while taking two losses to Norris and Waverly.
'We've just got to keep working to improve in practice,' he said. 'We'll get ready for Wednesday and Thursday. It's hard to simulate Kuemper's quickness and how they play defense. We've got to try and make things a little bit tougher in practice so the games are easier.'

title: Cyclones first half proves costly against Bears
author: Alex Martin
description: The HCHS Cyclones went quiet to open the game Friday as the Blair Bears opened the game on a 9-0, which forced a timeout from Cyclone head coach Mitch Osborn. When play resumed, Junior Cyclone Dallas McDowell got the Cyclones their first points of the game, but the Bears continued to make shots going on another 8-2 run putting themselves up 17-12 en route to a 73-62 victory. In the second quarter, the Bears got the first shot from Cooper Sorensen, expanding their lead to 18, but the Cyclones were able to slowly chip away with free throws from Senior Ben Leinen and a layup from Senior Jozef Reisz.
content:
The HCHS Cyclones went quiet to open the game Friday as the Blair Bears opened the game on a 9-0, which forced a timeout from Cyclone head coach Mitch Osborn. When play resumed, Junior Cyclone Dallas McDowell got the Cyclones their first points of the game, but the Bears continued to make shots going on another 8-2 run putting themselves up 17-12 en route to a 73-62 victory.
'I wasn't very pleased with how we started,' said Cyclone Head Coach Mitch Osborn. 'In the second half, we didn't fold. We were still down by quite a few in the fourth quarter and we got it cut to nine. We just can't dig that deep of a hole. They [Blair] shot the ball extremely well.'
In the second quarter, the Bears got the first shot from Cooper Sorensen, expanding their lead to 18, but the Cyclones were able to slowly chip away with free throws from Senior Ben Leinen and a layup from Senior Jozef Reisz.
Reisz got another layup and was fouled in the act of shooting, where he missed the free throw, but Sophomore Kobe Klaassen was there to grab the rebound, and was fouled where he went to the line making both free throws.
Reisz got the final shot of the quarter on a layup, but the Cyclones still trailed 41-21 at halftime.
'We just said you can't get it all back at once,' Osborn said. 'We first need to get it back to single digits, but we didn't. They sort of maintained their lead.'
In the third quarter despite a large deficit, the Cyclone offense attempted to chip away at the Bears lead starting with free throws from Leinen and a 3-pointer from Leinen, but the Bears continued to have answer with a mid-range jump shot from Kalan Steinbeck and a 3-pointer form Aidan Slominski.
Approaching the end of the quarter, the Cyclones got back-to-back buckets from McDowell and Klaassen, followed by Klaassen making a 3-pointer for the final shot of the quarter, but the Cyclones still trailed by 19.
In the fourth quarter, the Cyclones offense got going a little bit starting with back-to-back shots from Leinen, including a 3-pointer and a layup. Junior Gabe Arkfeld scored soon after with a put-back. A few more 3-pointers were made from Klaassen and Sophomore Colton Schneider, but it wasn't enough as the Cyclones lost their second consecutive game.
Cyclones drop weekend road match to Eagles
The Cyclones were hoping for a bounce back game Saturday afternoon on the road against the Underwood Eagles, but lost again 58-44.
'We were struggling at the offensive end of the floor, especially in the second half,' said Cyclone Head Coach Mitch Osborn. 'They [Underwood] did a great job locking Kobe Klaassen up. We couldn't really get him on track. In order to be successful, we need Dallas [McDowell], Kobe, and Jozef [Reisz] each with 15-20 points.'
The Cyclones got off to a strong start leading 16-14 at the end of the first quarter, but still had a chance to win being down just 33-28 at halftime.
'We needed to do a better job of rebounding and we did okay taking care of the ball,' Osborn said. 'It's one thing or another. We need more consistency.'
Offensively, McDowell the way with 17 points, followed by Reisz with 14, and Sophomore Colton Schneider with five.
'We had some good balance,' Osborn added. 'Colton Schneider hits a 3, Kobe hit one, and Dallas hit one. We went inside to Jozef and Ben [Leinen] attacked the rim, so we had good balance there.'
The Eagles were led by Nolan Baker with 21 points, followed by Garrett Luett with 11, and Tayden Hull with 10.
The Cyclones return to action Tuesday at home against the 0-12 Denison Monarchs. The Monarchs are led by Junior Blaine Grady averaging 8.2 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 1.3 assists per game.
'They're struggling this year,' Osborn said. 'We're looking forward to having them for that home game. I think we have four straight home games. We've got to try and take advantage of that.'

title: Schmitz signs LOI for equestrian at SDSU
author: Alex Martin
description: HCHS Senior Katy Schmitz will be heading off to South Dakota State University for horseback riding. With multiple choices in front of her, Schmitz talked about what led to her choosing SDSU. The Equestrian team at SDSU currently sits at 2-4 on the season, with wins against UC Davis and Minnesota Crookston.
content:
HCHS Senior Katy Schmitz will be heading off to South Dakota State University for horseback riding.
'I'm really excited and really grateful,' Schmitz said. 'It took a lot of work to get to this point. I've been competitively showing for 10 years now, and I'm very grateful for the opportunity.'
With multiple choices in front of her, Schmitz talked about what led to her choosing SDSU.
'I really like the environment and I got to visit there,' she said. 'I really liked the team. They were all super kind. The campus is beautiful and it just felt like home.'
The Equestrian team at SDSU currently sits at 2-4 on the season, with wins against UC Davis and Minnesota Crookston. The roster currently has 34 athletes, a vast majority being underclassmen.
Schmitz plans to major in pre-chiropractic's during her time at SDSU, along with some goals she has for her time in college.
'I hope to do well academically and athletically,' Schmitz said. 'I can't wait for more opportunities and I can't wait to learn.'
Even though her high school days have yet to conclude, Schmitz is grateful for her time at HCHS.
'I've made a whole bunch of friends and they have helped support me through my journey,' she said.
During the signing, Schmitz's brother and sister, Ethan and Clara, along with her mom, Jana, and her dad, Jeff, were there to show their support.
'I travel a lot when I show,' Schmitz added. 'My family has definitely helped pick up the slack at home. Mainly my mom, she'll drop everything and she'll help me travel. She's my number one supporter, so I'm very grateful for her.'

title: Cyclones cruise to home win over Huskies
author: Alex Martin
description: Leading by just six points approaching the end of the third quarter, Sophomore Cyclone Brinley Van Baale made back-to-back 3-point shots, followed by a layup from Sophomore Kenzley Bruck, helping lead the Cyclones to their 16 th win of the season over the Winterset Huskies 64-55. The Cyclone offense got going when Van Baale sunk a mid-range floater, followed by a mid-range jump shot from Bruck. As the quarter was winding down, Senior Molly Swensen made back-to-back 3-pointers before Schwieso closed out the quarter with a buzzer beater 3-point shot that went off the backboard for a 20-14 lead.
content:
Leading by just six points approaching the end of the third quarter, Sophomore Cyclone Brinley Van Baale made back-to-back 3-point shots, followed by a layup from Sophomore Kenzley Bruck, helping lead the Cyclones to their 16 th win of the season over the Winterset Huskies 64-55.
'I've been working on my 3's in practice,' Van Baale said. 'They haven't been falling that much this year, so it's a really good feeling just to see them go through the hoop and without my teammates I wouldn't get those looks, so it's a really good feeling to help out the team.'
Cyclone Senior Aubrey Schwieso scored the first basket of the night when she drove to the hoop for a layup, which was followed by free throws from Senior Grace Albertsen.
The Cyclone offense got going when Van Baale sunk a mid-range floater, followed by a mid-range jump shot from Bruck. As the quarter was winding down, Senior Molly Swensen made back-to-back 3-pointers before Schwieso closed out the quarter with a buzzer beater 3-point shot that went off the backboard for a 20-14 lead.
'It's always nice when you have a little bit of room to work with,' Van Baale said. 'You want to keep it up though. Those two [Swensen & Schwieso] are great players, so it's really fun.'
Schwieso opened the second quarter with a mid-range jump shot, followed by a layup from Swensen forcing a timeout from Winterset head coach Matt Young. When play resumed, Schwieso got possession of the ball drove to the hoop and made a bounce pass to Bruck, who went for a layup expanding the Cyclone lead 26-14.
Approaching the 3-minute mark, Sophomore Makenna Olson helped close the gap on the Cyclones when she made back-to-back shots, forcing a timeout from Cyclone head coach Zach Klaassen. Following Klaassen's timeout, the Cyclones closed out the half on a 6-3 run leading 36-25.
'I was just talking about when we took the high post away we eliminated penetration, they struggled to score,' Klaassen said. 'All of a sudden, [Makenna Olson] caught fire. She was on our radar before the game started. She hit two right there at the end of the second quarter there to keep it a little closer than what it was, so we focused on her at halftime that we were going to try and take her away.'
The Huskies opened the third quarter immediately getting the game back within single digits when Sophomore Natalie Smith and Senior Ashlynn Devine made back-to-back shots, which was followed soon after by a 3-pointer from Olson. However, Bruck continued to find shots making multiple mid-range jumpers to keep her team in front.
Winterset continued to keep the game close when Olson made another 3-pointer along with a layup under the hoop from Acton, cutting the Cyclones lead down to five points. The Cyclones closed out the quarter on an 8-0 run with 3-point shots from Van Baale and a layup from Bruck leading 53-39.
'She [Van Baale] hit the first one and the second one, she didn't question anything,' Klaassen said. 'It was catch and release and nothing but net. We need those kids with confidence and when they're open they've got to shoot, otherwise nobody's ever going to guard them. If they're hitting, it makes us really tough.'
The 3-point shot continued to fall for the Cyclones when Junior Addison Wicks opened the fourth quarter with one. The Huskies continued to fight back going on a 7-0 run, before Schwieso stole the ball, and drove to the hoop for another layup. Following Schwieso's layup, the Huskies went on another 6-0 run with back-to-back 3's from Acton and Smith cutting the Cyclones lead down to six.
The Cyclones were able to hang on for their 16 th win of the season and ninth consecutive, moving to 16-3 overall. They return to action Friday with the 9-8 Lewis Central Titans coming to town. The Titans are led by Senior Brooke Larsen averaging 19.3 points, 11.9 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game.
'When we played them at Lewis Central, he [Klaassen] had us bring a defense where one of us locks her [Larsen] down,' Van Baale said. 'We did pretty good. She averages a lot per game and we kept her below 10, so it's very helpful when we do that. I'm not sure what the plan is yet, but I'm sure we'll have a plan for her and the rest of the team. It should be a good game.'

title: Spartans ground Eagles to advance
author: Alex Martin
description: Leading by 13 at halftime in the Class 2A – Region 7 First Round Regional Game, the Exira-EHK Spartans kept their foot on the gas pedal opening the third quarter on a 12-0 run leading themselves to a 61-33 victory over the Underwood Eagles, punching their ticket to the second round. The offense got going soon though when Junior Spartan Kadence Sporrer and Sophomore Taryn Petersen connected making 3's of their own, trailing 12-10 at the end of the first quarter. In the second quarter, Senior Eagle Haley Stangl made a layup, but the Spartans got going on the offensive end of the floor with a 14-0 run with a 3-point shot from Sporrer, a layup from Taryn Petersen, and free throws from Jaelynn Petersen leading to a 13-point halftime lead.
content:
Leading by 13 at halftime in the Class 2A – Region 7 First Round Regional Game, the Exira-EHK Spartans kept their foot on the gas pedal opening the third quarter on a 12-0 run leading themselves to a 61-33 victory over the Underwood Eagles, punching their ticket to the second round.
'I'm very proud of the kids and what we did tonight especially on the defensive side,' said Spartan Head Coach Tom Petersen. 'We made a few adjustments here and there. I think they [Underwood] had 10 in the first quarter, and then 23 for the rest of the game. Our kids played some darn good defense.'
The game began with back-to-back 3-point shots from Sophomore Eagle Ainsley Roberts and Senior Tieler Hull as the Spartans found themselves trailing 6-0 early. The offense got going soon though when Junior Spartan Kadence Sporrer and Sophomore Taryn Petersen connected making 3's of their own, trailing 12-10 at the end of the first quarter.
In the second quarter, Senior Eagle Haley Stangl made a layup, but the Spartans got going on the offensive end of the floor with a 14-0 run with a 3-point shot from Sporrer, a layup from Taryn Petersen, and free throws from Jaelynn Petersen leading to a 13-point halftime lead.
'Our communication was what really kept us going,' said Jaelynn Petersen. 'The girls behind were able to tell the girls up front to go to the boards, and it really just worked itself out from there.'
In the third quarter, the Spartans offense continued to dominate going on a 12-0 run starting with back-to-back layups from Taryn and Jaelynn, followed by layups from Senior Harlee Fahn and Jaelynn, forcing a timeout from Underwood.
'She [Jaelynn] was running the floor,' said Tom Petersen. 'Taryn was looking at her and throwing full court passes all the way up the floor. It's stuff that we've worked on in practice and you've got to be able to apply it when kids are out in front.'
Following Underwood's timeout, Sporrer banked home a 3-pointer followed later by another two layups from Jaelynn. The Eagles closed out the quarter with a 3-point shot from Roberts, but still trailed by 25.
Jaelynn began the fourth quarter with a layup, along with making a 3-pointer. Sophomore Riley Miller got in on the action making a 3-pointer as the Spartans easily cruised to victory.
'Coming into the first game, I feel like we prepped really well,' said Jaelynn Petersen. 'Getting the first win and being able to move forward, it's just adrenaline pumping for us.'
The Spartans will play the 20-2 MVAOCOU Rams Friday, who defeated the AHSTW Vikings in the first round 71-47. The Rams are led by Senior Trista Ohlmeier averaging 16.3 points, 10.9 rebounds, and 4.9 assists per game.
'For 32 minutes, we've got to be able to play,' said Tom Petersen. 'Basketball is a game of runs. They're going to make some runs, we're going to make some runs and we've got to be able to bounce back regardless of what the situation is. Hopefully the girls are up for that challenge. They [Rams] have talent all over the floor. It's all about preparation for the next two days.'

title: Supervisors approve salary increase for county officials
description: SHELBY COUNTY ­ ­— The Shelby County Board of Supervisors voted to increase the salaries of some elected officials by 3.5% in fiscal year 2026. The increase was based on the recommendation of the compensation board, represented by Ruthanne Grimsley, at the board meeting Tuesday, February 18. Gross's proposal to the compensation board was for a 6% pay increase, and after discussion, the Supervisors voted to increase his pay 6%.
content:
SHELBY COUNTY ­ ­— The Shelby County Board of Supervisors voted to increase the salaries of some elected officials by 3.5% in fiscal year 2026.
The increase was based on the recommendation of the compensation board, represented by Ruthanne Grimsley, at the board meeting Tuesday, February 18. Grimsley said the recommended increase was based on current salaries for those same positions in similar sized counties. The approved 3.5% increase would pertain to the county's auditor, recorder, attorney, and treasurer.
The compensation board recommended a 9.5% increase for Sheriff Neil Gross. Gross's proposal to the compensation board was for a 6% pay increase, and after discussion, the Supervisors voted to increase his pay 6%.
'With the budget we have to work with right now. . . I'm not comfortable with 9.5%. It's a big chunk of money. We do need to catch up, but maybe do it over time,' said Supervisor Mike Kolbe.
'I agree with what Neil recommended,' said Supervisor Charles Parkhurst.
In other business, County Pipeline Liasion Steve Kenkel provided an update on the proposed Summit Carbon Solution pipeline. More on Kenkel's update may be found in the Tuesday, February 25 edition of the Harlan Tribune.
The board also approved a 28E Cooperative Agreement for a Competitive Highway Bridge Program (CHBP) Grant Project. Shelby County, along with 20+ other counties, cities and the Iowa Department of Transportation (Iowa DOT), is applying to receive funding to help rebuild 33 bridges in poor condition across the state. Shelby County is applying for funding assistance to replace a concrete box culvert on Hwy F-24 west of Earling.
County Engineer Chris Fredericksen said, 'It sounds positive this will happen and we will get some funding through this grant.'

title: Lady Vikings open with Early Bird Event
author: Alex Martin
description: The AHSTW Lady Vikings track and field team are back in action , practicing for the upcoming season set to begin in a few weeks. During the 2024 season, the Vikings were led by Brooke Lee in the 100m dash with 13.78, Delaney Goshorn in the 200m dash with 27.86, Bella Lamp in the 400m with 1:03.78, and Macey Goshorn in the 800m dash with 2:37.15. Pelzer will be looking to his seniors this year to lead the way, along with some returners including Lamp, who qualified for state in four events as a freshman.
content:
The AHSTW Lady Vikings track and field team are back in action , practicing for the upcoming season set to begin in a few weeks.
'As a group, I think we are all very ready for this season,' said Viking Head Coach Traye Pelzer. 'We have a lot of goals for improvement and are excited to get started.'
Pelzer and his assistant coach, Kinsey Scheffler, have been highlighting what will be key to performing their best on race day.
'This year, there is an emphasis on doing all the small things correctly,' Pelzer said. 'Every rep is a chance to improve, and it will translate to good habits and hopefully success on the track.'
During the 2024 season, the Vikings were led by Brooke Lee in the 100m dash with 13.78, Delaney Goshorn in the 200m dash with 27.86, Bella Lamp in the 400m with 1:03.78, and Macey Goshorn in the 800m dash with 2:37.15.
In the long distance events, Rylie Knop set the tone in the 1500 and 3000m run with times of 6:02.34 and 12:47.87.
Pelzer will be looking to his seniors this year to lead the way, along with some returners including Lamp, who qualified for state in four events as a freshman.
'We have a strong returning cast of runners this year. I return three seniors who were integral in the success that we had last year,' he said. 'Caitlyn Dills, Loralei Wahling, and Brooklyn Buck will all be important leaders for us throughout the season. Ava Paulsen and Bella Lamp return as key members of our middle distance core. I'm also very excited for many of my sophomores and freshmen. We will have lots of options, thanks to the hard work that everyone has displayed so far through practices.'
March 31 will be the Vikings first event of the season at the Audubon Early Bird, where they will be one of 14 schools in attendance.
'We plan to take everyone to Audubon for the Early Bird Meet,' Pelzer said. 'It is a great meet to start the season with, a lot of great teams to run against early in the season. Key to starting off on the right foot is to embrace that early challenge and compete no matter where we are in the race.'
Pelzer talked about the challenges of getting through the long track season, along with some of the tougher schools he feels the girls will compete against.
'We expect tough competition at just about all the meets we will attend,' he said. 'We have a very tough conference when it comes to track. Riverside, Tri-Center, Treynor, Underwood, Logan-Magnolia, IKM-Manning, Missouri Valley, and Audubon all have talented runners that will challenge us just about everywhere we go. The nice thing about a tough conference is that it fuels excellence, and in that regard, we are very lucky to be a part of the Western Iowa Conference.'

title: Vikings open new track season
author: Alex Martin
description: The AHSTW Vikings boys track and field team is preparing for another season, and despite the small roster, Head Coach Jackson Renberg is excited to have the season start. Renberg is expecting leadership from returning team members, including Jett Peterson and Luke Sternberg. 'Despite battling injuries, he got better from his sophomore year to his junior year, which was great to see,' Renberg said of Peterson, who qualified for State his sophomore year.
content:
The AHSTW Vikings boys track and field team is preparing for another season, and despite the small roster, Head Coach Jackson Renberg is excited to have the season start.
'The group we have is about 15 kids in total, but they have all been working hard and gradually progressing so far this season,' Renberg said.
Renberg is expecting leadership from returning team members, including Jett Peterson and Luke Sternberg.
'Despite battling injuries, he got better from his sophomore year to his junior year, which was great to see,' Renberg said of Peterson, who qualified for State his sophomore year. 'He is hungry and motivated to have a good senior season.'
Sternberg will be the team's top sprinter, running both the 200 and 400 meter dash. 'We will utilize him in some different relays or individual events throughout the season, as well,' said Renerg.
Newcomers Kayden Sandbothe and Jackson Jensen have looked good in practice so far, and Renberg said, 'We are excited to have them out.'
Renberg and Assistant Coach Gage Clay are helping the athletes realize the key to race day success.
'We have really been emphasizing getting in shape, and while doing it really focusing on our form,' Renberg said. 'We have been lucky and have been outside this far. The next few weeks we will continue to focus on those things, but also get going on the handoffs, blocks, and work on field events as well.'
The Vikings' first meet will be the IATC Indoor Championships held March 13 at Iowa State University's Lied Recreation Center.
'Hopefully, Luke will run the 400 and 200 at the ISU Indoor meet,' Renberg said. 'We also will have Collin Harder run the mile. The 4x8 team of Ty Nelson, Caden Geraghty, Chase Wheatley, and Collin will also run as well at the meet. Jett is also looking to throw the shot put. We can only take ones that will qualify, so some will stay back and practice on that day, and hopefully they can go next year if we like the meet. It appears to be a great situation for a lot of upper-classman to get a chance to compete against competition they don't see very often, and also see where they are at this early in the season and what we need to look at to get our guys better in the future.'
Renberg talked about some of the hurdles he feels his team will battle throughout the season, and what will be key to overcoming those challenges.
'I think the biggest challenge we will have is trying to figure out our lineup early in the year,' he said. 'We have a lot of new kids out, and we lost about six upperclassmen from last year. Therefore, we have some newcomers that will have to step up on our team to help us in some events. I am excited for some of those younger guys to take on big roles for our team. I am also excited for the juniors and seniors to take on leadership roles and take bigger steps to help the team in various ways.'

title: Albertsen commits to play basketball at Iowa Western
author: Alex Martin
description: HCHS Senior Grace Albertsen will continue her education and basketball career at Iowa Western. Albertsen said Iowa Western made her feel at home. Albertsen's coaches, Zach Klaassen, Mark Kohorst, and Sam Brummer, were all in attendance at the letter of intent signing.
content:
HCHS Senior Grace Albertsen will continue her education and basketball career at Iowa Western.
'It's pretty cool,' Albertsen said. 'If you had asked freshman me if I was going to go play basketball in college, I probably would've laughed and said no. Looking back, I'm glad I decided to and I'm excited for the next three years.'
Albertsen said Iowa Western made her feel at home.
'The coaches are super nice, and I just feel like it's going to be the best fit for me,' she said.
Albertsen's coaches, Zach Klaassen, Mark Kohorst, and Sam Brummer, were all in attendance at the letter of intent signing.
'Her journey is much different than any other kid I've coached before,' Klaassen said. 'When she came in, she was figuring herself out a little bit. Just to watch the growth from freshman year to now is unbelievable. To come in and be a double-double person for us as a senior is crazy, and I'd be lying if I said I saw that coming.'
Klaassen talked about highlights from Albertsen's Cyclone career that stand out.
'Her breaking the rebound record is pretty awesome,' he said. 'I wish I could remember the game for sure, but when she hit the 3-pointer from up top and the crowd and the kids exploded and the gym got super loud was pretty awesome. Watching her rebound, the way she can tip the ball to herself is fun to watch and she's always smiling. She'll be greatly missed.'
Albertsen expressed gratitude towards her family for their help and guidance along the way.
'They definitely mean a lot to me,' she said. 'I'm a big family person. I just love all of them being here to support me. It's definitely been a lot of stress on my parents figuring out where I'm going to go and play, but they've been there by my side and helped me make this decision.'
With graduation right around the corner, Albertsen talked about what she'll remember most about being a Cyclone and some life lessons she'll take with her to college and beyond.
'Being a good person,' she added. 'That's what Harlan is all about. Being a good sport and having good sportsmanship. That's one big takeaway from Harlan.'

title: Vikings open season against Raiders at home
author: Alex Martin
description: After a struggle during their 2023 season in which the AHSTW Vikings boys soccer team finished 5-9, losing 3-1 in the 1A-8 First Round Tournament Game to St. Albert, the Vikings are back to work set to open their season March 25 at home. They were led by Sophomore Kayden Baxter with 13 goals, Senior Braydon Lund with seven assists, and Senior Jaicob Madsen with 94 saves. Other scorers on the team included Lund with eight goals and Sophomore Ethan Holtz with six goals.
content:
After a struggle during their 2023 season in which the AHSTW Vikings boys soccer team finished 5-9, losing 3-1 in the 1A-8 First Round Tournament Game to St. Albert, the Vikings are back to work set to open their season March 25 at home.
'The boys and I are super excited for this season,' said Viking Head Coach Michael Mertz. 'It's my favorite sport to watch and play, and I know there are guys on the team that feel the same way. Overall it's a great feeling to be able to step back onto the pitch and get things rolling.'
Last season, some of the Vikings wins came against Grand View Christian, Logan-Magnolia, Riverside, Atlantic, and Council Bluffs Jefferson. They were led by Sophomore Kayden Baxter with 13 goals, Senior Braydon Lund with seven assists, and Senior Jaicob Madsen with 94 saves.
Other scorers on the team included Lund with eight goals and Sophomore Ethan Holtz with six goals. Lund, Madsen, Cole Scheffler, Jacob Coon, Aidan Martin, and Ethen Gubbels have all graduated. Mertz is looking to some returners, mostly seniors, to step up and lead the way.
'This year our team captains are Sawyer Kiesel, Kaeden Rold, and Bryan Mertz,' Mertz said. 'I will rely on all three of them to help foster positive attitudes, work ethic, and soccer skills for our younger and newer members of the team. We also have two of our top scorers from last season back with us; Kayden Baxter and Ethan Holtz will look to lead our offense and create opportunities for the rest of the squad.'
Mertz is new to the team, taking over for James Johnson who stepped down from the head coach role at the end of last season.
'The original goal was to take over as head coach at the beginning of last year's season, but I ended up taking a volunteer position and learned as much as I could under Head Coach James Johnson and Assistant Coach Ryan Neilsen,' Mertz said. 'I'm grateful that they decided to come back for one last season and for showing me the ropes of coaching soccer. It will for sure be tough to fill the shoes both of them left, but I have a great support system and nothing but positive thoughts for the future of our program.'
Like any new coach, Mertz understands there will be some struggles along the way, but remains optimistic about the challenges ahead.
'The communication of expectations and getting the ideas from my head to come across properly to the team,' he said. 'Also as a first-year coach, it's sometimes tough to get your team to buy into the process and believe that you know how to help them succeed, but I know as the season goes on that connection and trust will only strengthen.'
The Vikings will welcome East Sac Country to town Monday night at 7 p.m. looking to start their season off with a home win. The Raiders finished last season with a 4-9 record and were led by Junior Luke Wright with 11 goals, Senior Elias Aragon with seven assists, and Junior Luke Wernimont with 222 saves.
'Doing the little things right. Plain and simple, we need to come out with energy and a positive mentality that we can win,' Mertz said. 'It was a tight game between us last year and that was even after having to play with only 10 players after a red card for a handball in the goal occurred close to the middle of the game. I imagine it will be a close affair again this season, but I expect it to be a good opener.'

title: Vikings get shut down by Wildcats at home
author: Alex Martin
description: Senior Wildcat Sara Titkova set the tone for her team Monday night on the road in Avoca, scoring the first two of three goals, including the first one less than two minutes into the game, handing the AHSTW Vikings girls soccer team their second loss of the season. Following Titkova's second goal, the Wildcat offense continued to stomp on the Viking defense when Junior Wildcat Emily Partlow added a goal approaching the 15-minute mark in the first half. The Vikings were finally able to capitalize on a scoring opportunity when Sophomore Halle Goodman scored the first goal for her team approaching the 2-minute mark, still trailing 6-1.
content:
Senior Wildcat Sara Titkova set the tone for her team Monday night on the road in Avoca, scoring the first two of three goals, including the first one less than two minutes into the game, handing the AHSTW Vikings girls soccer team their second loss of the season.
'I'm very confident we will get things turned around,' said Viking Head Coach Beth Herbst. 'We have never been successful on a Monday game after a 3-day weekend. We will be working harder than ever this week to make sure we don't make the same mistakes next Monday when we take on Van Meter.'
Following Titkova's second goal, the Wildcat offense continued to stomp on the Viking defense when Junior Wildcat Emily Partlow added a goal approaching the 15-minute mark in the first half.
The Vikings were finally able to capitalize on a scoring opportunity when Sophomore Halle Goodman scored the first goal for her team approaching the 2-minute mark, still trailing 6-1.
'Halle Goodman is a great soccer player,' Herbst said. 'We rely on her a lot to hit the back of the net. I always like seeing her score. She has a beautiful foot on her.'
The Wildcats took a 5-point lead into halftime, Herbst and the coaching staff kept the positivity level up, knowing the Vikings could turn the table on the Wildcats in the second half.
'It's up to the girls to perform,' she said. 'I can only do so much at halftime. They hung their heads hard at halftime. That is to be expected after their performance. They knew they weren't performing. Sometimes saying nothing is better than saying anything.'
When the second half began, Titkova continued her dominant night, scoring two goals with the first 15 minutes, followed by another two goals later in the half, which put the Wildcats up 11-1, ending the game via mercy rule.
The Vikings fall to 0-2 on the season and won't return to action until April 8, which will be the start of a 3-game week on the road against the Van Meter Bulldogs, who went 12-4 during their 2023 campaign. They were led by Junior Eden Moore with 36 goals, Senior Mary Kelly with 14 assists, and Junior goalkeeper Regan Bernhardt with 58 saves.
This season, they are 1-1 with their first win of the season coming against Central Iowa United, following by a loss to Des Moines Christian. Moore leads the team with six goals, and Junior Katie Vaught has two assists.
'We are going to have to work very hard this week,' Herbst said. 'We are going to have to condition more than ever this week. Van Meter is a tough team to beat. It all depends on what Lady Vikes team shows up.'

title: Vikings boys soccer drops game in second half
author: Alex Martin
description: With the AHSTW Vikings boys soccer team trailing 1-0 at the half, courtesy of a goal from West Central Valley Senior Kamron Kunkle, it looked like the Vikings were going to turn the tables on the Wildcats in the second half and score, but unfortunately couldn't as the Wildcats scored six more goals, cruising to a 7-0 victory, handing the Vikings their second loss. 'We were playing a good first half,' said Viking Head Coach Michael Mertz. The Wildcats added one more goal, which would be their final goal of the night, handing the Vikings their second shutout loss, falling to 0-2 on the season.
content:
With the AHSTW Vikings boys soccer team trailing 1-0 at the half, courtesy of a goal from West Central Valley Senior Kamron Kunkle, it looked like the Vikings were going to turn the tables on the Wildcats in the second half and score, but unfortunately couldn't as the Wildcats scored six more goals, cruising to a 7-0 victory, handing the Vikings their second loss.
'We were playing a good first half,' said Viking Head Coach Michael Mertz. 'We were sticking with a really good team that has a lot more numbers than we do, and they are able to sub in fresh players a lot more often. I told them to just keep their heads up and keep doing what we do in practice.'
Both teams came out of the gate playing great defensively including Junior Viking goalkeeper Aiden Akers, who came away with 33 saves on the night.
'Aiden, surprisingly has never played goalie before,' Mertz said. 'This is his first year in soccer since he was a little kid, so we kind of just threw him in there and he's really stepped up and become a leader back there for our defense and he just gets at it.'
When the second half began, it didn't take long for the Wildcats to score their second goal less than four minutes in from Senior Braylen Taylor. The Viking defense kept the game at 2-0 for a while, until the Wilcat offense came alive and erupted for four goals in 10 minutes with another two from Kunkle.
The Wildcats added one more goal, which would be their final goal of the night, handing the Vikings their second shutout loss, falling to 0-2 on the season.
The Vikings won't return to action until April 8, which will be the start of a 3-game week on the road against the Van Meter Bulldogs, who went 8-10 during their 2023 season. They were led by Sophomore Caleb Moore with nine goals, Freshman Henry Lounsbury with five assists, and Senior goalkeeper Ashtian Watson with 52 saves.
This season, the Bulldogs are 1-0 with their first win coming against the Des Moines Christian Lions.
'We have some little things to work on,' Mertz added. 'Our fundamentals, the passing, the spacing, and our offense is needing a little more work just for our formation.'

title: Cyclones fall to Saintes on Klusman's big night
author: Alex Martin
description: Less than 10 minutes into Tuesday's home game at Merrill Field, Senior Saint Ella Klusman scored her first goal of the game, giving St. Albert an early 1-0 lead, which would be all they would need en route to a 4-0 victory over the HCHS Cyclones. Klusman knocked in another goal five minutes later, along with a goal just before the first half concluded, putting her team up by four points. When the second half began, neither team scored a goal, but Boysen was proud of his defense for preventing more goals from St. Albert.
content:
Less than 10 minutes into Tuesday's home game at Merrill Field, Senior Saint Ella Klusman scored her first goal of the game, giving St. Albert an early 1-0 lead, which would be all they would need en route to a 4-0 victory over the HCHS Cyclones.
'She's a great player,' said Cyclone Head Coach Jared Boysen. 'I've always said that since she's been a freshman. Trying to stop her, we've done a lot of different things.'
Klusman knocked in another goal five minutes later, along with a goal just before the first half concluded, putting her team up by four points. Despite an uphill battle the Cyclones would be facing in the second half, Boysen told the girls to remain positive at halftime.
'Just keep your heads up,' he said. 'The wind was a huge advantage, and then it switched and I think it died down a little bit compared to what the first half was.'
When the second half began, neither team scored a goal, but Boysen was proud of his defense for preventing more goals from St. Albert.
'We were still playing well and clearing the ball,' he added. 'Lily [Schechinger] does a great job in the back there. We tried to keep her on Ella as much as we could.'
Towards the back end of the second half, there were a few moments where the Cyclone offense had opportunities to score late in the game, but unfortunately came up empty.
'We had a few open looks going forward there at the end,' Boysen said. 'Hailey [Good] had a couple of opportunities and if it would've went the other way, she could have scored and kept it in.'
St. Albert hung on for the win, their first of the season, and handed the Cyclones their second loss. The Cyclones move to 1-2 on the season and will return to action Monday at home at 5 p.m. against the 0-1 Kuemper Catholic Knights, who lost their season opener 2-0 to Lewis Central.
During their 2023 season, the Knights finished 12-7 and were led by Senior Catherine Mayhall with 25 goals, Junior Lauren Boell with 11 assists, and Freshman goalkeeper Brianna Wittrock with 152 saves.
'Hopefully we can rest up this week and watch a little more film on this one and fix a few of those things,' Boysen said. 'Kuemper was one last year that got us and we thought we should have won that one. Hopefully we can be a little more prepared for that one on Monday.'

title: County in good financial position according to audit report
author: Renée Brich
description: SHELBY COUNTY — Shelby County is in a good financial position according to an audit report for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2023. 'It demonstrated that our department heads lived within their tight budgets and are providing quality services at a cost to the tax payer below our county's state ranking.' Revenues of the county's governmental activities increased 3.0%, , or approximately $488,000 from the fiscal year 2022 to 2023, according to the report. Program expenses of the County's governmental activities increased 11 .5%, or approximately $1,751,000, more in Fiscal 2023 than in Fiscal 2022.
content:
SHELBY COUNTY — Shelby County is in a good financial position according to an audit report for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2023.
Chris Nelson, president of Gronewold, Bell, Khynn & Co., PC of Atlantic presented the report to the Shelby County Board of Supervisors April 2.
'There was nothing new or unusual,' Nelson said. 'There are no red flags at all.'
Steve Kenkel, Chairman of the Shelby County Board of Supervisors said he was pleased with the results.
'The audit presented a very healthy financial picture of our county,' Kenkel said. 'It demonstrated that our department heads lived within their tight budgets and are providing quality services at a cost to the tax payer below our county's state ranking.'
Revenues of the county's governmental activities increased 3.0%, , or approximately $488,000 from the fiscal year 2022 to 2023, according to the report. Property and other county taxes and local option sales tax increased approximately $510,000. Operating grants and contributions decreased approximately $445,000, and capital grants and contributions increased by approximately $335,00.
Program expenses of the County's governmental activities increased 11 .5%, or approximately $1,751,000, more in Fiscal 2023 than in Fiscal 2022. to June 30, 2023.
As Shelby County completed the year, its governmental funds reported a combined fund balance of $5.42 million, a decrease of approximately $1,891,000 from last year's total of $7.31 million. The following are the reasons for the changes in fund balances of the major funds from the prior year:

The Secondary Roads Fund ended Fiscal Year 2023 with a fund balance of $3,117,267, down $445,396 when compared to the ending balance for Fiscal Year 2022.
