title: Cyclones boys tennis falls 9-0 to Knights
author: Alex Martin
description: 'Kuemper is a great team this year and showed it yesterday,' said Cyclone Head Coach Dillon Stane. During his singles match, despite losing 8-0 to the Knights' Mason Reicks, Stane was proud of how one of his Cyclone Juniors battled against him, along with another Junior who lost 8-0 to the Knights' Hans Kraus. Other highlights included Cyclone Junior Abram Wilwerding going against Josh Langel, Cyclone Junior Thomas Kurtz battling with Max Reincke, Cyclone Sophomore Teagon Bissen matching up with Jake Hausman, and Freshman Cyclone Dale Scheuring going against Braxton Lu.
content:
Monday, the HCHS boys tennis team fell to 0-6 on the season after a hard fought battle with the Kuemper Catholic Knights who won in dominant fashion 9-0.
'Kuemper is a great team this year and showed it yesterday,' said Cyclone Head Coach Dillon Stane. 'I was extremely proud of how our kids kept their heads up and went down swinging until the final point. Our kids are doing a better job keeping the ball in play, and are beating themselves less and less every meet.'
During his singles match, despite losing 8-0 to the Knights' Mason Reicks, Stane was proud of how one of his Cyclone Juniors battled against him, along with another Junior who lost 8-0 to the Knights' Hans Kraus.
'Colton Hagle had as good of a night as could be expected going against a state tournament quality player,' he said. 'He is getting more consistent and is continuing to grow as a leading player on the team. Jeb Sonderman also played an aggressive match and is learning to get to the night when the match calls for it.'
Other highlights included Cyclone Junior Abram Wilwerding going against Josh Langel, Cyclone Junior Thomas Kurtz battling with Max Reincke, Cyclone Sophomore Teagon Bissen matching up with Jake Hausman, and Freshman Cyclone Dale Scheuring going against Braxton Lu. All Cyclones lost 8-0, but Stane credited Kuemper Catholic for the roster they have.
'Pick any kid on the roster and it is a perfect example of what makes them a solid opponent,' he added. 'They could interchange their 4-6 and it would not affect the final results.'
One Cyclone who was missing from the match was Freshman Caden Herbst, and with Herbst out, Scheuring stepped up in his place filling in the final varsity spot.
'Dale stepped up last week against Audubon and got a win last week, which was amazing to see,' Stane said. 'Then for him to get back into the line up last night against a quality opponent was what we like to see from him.'
The Cyclones were originally supposed to take on the 4-0 Glenwood Rams Tuesday at home at 4:30 p.m., but due to inclement weather conditions, their next match will be back at home Thursday at 4:30 p.m. against the 5-0 Shenandoah Mustangs. The Mustangs are led by Andrew Lawrence, Lucas Sun, Seth Zwickel, Teagan Brunk, and Luke Daoust with five match wins, along with Ryan Lawrence with three match wins, and Drew Morelock with one.

title: Wolves run strong at Ace Nelson Relays
author: Alex Martin
description: Monday in Denison, the IKM-Manning Wolves girls track and field team earned themselves a 5 th place finish with 64 points, 77.5 points behind the winner, Cherokee Washington. Garrison also helped the 4x800 relay team, which also featured Addisyn Bandow, Taylor Beckendorf, and Karlee Arp, to a second place finish with a time of 11:25.04, finishing behind Cherokee Washington who won the event with 10:48.55. Other Wolves highlights on the track included Caylie Rasmussen finishing second in the 100m dash with 13.38, finishing behind Morgan Hast of Boyer Valley, and 6 th in the 200m dash with 28.63.
content:
IKM-Manning Girls
Monday in Denison, the IKM-Manning Wolves girls track and field team earned themselves a 5 th place finish with 64 points, 77.5 points behind the winner, Cherokee Washington.
'Overall, the girls placed 5 th, which we thought was pretty good for missing 7 runners due to an FFA conflict,' said Wolves Head Coach Emma Konkler-Petersen.
Wolves Junior Raegan Garrison shined in the 3000 meter run, winning the event with a time of 12:03.93, edging out Grace Woodall of Cherokee Washington, who finished with 12:30.16. Garrison also helped the 4x800 relay team, which also featured Addisyn Bandow, Taylor Beckendorf, and Karlee Arp, to a second place finish with a time of 11:25.04, finishing behind Cherokee Washington who won the event with 10:48.55.
'Raegan Garrison had a really good night and took home the meet champion in the 3000 and ran a great leg of the 2nd place, finishing 4x800 relay that followed shortly after the 3000,' Konkler-Petersen said.
Other Wolves highlights on the track included Caylie Rasmussen finishing second in the 100m dash with 13.38, finishing behind Morgan Hast of Boyer Valley, and 6 th in the 200m dash with 28.63. The 200m dash was won by Laney Wolfswinkel of Cherokee Washington.
'Caylie Rasmussen placed 2nd in the 100 with a new personal best for her,' Konkler-Petersen added.
Konkler-Petersen was pleased with how relay races turned out, which resulted in some top five finishes. The 4x200 team which featured Audrey Menough, Abby Wanser, Hannah McKinney, and Arp took a 4 th place finish with a time of 2:02.57, finishing just 12+ seconds behind Lawton-Bronson who won the event with 1:49.74.
The 4x400 team which had Arp, Rasmussen, Addisyn Bandow, and Katelyn Bandow also finished 4 th with a time of 4:40.20, just 14+ seconds behind Cherokee Washington, who won the event with 4:25.58.
'We had many relays place in the top 5, which made us very happy, since we were running against some really good 2A and 3A schools,' she said. 'It was nice to have them to help pace us in different relays and put up some good times.'
In field events, Arp took a 7 th place finish in long jump with a jump of 13-03.00, just 3.5 feet behind Irelynne McNamara who won the event with 16-03.50. Beckendorf took a 7 th place finish in high jump with 4-06.00, not far behind Trista Ohlmeier from MVAOCOU who won the event with 5-00.00.
The Wolves next event will be at OABCIG High School Thursday at 4:30 p.m. where they will be one of nine schools competing.
'We will hopefully have all of our runners back at this time and will be excited to see what our relays and individuals can continue to do,' Konkler-Petersen said.
IKM-Manning Boys
With many schools in both Class 2A and 3A, the IKM-Manning Wolves boys track and field team still managed to earn a fourth place finish 85 points, 58 points behind Cherokee Washington, who won the event with 143.
'I thought we had a decent night overall,' said Wolves Head Coach Kyle Vanderhorst. 'The wind was very tough and I thought we battled through that. We also had some guys that were out because of injury, and then also battled injuries once the meet got going, so it became a challenge filling out all the events.'
Despite injuries, multiple Wolves stepped up and delivered including Davis Rasmussen, who ran a strong time in the 100m dash with 11.56 for a 6 th place finish, half a second behind Karson Elwood of Treynor who won with 11.06.
'Davis is one of the hardest workers we've got, and he keeps getting better and better as the season goes forward,' Vanderhorst said. 'I think he is going to finish very well in the last month of the season.'
In the longer distance events, Lane Sams took home some high finishes, taking third in the 800 meter run 2:09.69, just a little over a second behind the winner, Logan Stowater of Cherokee Washington, who won with 2:08.45.
Sams also got second place in the 1600 with a time of 5:13.27, almost a second a half behind Brennan Boden of Tri-Center, who won with 5:11.60.
'Lane is one of our senior leaders and I have been really proud this year with his ability to try a combination of events,' Vanderhorst added. 'He knew that his 1600 time was not going to be the best tonight with the 800 so close to the 1600, but he competed well in the event and came away with a second place finish. Lane's best attribute is his willingness to compete at all times, even when he may be tired.'
Vanderhorst was pleased with the results in relay races, including the 4x800 that won with Sams, Abe Polzien, Ben Ramsey, and Isaac Blankman with a time of 8:49.39, beating out Tri-Center, who came in second place with 9:02.55.
The 4x400 team which included Polzien, Kusel, Lueth, and Blankman, finished third with a time of 3:42.22 behind Lawton-Bronson who won the event with 3:39.01. The 4x200 team which featured Jase Lueth, Rasmussen, Polzien, and Ross Kusel finished second with a time of 1:35.94, right behind Lawton-Bronson who won with 1:34.34.
'Our 4x8 has been a staple for us the past six years and the guys that have ran it so far this year have taken pride in that event,' he said. 'We know there are some great teams around the area in that event and look forward to competing with them as the season progresses. We have to get healthy first and foremost as we get closer to the Conference and State Qualifying Meet, and then we can lock in our lineups that we will use for those meets.'
In field events, Kusel finished in second place in high jump with a jump of 6-00.00, right behind Jon Jenness of Cherokee Washington who jumped 6-02.00.
The Wolves next event will be at OABCIG High School Thursday at 4:30 p.m. where they will be one of nine schools competing.
'The OABCIG Meet is always a good one because we get to compete with some teams that are up in Northern Iowa,' Vanderhorst said. 'We know teams like Lawton Bronson, OABCIG, and Ridge View will be a challenge and look forward to competing against all the teams there.'

title: Myrtue Medical Center named among Top 20 Critical Access Hospitals in the nation
description: HARLAN— Myrtue Medical Center has been recognized as one of the 20 highest-ranked Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs) in the country by National Rural Health Association (NRNA). This recognition underscores the service every team member has provided to our community over the last seven decades,' said Barry Jacobsen, CEO of Myrtue Medical Center. 'It is an acknowledgment of the medical center's vital role in ensuring the health and wellness of the community we serve.' As Myrtue Medical Center continues to build on this foundation of excellence, it remains focused on enhancing its services for the future health needs of generations to come.
content:
HARLAN— Myrtue Medical Center has been recognized as one of the 20 highest-ranked Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs) in the country by National Rural Health Association (NRNA). This distinction places Myrtue in the top 1 percent of more than 1,300 critical access hospitals in the nation in the categories of quality, patient perspective, finance and market share.
'We are celebrating a significant milestone of 70 years of service to our community. This recognition underscores the service every team member has provided to our community over the last seven decades,' said Barry Jacobsen, CEO of Myrtue Medical Center. 'It is an acknowledgment of the medical center's vital role in ensuring the health and wellness of the community we serve.'
As Myrtue Medical Center continues to build on this foundation of excellence, it remains focused on enhancing its services for the future health needs of generations to come.

title: Cyclones edged out by four strokes in triangular
author: Alex Martin
description: The HCHS Cyclones girls golf team competed in a triangular Monday at the Harlan Golf & Country Club, finishing with 206 strokes, four behind Red Oak, who won the event with 202, and 10 ahead of Shenandoah who came in third place with 216. Cyclone Senior Kara Kenkel finished in first among Cyclone golfers with 48 strokes, and second overall, two strokes behind Red Oak Junior Brynn Knaus, who won the event with 46. Other Cyclone highlights included Junior Macy Mueller finishing second among Cyclone golfers with 49 strokes, finishing fourth overall.
content:
The HCHS Cyclones girls golf team competed in a triangular Monday at the Harlan Golf & Country Club, finishing with 206 strokes, four behind Red Oak, who won the event with 202, and 10 ahead of Shenandoah who came in third place with 216.
'At home, the goal is to win,' said Cyclone Head Coach Todd Bladt. 'But we're always look for improvements, and we definitely saw that in a couple of different places.'
Cyclone Senior Kara Kenkel finished in first among Cyclone golfers with 48 strokes, and second overall, two strokes behind Red Oak Junior Brynn Knaus, who won the event with 46.
'Kara Kenkel, that's the first time she's medaled at home in her career,' Bladt said. 'Kara played her game, playing the fairway, managing the course, she did that very well.
Other Cyclone highlights included Junior Macy Mueller finishing second among Cyclone golfers with 49 strokes, finishing fourth overall. Senior Ella Freund finished with 50 strokes, Freshman Ava Langenfeld with 59, and Senior Regan Martin with 73.
'Ava Langenfeld, shot under 60 for her first time this year on a difficult course,' Bladt added. 'It's very long compared to a lot of the other courses we play.'
The last time the Cyclones played at the Harlan Golf & Country Club, they shot 243 as a team against Lewis Central. Bladt commented on the improvements they've made since that opening meet.
'To go from 243 to now down at 206 on a difficult course, that shows a lot of improvement,' he said. 'That's what we're looking for. We had a couple of girls that maybe didn't shoot their best ever, but they're not far off. Just a few strokes here and there. We're going in the right direction, and we want to keep lowering those scores.'
The Cyclones return to the course Thursday at home at 3:30 p.m. against the 1-13 Clarinda Cardinals. The Cardinals are led by Taylor Rasmussen with 47 strokes on a 9-hole course, and Paige McCoy with 119 strokes on an 18-hole course.
'We've got to eliminate some putts,' Bladt said. 'We'd love to 2-putt every green. It's not easy to 2-putt everything, but that is the goal. If on our second shots be near the green and if we're on the green, that's a bonus. Then on that third shot, if we can get maybe five feet closer, we'll have a much better chance of getting out of there with a par or bogey. It's just about managing the course.'

title: Wolves & Spartans compete at Bob Clark Relays
author: Alex Martin
description: Tuesday night, the IKM-Manning Wolves girls track and field team finished strong at the Bob Clark Relays taking fourth place with 89 points, finishing 25 points behind the winner Tri-Center. Another event that included a personal record was the 4x800 relay team which featured Taylor Beckendorf, Alikxa McGinn, Addisyn Bandow, and Garrison winning the event with 10:55.59, beating out ACGC who came in second place with a time of 11:16.46. The shuttle hurdle relay team took second place with 1:13.46 featuring Grace Carroll, Abby Wanser, Anna Stangl, and Abby Neilheisel finishing right on the tails of Tri-Center who beat them by less than a second with 1:13.21.
content:
IKM-Manning Girls
Tuesday night, the IKM-Manning Wolves girls track and field team finished strong at the Bob Clark Relays taking fourth place with 89 points, finishing 25 points behind the winner Tri-Center.
Junior Raegan Garrison set the tone with a strong performance in the 3000 run, taking second place with 11:36.09, just 6.06 seconds behind Kylie Rochholz of Panorama who won the event with 11:30.03. Despite coming in second, Garrison still set a new personal record.
'The girls started the meet with Raegan Garrison placing 2nd in the 3000 with a huge PR for her,' said Wolves Head Coach Emma Konkler-Petersen. 'This gave us a lot of momentum going forward the rest of the meet.'
Another event that included a personal record was the 4x800 relay team which featured Taylor Beckendorf, Alikxa McGinn, Addisyn Bandow, and Garrison winning the event with 10:55.59, beating out ACGC who came in second place with a time of 11:16.46.
The shuttle hurdle relay team took second place with 1:13.46 featuring Grace Carroll, Abby Wanser, Anna Stangl, and Abby Neilheisel finishing right on the tails of Tri-Center who beat them by less than a second with 1:13.21.
The distance medley team had Carroll, Laynie Gawley, Bandow, and Oriah Meiners finishing second as well, with a time of 4:45.89, 4+ seconds behind Audubon who won the event with 4:41.49.
'The 4x800 went on to take 1st in the meet followed by the shuttle hurdle relay taking 2nd with a huge PR for that group as well,' Konkler-Petersen said. 'They are a group that is continuing to progress well as the season has gone on. The distance medley ran a good race placing 2nd with Audubon just ahead of them to push them.'
Towards the end of the night, the 4x200 team earned a first place finish with a personal record of 1:54.04, won by Beckendorf, Caylie Rasmussen, Meiners, and Carroll, beating out Tri-Center who came in second place with a time of 1:55.68.
The Wolves next event will be Thursday at 4:30 p.m. at ACGC High School where they will be one of eight schools competing.
IKM-Manning Boys
The IKM-Manning Wolves boys track and field team took a fourth place finish Tuesday at the Bob Clark Relays in Audubon with 77 points, 40 behind AGCG who won the event with 117.
'I thought we competed very well,' said Wolves Head Coach Kyle Vanderhorst. 'We set a lot of personal bests as individuals and ran multiple season bests in our relays. It was a great meet that had a bunch of great competition.'
In the 200m dash event, Ross Kusel and Jase Lueth took fourth and fifth place finishes with times of 23.79 and 23.82, finishing less than a second behind Exira-EHK Senior Cash Emgarten, who won the event with 23.07.
'Both of those guys have been two of our top scorers all season long and ran really well in a race that was full of great sprinters,' Vanderhorst said.
During relays, the Wolves took some high finishes including first place in the 4x800 featuring Lane Sams, Ben Ramsey, Abe Polzien, and Isaac Blankman with a time of 8:39.82, beating out Clarinda who came in second place with 8:58.47.
In the distance medley, the Wolves finished third with Lueth, Kusel, Polzien, and Sams with 3:47.89, just 2.04 seconds behind the winner, Tri-Center. The 4x200 team finished second with 1:35.73 that had Lueth, Polzien, Kusel, and Davis Rasmussen, just 2.11 seconds behind ACGC who won the event.
In the 4x100, IKM-Manning had another strong finish with Lueth, Max Butler, Polzien, and Rasmussen taking fourth place with a time of 46.36, just 1+ second behind ACGC who won the event.
'Our relays ran well. Our 4x8 cut off five seconds and has been a strong unit for us all season long,' Vanderhorst added. 'Our Distance Medley was able to shave off three seconds and our 4x2 also ran a season best. It is good to see the progress in those events with the conference meet and state qualifying meet right around the corner. We need to keep working on handoff execution and stay healthy as we head into the stretch run of the season.'
The Wolves will return to action at the ACGC Invitational Thursday at 4:30 p.m. going up against eight other schools.
'It is a great meet for us because AC/GC allows multiple entries in most events,' Vanderhorst said. 'It allows us to see some final combinations before the conference meet as well as getting our younger athletes more opportunities to race/throw/jump against athletes from other schools. AC/GC, Audubon, and Panorama will have great teams there and we hope to compete to the best of our abilities on Thursday evening.'
Exira-EHK
Thursday night at Audubon, the Exira-EHK Spartans boys track and field team finished 10 th with 42 points. Spartan head coach Kevin Brown was pleased with what he saw specifically from a few events, including some personal records.
'I enjoyed seeing our sprint medley and 4x100 hit season bests last night,' he said. 'Austin Rasmussen had a personal best in the mile, and is only a few seconds from breaking five minutes. Anthony Young also had a personal best in the discus. Coach Tony [Santisteban] has spent a lot of time with our throwers this season and it's showing.'
Senior Spartan Cash Emgarten continues to run strong in the 100 and 200m dash finishing with times of 11.02 and 23.07.
'Cash looked better out of the blocks in his 100 and 200 in Audubon,' Brown said. 'He is putting in the extra work in the weight room and on the track to see his times improve throughout the season. The expectation is that he is on the starting line for the finals in both events at state.'
Other Spartan highlights included the 800 sprint medley team which featured Alex Hansen, Bryce Brabham, Jonas LaCanne, and Emgarten finishing fourth with a time of 1:42.17, 3+ seconds behind Panorama who won the event with 1:38.96.
The 4x200 team which featured Levi Jessen, Ben Baggett, John Ty, and Owen Juhl finished with a time of 1:56.29. The event was won by ACGC with a time of 1:33.62. The 4x100 team that featured Emgarten, Brabham, LaCanne, and Hansen finished sixth with 47.64, just a few seconds behind ACGC, who won with 44.70.
'Blocks, hand offs, and running mentally strong are three things we need to continue to work on as the season progresses,' Brown added.
LaCanne also competed in 110 hurdles taking ninth overall with a time of 16.85, but only finishing 1+ second behind Peyton Cook of Griswold who won the event. He also got fourth place in 400 hurdles with a time of 1:00.17, finishing 4+ seconds behind Jack Follmann of CAM with 55.75.
The Spartans next event will be Thursday at 4:30 p.m. at AGCG High School competing against eight other schools.
'We haven't had a Tuesday/Thursday meet all season,' Brown said. 'Our plan is to load up the guys and get some personal bests leading up to the conference meet. ACGC, Audubon, and IKM-Manning all have talented programs, so it should be some good competition.'

title: Cyclones prepare to build off state tournament run
author: Alex Martin
description: After opening their 2023 season 0-5, but still earning a trip to the state tournament after beating Lewis Central 9-6 in the 3A-8 Championship Game July 12, the HCHS Cyclones baseball team is ready to get back to work and build off their state tournament run. 'Like any spring, we've got guys involved in a bunch of different activities, so we haven't had too much time together as a unit, but as far as the work we've been putting in, we got started back in January and we've been chomping at the bits.' Leinen batted .370 with two home runs, 29 runs batted in, with 44 hits, and 31 runs scored.
content:
After opening their 2023 season 0-5, but still earning a trip to the state tournament after beating Lewis Central 9-6 in the 3A-8 Championship Game July 12, the HCHS Cyclones baseball team is ready to get back to work and build off their state tournament run.
'We're definitely ready to get going,' said Cyclone Head Coach Heath Stein. 'Like any spring, we've got guys involved in a bunch of different activities, so we haven't had too much time together as a unit, but as far as the work we've been putting in, we got started back in January and we've been chomping at the bits.'
The Cyclones lost two talented seniors from a year ago in Stephen Leinen and Cael Goshorn.
Leinen batted .370 with two home runs, 29 runs batted in, with 44 hits, and 31 runs scored. Leinen also led the Cyclones with six wins on the mound and 39 strikeouts in 46.2 innings pitched. Goshorn batted .293 with 26 runs batted in, along with 34 hits and 23 runs scored.
'Cael and Stephen were big parts of that team last year,' Stein said. 'They contributed to a lot of the success, but we have quite a few guys back. We have nine spots on the field and we've got a lot of guys on the mound that are back and some newcomers that are going to push for some time.'
Two Cyclone Seniors who won't be with the team the entire season due to signing letters of intent to play football in college are Franz Reisz and Cade Sears.
During the 2023 season, Reisz went 2-3 on the mound with a 4.94 earned run average, along with 25 strikeouts in 28.1 innings pitched. Sears led the team in batting average with .402, while hitting four home runs with 34 runs batted in, along with 49 hits and scoring 48 runs.
'Two very valuable people,' Stein added. 'We're going to get all we can out of them and the plan for them to leave, I believe is around June 9 potentially, something might change, I hope it does. That's kind of the tentative plan. They'll be tough to replace. We'll enjoy having them as long as we can.'
Some of the Cyclones losses last season came against Sioux City North, LeMars, Sioux City East, ADM, Lewis Central, St. Albert, and others. Stein talked about some of the competition he expects to see this year whether it's Hawkeye-10 opponents or others.
'Sioux City North, LeMars, Dallas Center-Grimes, ADM, Bishop Heelan, all five of those teams out of the gate are very, very good,' he said. 'Lewis Central is going to be quality, Creston will be a good matchup for us, Kuemper Catholic is tough, and Carlisle and Sergeant Bluff-Luton are always good.'
The new season for the Cyclones gets underway on the road Monday at 5 p.m. starting with a doubleheader against Sioux City North. Last season, the Stars went 26-13. Offensively, they were led by Cael Walrod with 44 hits and Eli Cedillo with 35 runs batted in. On the mound, Steven Kling had seven wins with a 0.86 earned run average, while Ayden Schrunk led the team in strikeouts with 92.
'The keys to winning any high school baseball games are throwing strikes, limiting errors, and finding ways on base, and score runs,' Stein said. 'That's what we'll try to do. With starting pitchers, I don't know if I have them exactly slated yet. We'll probably going to have to use four or five guys early in the season on pitch counts.'

title: Pauley commits to Iowa Western for Dance
author: Alex Martin
description: AHSTW Senior Makenzie Pauley will be joining the dance team at Iowa Western CC following the conclusion of her high school days. 'You can tell they put in so much work and dedication to the team, and I'm ready to be a part of it. The love for dance started at an early age for Pauley courtesy of her mom enrolling her in a class.
content:
AHSTW Senior Makenzie Pauley will be joining the dance team at Iowa Western CC following the conclusion of her high school days.
'I'm pretty excited to be joining this team,' Pauley said. 'You can tell they put in so much work and dedication to the team, and I'm ready to be a part of it. I am also nervous as well. It's going to be a lot of work and I really have to push myself to do my best at the college level. I'm very grateful to have the opportunity to be on such a great team.'
The love for dance started at an early age for Pauley courtesy of her mom enrolling her in a class.
'I started dancing when I was around the age of four,' she said. 'My mom put me in dance and ever since It's always been in my life. When I was younger I would always love to watch the older girls dance and wanted to be just as good as them. One of them being my childhood babysitter. She would come over and help me with my dance moves and tricks. For the majority of my dance career I grew up in a small studio in Neola. I was there for 12 years, with also being on the competitive team for five years. Once I got into highschool I was on AHSTW varsity dance team all four years.'
Like most students, Pauley had options in front of her, and talked about what led her to choosing Iowa Western.
'Iowa Western Community College has a really great nursing program,' she added. 'I have some friends and family that already go there that are in IWCC nursing programs. When I went on a tour of the campus a couple weeks ago, I got a tour of the nursing part of the campus. I was shocked at how many scenarios can be played out and all of the hospital rooms set up for lab practicals. Once I entered my junior year of high school, I wanted to be a part of their dance team. They have won national championships with their routines. I want to keep dancing as long as I can before moving on to the next big part of my life. IWCC is also close to home, I can go back on weekends or breaks and won't have to worry about a long drive there and back.'
Pauley gave credit to her family for the support they've given her.
'My Family has always been a big supporter,' she said. 'It would be stressful and challenging to pick up new moves in a class with girls older than me. Being one the youngest in some classes I knew I would need to put work outside of the studio. My mom was with me throughout my competitive days and these long days get tiring but she was there and pushed me to be my best even when I was tired. My dad and brothers would come watch every dance recital I performed at even though they were hours long.'
With her high schools days nearing an end, Pauley has already a chance to meet the head dance coach for Iowa Western, Michaela Patterson, and is looking forward to learning from her/working with her.
'Meeting and talking to Michaela again was a great experience,' Pauley said. 'She talked through what being on the dance team would be like and how much work is needed to be put in. I am very excited to be able to have her as my college dance coach.'
Like any sport, athletes learn lessons along the way, and regardless of how her college dance career plays out, Pauley will take some of the lessons she learned dancing in high school to her college dance team.
'I always offer help and motivation if needed,' Pauley added. 'It may be challenging at first but the more you practice the better you will get. Also teamwork is another thing. Without teamwork there really can't be a team. In high school we always found time to bond with one another. Helping each other out with moves or counts.'

title: Cyclones win close 3-2 battle at home with Titans
author: Alex Martin
description: In the bottom of the sixth inning with the HCHS Cyclones baseball team leading 2-1, the Cyclones had runners on the corners and attempted a rare double steal, which allowed Cyclone Junior Landen Kaufman to come in to score, putting them ahead 3-1 at the time. In the bottom of the third inning starting with a single by Kaufman, a walk by Cade Sears, a sacrifice bunt by Matthew Sorfonden to force both runners into scoring position, Hayden Soma got the Cyclones on the board with a fielders choice to score Kaufman. The Cyclones would get another run when Quinn Koesters hit a routine fly ball into the outfield, but it was dropped by Freshman Titan Caden Nepple allowing Sears to score giving them a 2-0 lead.
content:
In the bottom of the sixth inning with the HCHS Cyclones baseball team leading 2-1, the Cyclones had runners on the corners and attempted a rare double steal, which allowed Cyclone Junior Landen Kaufman to come in to score, putting them ahead 3-1 at the time. The Titans would score one more run in the top of the 7th, but the Cyclone hung on for a 3-2 win.
'It's always fun to play Lewis Central,' said Cyclone Head Coach Heath Stein. 'I told the boys that was probably the ugliest 3-2 ballgame I've seen. The amount of free bases we gave them put us in tough spots, but how we responded in tough spots was good to see. Guys made plays and pitches when we had to to get us out of jams.'
In the bottom of the third inning starting with a single by Kaufman, a walk by Cade Sears, a sacrifice bunt by Matthew Sorfonden to force both runners into scoring position, Hayden Soma got the Cyclones on the board with a fielders choice to score Kaufman.
The Cyclones would get another run when Quinn Koesters hit a routine fly ball into the outfield, but it was dropped by Freshman Titan Caden Nepple allowing Sears to score giving them a 2-0 lead.
The Titans responded back right away in the top of the fourth inning cutting the lead in half at 2-1. The Cyclones couldn't responded in the bottom of the fourth coming up empty on the basepaths keeping the game at a one run lead.
In the top of the fifth inning, after getting just one out, Stein pulled starting pitcher Caleb Schleis from the game with 84 pitches, replacing him with Quinn Koesters out of the bullpen. Koesters allowed the bases to load up, but was able to get out of the inning when a line drive out was caught on the run by right fielder Sorfonden.
'That was good play,' Koesters said. 'You've got to trust your defense and he made a good play.'
In the bottom of the sixth inning, Kaufman gave the Cyclones an insurance run by scoring after a step off from the mound by Mullett, giving his team a 3-1 lead. The Titans returned to bat in the top of the seventh inning, getting an RBI single by Gaven Goldsberry to cut the lead to 3-2, but that would be the final run of the game as the Koesters punched out Brody Goeser to end the game jumping into Soma's arms and hugging each other.
'It's always fun to beat a rival,' Koesters added. 'You've got to celebrate when you do. Me and Soma said some things I can't repeat, but it was a fun win.'
The Cyclones earned their seventh win of the season moving their overall record to 3-2. They return to Jim Goeser Field Thursday at 5:30 p.m. to take on the 4-2 Denison Monarchs. Offensively, the Monarchs are led by Cole Kastner with eight hits, Cody Schulte with six runs batted in. On the mound, Camdyn Nemitz has two wins, while Schulte leads the team in strikeouts with 15.
'Another good opponent,' Stein said. 'We'll have Brock Lemrick on the mound to go at them.'
It will also be senior night as before the game Schleis, Sears, Sorfonden, Lemrick, Koesters, Franz Reisz, Braydon Ernst, Gavin Bruck, and Keegan Ring will be honored for their contributions to the program.
'It's a great group of guys, a big group of seniors,' Stein added. 'It's awesome that all these guys have stuck it out and worked as hard as they have through the years.'

title: Wolves struggle to get bats going in road loss
author: Alex Martin
description: In the bottom of the 4 th inning with an already sizeable lead, eighth grader Kaitlyn Evans launched a 2-run home run to put the Logan-Magnolia Panthers up 10-0, which gave the Panthers the victory via the mercy rule. The first two innings were quiet for both sides, but seemed promising offensively for the Wolves with Anna Stangl leading off the top of the first with a double and Karlee Arp starting the top of the second inning with a leadoff single, along with Emma Branning connecting at the plate for a leadoff double to open the third inning. 'We had base runners in multiple innings and multiple baserunners in a couple of innings.
content:
In the bottom of the 4 th inning with an already sizeable lead, eighth grader Kaitlyn Evans launched a 2-run home run to put the Logan-Magnolia Panthers up 10-0, which gave the Panthers the victory via the mercy rule. Sophomore Campbell Chase returned to the field in the top of the 5 th inning, not giving up any runs, securing the final three outs for the win.
'We've got to do a better job of defending the bunt, the slap bunt play,' said Wolves Head Coach Cory McCarville. 'That's what really got things rolling for Logan. The bottom of the order, girls got on. There's base runners and traffic for the top of the order, and that's what got us in trouble.'
The first two innings were quiet for both sides, but seemed promising offensively for the Wolves with Anna Stangl leading off the top of the first with a double and Karlee Arp starting the top of the second inning with a leadoff single, along with Emma Branning connecting at the plate for a leadoff double to open the third inning.
Even though none of these innings runs were scored, McCarville was pleased with the girls finding ways on base.
'I think offensively we are taking steps forward,' he said. 'We had base runners in multiple innings and multiple baserunners in a couple of innings. We've just got to do a better job of executing some bunts and executing a couple of situations and we're taking steps in the right direction.'
In the bottom of the third inning, the Panthers opened the inning with three consecutive singles to load the bases. Their first runs of the game came when a fielders choice occurred scoring eighth grader Teagan Carritt, followed by a sacrifice fly, which was later followed by a 2-run double from Evans to give the Panthers a 4-0 lead at the end of three innings.
When the bottom of the fourth inning began, the Panthers continued to swing hot bats and drive in runs dropping a 6-spot, putting themselves up 10-0. The inning finally came to an end when Arp was able to chase down a flyball in mid centerfield to end the inning.
'They're starting to track the ball a lot better,' McCarville said of his defense. 'They are starting to gauge what hitters are whether they be deep or shallow. They're doing a great job at communicating with one another, so I applaud their efforts so far.'
When they returned to the field in the top of the fifth inning, they just needed three outs to get the victory via the mercy rule, and were able to do so, even with the Wolves making some noise with some baserunners.
Campbell capped off the complete game victory giving her team their fifth win and handing the Wolves their seventh loss. The Wolves return to action Monday at 7 p.m. on the road against the 1-1 Treynor Cardinals. Offensively, the Cardinals are led by Delaney Mathews with four hits and Jadyn Huisman with three runs batted in. In pitching, Huisman has one wins, while Mathews leads the team with 16 strikouts in 13 2/3 innings pitched with a 2.56 earned run average.
'I think the biggest thing is we're going to have to execute a little more on offense and continue to develop with our defense on the infield,' McCarville said.

title: Wolves fall to Wheelers on the road
author: Alex Martin
description: Ella Richards got the ball for the Wolves, pitching six innings, striking out two Wheeler batters, but ran into some trouble in the second and fifth inning, giving up three runs in each of those innings. In the top of the first inning, Wolves Sophomore Anna Stangl got a leadoff double to open the game, got all the way to third base, but was unable to score. The Wolves offense had multiple players get on base via hits including Hannah McKinney, Keagan Eischeid, Olivia Linde, and two hits from Alikxa McGinn.
content:
The struggles continue for the IKM-Manning Wolves, dropping Tuesday's game to the Audubon Wheelers 8-0 for their fifth loss in a row.
Ella Richards got the ball for the Wolves, pitching six innings, striking out two Wheeler batters, but ran into some trouble in the second and fifth inning, giving up three runs in each of those innings.
'She did a nice job,' said Wolves Head Coach Cory McCarville of Richards. 'She had a couple of strikeouts and for the most part, she commanded her pitches and got a lot of popups and some groundouts and she did a nice job of mixing up pitches, locations, things like that.'
In the top of the first inning, Wolves Sophomore Anna Stangl got a leadoff double to open the game, got all the way to third base, but was unable to score. The Wolves offense had multiple players get on base via hits including Hannah McKinney, Keagan Eischeid, Olivia Linde, and two hits from Alikxa McGinn.
Even with the struggles at the plate across their lineup, McCarville is confident that those baserunners will eventually turn into some runs being scored.
'The whole idea is that we got some people on base, and we bunted a little bit to get people in scoring position,' he said. 'At times we had a couple of hard hit balls, they were just right at people. I told the girls over the course of the season, that'll balance itself out. I thought we did okay offensively. I know we didn't score, but we had some baserunners and some base hits.'
In the bottom of the fifth inning, the Wheelers dropped a 3-spot on the Wolves defense starting with an RBI single from Jordan Porsch to score Gemini Goodwin, followed by a 2-run single from Alexis Obermeier to put her team up 6-0 at the end of the inning. Wolves Sophomore Karlee Arp made a running catch in center field to get the final out of the inning.
'The outfield did a nice job,' McCarville said of his defense. 'The infield is coming along, and they're starting to trust themselves a little bit more all the time, and we're taking steps in the right direction.'
The Wheelers hung on for the victory as Obermeier went the distance securing the 8-0 victory for their eighth win of the season and handing the Wolves their ninth loss. The Wolves return to action Thursday on the road at 7:15 p.m. against a Western Iowa rival in the 3-5 AHSTW Vikings.
The Vikings offensively are led by Clara Pace with nine hits and Loralei Wahling with 10 runs batted in. In pitching, Etta Partlow has 21 strikeouts with a 2.66 earned run average.
'We're going to play hard,' McCarville said. 'I think the girls have had great spirits throughout, and we have great faith.'

title: Cyclones struggle in doubleheader with Rams
author: Alex Martin
description: In both games of a doubleheader Monday night at home, the later innings proved costly for the HCHS Cyclones baseball team, as they dropped game one 16-7 and game two 10-7. Schleis pitched 5 2/3 innings, striking out five Rams, but gave up 11 runs on six hits, while walking three batters and hitting three batters. Offensively, the Cyclones were able to produce runs, starting with a game tying RBI double in the bottom of the first inning off the bat of Brett Heese to score Quinn Koesters, followed by Colton Schneider with an RBI single to score Heese to give the Cyclones a 2-1 lead at the end of the first inning.
content:
In both games of a doubleheader Monday night at home, the later innings proved costly for the HCHS Cyclones baseball team, as they dropped game one 16-7 and game two 10-7.
'It's a long season with long weeks where we'll have to get deeper into our staff,' said Cyclone Head Coach Heath Stein. 'Up until this point in the season, our starting pitching has been so good that we haven't used a ton of guys.'
In game one, Cyclone Senior Caleb Schleis took the mound and was finding ways to record outs until the top of the fifth inning. The Rams offense busted the game wide open with a 4-spot, followed by another five runs in the top of the sixth that forced Stein to go to the bullpen, replacing Schleis with Owen Neve.
Schleis pitched 5 2/3 innings, striking out five Rams, but gave up 11 runs on six hits, while walking three batters and hitting three batters.
'He had a lot of free bases that kind of piled up,' Stein said. 'When you put guys on base in front of the two guys in their lineup that can hit, that's what happens.'
Offensively, the Cyclones were able to produce runs, starting with a game tying RBI double in the bottom of the first inning off the bat of Brett Heese to score Quinn Koesters, followed by Colton Schneider with an RBI single to score Heese to give the Cyclones a 2-1 lead at the end of the first inning.
Later in the bottom of the third inning with the Cyclones trailing by one once again, they were able to get their bats going and take the lead back with Cade Nelson connecting at the plate with a two out 2-run double to give his team a 4-3 lead.
Schneider knocked in another run in the bottom of the fourth inning to give the Cyclones a 2-run lead, but when the Rams returned to bat in the top of the fifth inning, Senior Ram Kayden Anderson launched a home run, his second of the night and from then on the Rams took control of the game.
'He's a good player,' Stein said of Anderson. 'If you put guys on in front of him, it makes it tough. They have a couple of guys in their lineup where you've got to execute pitches and if you miss, they might hurt you.'
The Cyclones were able to score a few more runs with their final run of game one coming on a bases loaded walk by Weston Reisz, but the Rams hung on for a dominant 16-7 win.
In game two, Koesters got the ball, and like Schleis in game one, Koesters was making dominant pitches going five innings, striking out seven batters, and only allowing three runs on four hits.
'Quinn has been in his bullpen role because our four starters have been throwing the ball very, very well,' Stein said. 'He's been on the back end, and we needed to have him start today. He did a good job. He executed really good pitches and had the curveball going pretty good. He just hung one to [Trent] Patton that got hit in the gap, and that's the three runs he gave up basically.'
Offensively, the Rams struck first in the top of the third inning when Patton hit a groundball for a fielders choice to knock in a run giving his team a 1-0 lead. In the bottom of the third inning, the Cyclones answered back with an RBI single from Heese to score Landen Kaufman tying the game at one run apiece.
The Rams got two runs in the top of the fifth to put themselves up 3-1, and the Cyclones once again responded dropping four runs in the bottom of the fifth to put themselves up 5-3 with a 2-run double from Hayden Soma, followed by another 2-run double by Schneider, who was thrown out at third base attempting to stretch a double into a triple.
In the sixth inning, the Rams busted the game open once again scoring six runs, followed by another run in the top of the seventh. The Cyclones added a few more runs, but lost 10-7 dropping both games of the doubleheader.
Their busy week continues with their next game Tuesday on the road 7:30 p.m. at Denison playing the 8-6 Monarchs. The Cyclones are hoping for redemption after dropping their game at home 5-4 May 30 in six innings due to game being called early with potential thunder in the area.
Offensively, the Monarchs are led by Jake Fink with 16 hits and Cole Kastner with nine runs batted. On the mound, Camdyn Nemitz has four wins, while Kastner leads the team in earned run average with 1.40, and Cody Schulte leads the team in strikeouts with 25.
'We're looking forward to it,' Stein said. 'It's another conference game. It'll be tough. They got us last time here in a game maybe they shouldn't have and we know that, so we'll go compete.'

title: Cyclones walk off in dramatic fashion, 4-3
author: Alex Martin
description: In the bottom of the seventh inning in a game where the HCHS Cyclones trailed 3-2 with one out, Junior Cyclone Brett Heese stepped to the plate and delivered a walk-off 2-run single to center field off of Sophomore Sioux City East Black Raider Quinton Ashcraft winning the game 4-3 as the Cyclones stormed the field to jump on the back of Heese for their 22 nd win of the season. Senior Cyclone Caleb Schleis took the mound to start the game for his team and ran into some early trouble when the Black Raiders leadoff hitter Jax Theeler launched an opposite field home run over the left field fence just three pitches into the game to give his team a 1-0 lead. The Cyclones tied the game at one in the bottom of the third when Senior Matthew Sorfonden connected at the plate for a home run down the left field line that went right over the foul pole.
content:
In the bottom of the seventh inning in a game where the HCHS Cyclones trailed 3-2 with one out, Junior Cyclone Brett Heese stepped to the plate and delivered a walk-off 2-run single to center field off of Sophomore Sioux City East Black Raider Quinton Ashcraft winning the game 4-3 as the Cyclones stormed the field to jump on the back of Heese for their 22 nd win of the season.
'It felt good,' Heese said. 'I struggled at the plate and I was a little passive early on in the game, but shook that off. He [Ashcraft] threw a fastball and I just crushed it right up the middle.'
Senior Cyclone Caleb Schleis took the mound to start the game for his team and ran into some early trouble when the Black Raiders leadoff hitter Jax Theeler launched an opposite field home run over the left field fence just three pitches into the game to give his team a 1-0 lead.
Schleis had to battle in the top of the second and third inning throwing a lot of pitches as he had 59 after three innings, but kept his team in the game as they were still trailing 1-0 heading into the bottom of the third.
'He gave up that leadoff home run,' said Cyclone Head Coach Heath Stein of Schleis. 'They have a great hitting team, so he had to make quality pitches throughout to keep us right there in the ball game, even though we weren't putting up a lot of runs.'
The Cyclones tied the game at one in the bottom of the third when Senior Matthew Sorfonden connected at the plate for a home run down the left field line that went right over the foul pole.
'Sorfonden put a good swing on that ball,' Stein said. 'I'm glad it stayed fair and we hit a couple of balls hard that could have turned into some runs. Overall good at bats.'
Following Sorfonden's home run, it didn't take the Black Raider offense long to get their lead back when in the top of the fourth, Freshman Christopher Ford had a 1-out RBI single putting his team ahead 2-1.
In the top of the fifth inning, Schleis was back on the mound and allowed the first two Black Raiders hitters to reach base, but Stein removed him for Senior Brock Lemrick. Sophomore Black Raider Logan Cherkas connected for a base hit off Lemrick, but that run was charged to Schleis as the Raiders extended their lead to 3-1. Following Cherkas' hit, Lemrick picked off Theeler at second back and struck out Freshman Kason Clayborne to get his team back in the dugout down by two.
'Lemrick was kind of a bullpen guy last year, so he's kind of used to that role,' Stein said. 'He came in and executed pitch after pitch.'
In the bottom of the fifth inning, Freshman Colton Schneider got his team one of those back when he hit an RBI single scoring eighth grader Foxx Argotsinger, putting his team down 3-2.
When Lemrick returned to the mound in the top of the sixth inning, he shut down the Black Raider offense needing just 13 pitches to retire the side.
'Lemrick, he likes to get loud on the mound, but gets us cooking, plays hard, and is fun to be around,' Heese said.
Lemrick came back out for the top of the seventh and threw just ten pitches to keep his team within striking distance going into the bottom of the seventh inning.
When the bottom half of the inning began, Argotsinger drew a leadoff walk, following by Sorfonden getting hit by a pitch. Senior Quinn Koesters poped up for the first out, Schneider was walked intentionally to load the bases, and following Schneider's walk, Heese was the hero winning the game with a walk-off single.
'We had a talk before he went to the plate and I said 'hey stay within yourself, be confident, stay in your routine and things we're working on' and he executed that breaking ball,' Stein said of Heese's walk off.
The Cyclones move to 22-7 overall on the season, and return to action Wednesday afternoon at 1 p.m. against a Hawkeye Ten rival in the 19-3 Clarinda Cardinals, who have won four consecutive games. Offensively, the Cardinals are led by Cole Baumgart with 32 hits, and Creighton Tuzzio with 36 runs batted in and a .429 batting average. On the mound, Tuzzio has seven wins and 72 strikeouts with a 1.01 earned run average in 34 2/3 innings pitched.
'We've just got to get out and start off the game really well and get the bats hot right away,' Heese said. 'We've been kind of a middle inning game type of team.'

title: Eight Cyclones take home baseball awards
author: Alex Martin
description: Quinn Koesters and Braydon Ernst made 1 st Team, Colton Schneider, Brett Heese, and Cade Sears made 2 nd Team, while Caleb Schleis, Brock Lemrick, and Matthew Sorfonden received honorable mention. Koesters lead the team in hits with 38, batting .345, while Ernst led the team in wins with eight, pitching 65.1 innings with 52 strikeouts and a 1.71 earned run average. During the 2024 season, the Cyclones as a team finished with an overall record of 27-9, winning their first round of Regionals against Carroll 11-3, the second round against Creston 9-1, and their Regional Final against Lewis Central 10-0, making their second consecutive appearance, losing the quarterfinal round to the North Polk Comets 5-4, who eventually win on to win the 3A – Championship Game against Bishop Heelan 5-4.
content:
Eight Cyclones recently received awards in the Hawkeye Ten All Conference for their efforts in baseball, where they won 27 games as a team, including making an appearance at their second consecutive state tournament berth.
Quinn Koesters and Braydon Ernst made 1 st Team, Colton Schneider, Brett Heese, and Cade Sears made 2 nd Team, while Caleb Schleis, Brock Lemrick, and Matthew Sorfonden received honorable mention.
'It's nice to see the kids get honored for the seasons they had,' said Cyclone Head Coach Heath Stein. 'All those kids had tremendous years. They even had Cade on there as he's well respected in this conference and everybody in the league knew that he was one of the best players in the league.'
Koesters lead the team in hits with 38, batting .345, while Ernst led the team in wins with eight, pitching 65.1 innings with 52 strikeouts and a 1.71 earned run average. Schneider came out of the bullpen during the season having a 0.78 earned run average.
During the 2024 season, the Cyclones as a team finished with an overall record of 27-9, winning their first round of Regionals against Carroll 11-3, the second round against Creston 9-1, and their Regional Final against Lewis Central 10-0, making their second consecutive appearance, losing the quarterfinal round to the North Polk Comets 5-4, who eventually win on to win the 3A – Championship Game against Bishop Heelan 5-4.
'They put in the time,' Stein said. 'They got in good spots they deserved to be in. It's always in the back of your mind, the 'what if's' kind of stuff, but we won 27 games, made the state tournament, competed as well as we could've and there's a lot to be proud of.'
Koesters, Sorfonden, Ernst, Lemrick, Sears, Schleis, Keegan King, Gavin Bruck, and Franz Reisz won't return due to graduation.
'I wish them the best,' Stein added. 'They are all going to go do great things. Just a good group of kids and I got to see them grow. This group is special. They are fun, they are energetic, there are a handful of personalities and they all gel pretty well together.'
While the Cyclones will be losing nine players, Stein is optimistic about the future of Cyclone baseball with his next senior class featuring Heese, Hayden Soma, Landen Kaufman, Weston Reisz, and Jozef Reisz.
'I think we should be a team that can go compete with anyone again and win a lot of ballgames and put ourselves in a position to return to the state tournament,' Stein said.

title: Cyclones look to run strong this season
author: Alex Martin
description: The HCHS Cyclones cross country team has been working hard as they prepare for their first event Aug. 27 at the Shenandoah Early Bird where they will be one of 15 schools in attendance. 'I think Harlan's cross country program stands out among other schools because of how close the teams are, and the mindset that the coaches teach the athletes to have. The Cyclones graduated a lot of students from this past season including Taylor Bieker, Emily Schechinger, and Lauren Wingert, who is now at Peru State to run cross country.
content:
The HCHS Cyclones cross country team has been working hard as they prepare for their first event Aug. 27 at the Shenandoah Early Bird where they will be one of 15 schools in attendance.
'I am so excited for my final year of high school cross country,' said Senior Lindsey Sonderman. 'I think Harlan's cross country program stands out among other schools because of how close the teams are, and the mindset that the coaches teach the athletes to have. I've learned so much and I am so grateful that I've gotten to be a part of it for all four years.
During practices, Cyclone Head Coach Zach Klaassen has been talking to the students, making it clear what's going to be key to being successful when running five kilometers this season.
'We stress a little bit about competing every day,' he said. 'We call them windows, the distance between you and the next runner, and we need that time to be less and less, so in practice you need to be right next to the person in front of you, otherwise come race day there could be three or four other runners, and maybe more, between you and your teammate. We need five kids scoring, five kids close, and just competing to be in that top seven is not enough. You should be competing to score.'
The Cyclones graduated a lot of students from this past season including Taylor Bieker, Emily Schechinger, and Lauren Wingert, who is now at Peru State to run cross country. On the boys side, Ian Shelton, Joseph Bragg, Keaton Heileson, and others have all graduated. With the season yet to begin, and the uncertainty of who will be on varsity or JV, Klaassen is already impressed with what he's seeing up and down his roster.
'There's people fighting for those spots, so it's good to see,' he said. 'With the camp race a week ago, just seeing times went down for almost everybody by minutes, not just seconds, and it just shows what they did this summer. They've dedicated themselves to the program and to themselves and just trying to be the best versions of themselves.'
One of Klaassen's top runners this past season Lindsey Sonderman has been working hard all year preparing for her senior season, training with her friends and fellow teammates, Brylee Schechinger and Molly Swensen.
'It's not the most verbal group of kids, but they set the example by what they do,' Klaassen said. 'How they perform in practice everyday, showing up everyday, and being dedicated to the program. We have some big shoes to fill. We graduated a large senior class of great leaders, not just runners, but leaders too. They have work to do, they started on the right foot, and they're on that path right now.'
Sonderman took some high finishes last season, including first place in the Glenwood Invitational with 18:47.49, 19:38.06 in the Shenandoah Early Bird, 19:25 in the Lewis Central Invitational, 19:11.00 at Storm Lake, and 18:55.90 at the Harlan Invitational.
'My personal goals for this year are to run sub 19:00 as much as possible,' Sonderman said. 'I know times can change a lot on different courses, but I would really like to be running more consistent times.'

title: With small roster, Vikings have big plans
author: Alex Martin
description: With just five students out for cross country for the AHSTW Vikings, head coach Jackson Renberg is excited and eager to see what his team could be capable of accomplishing. Ava Paulsen, Makenna Paulsen, Yana Lander, and Bella Lamp are returning students, while Emery Brockhoff is joining the team for the first time as an incoming freshman. She had a very strong track season and we look forward to coaching her this cross country season.
content:
With just five students out for cross country for the AHSTW Vikings, head coach Jackson Renberg is excited and eager to see what his team could be capable of accomplishing.
Ava Paulsen, Makenna Paulsen, Yana Lander, and Bella Lamp are returning students, while Emery Brockhoff is joining the team for the first time as an incoming freshman.
'I am very excited to have four girls back from the previous season,' Renberg said. 'I am also excited about the new freshman runner Emery Brockhoff that we have coming up. Emery has been a great addition to the team with a very good attitude and work ethic that her other teammates feed off of. Ava Paulsen is a returning individual state qualifier for last year and she has looked good in practice. She had a very strong track season and we look forward to coaching her this cross country season. Kenna Paulsen has also had a very strong start of the season and we hope to continue to build on it. She's a very good kid that I believe has had better form and better paces early on in the season. Yana Lander is also one we are fortunate to have as she has been a consistent runner in our program since she was in Junior High. She has been improving in the right way thus far in the season. We just need to keep building her endurance and form up every day.'
The Vikings will open their season Aug. 27 at the Shenandoah Early Bird event, where they will be one of 14 schools in attendance.
'I think the Shenandoah meet is going to be a good indicator of where we are as a whole team and individually early on in the season,' Renberg added. 'The biggest thing is going to be mentally tough and trusting their training, pushing themselves to get better. We want to use every day and every meet to get better, and that meet will be no different. However, it will be good to run against other teams and individuals and see where we stack up early in the season and go out and compete.'
Last year at the Shenandoah Early Bird, Lamp was the fastest among all the Vikings girls taking an eighth place finish overall 23:31.33, just under four minutes behind the winner, Lindsey Sonderman of Harlan Community, who won the event with 19:38.06.
Lamp also took a sixth place finish at the Logan-Magnolia Invitational with 21:00.84, seventh place at the Treynor Invite with 23:10.19, 11 th place at the Nodaway Valley Invite with 23:14.90, and seventh place at the 1A State Qualifying Meet at Mount Ayr with 21:11.30.
'Bella had a very good freshman year qualifying for state individually and helping our team qualify for state,' Renberg said. 'Bella is a talented athlete, but more importantly she is a hard worker that does the little things right every time. She's one that does the right things over and over and it compounds to her being more successful than just her talent allows. I am excited to see her continue to grow and hopefully improve her times as she has had a very strong summer as well and a good start to the season.'
Renberg has been having the girls practice and been making it clear to them what will be important to have a strong season.
'Most important thing is doing the small things right and building off of each day,' he said. 'We know that everything isn't going to perfect itself right away. Sports in general is about improving yourself each and every day to become the best athlete and person you can be. Thus far this season the group has been successful in doing this and if we continue we will be a very strong team. We have also wanted to continue to emphasize form as it will help them run faster and more efficiently. This is a hard process, but the girls are going to continue to work on it to become better runners and athletes.'
However, Renberg knows the challenges that come with a long season, but knows if body management takes place and staying hydrated with the proper nutrition, the less that will occur.
'The biggest challenge we have in cross country is our team numbers,' he added. 'We have a great group of kids for our girls high school team. The biggest thing is making sure we take care of our bodies and making sure we prevent injuries by doing the small things right like nutrition, hydration, stretching, and sleep. The group is a very dedicated team and we look forward to continuing to push them to get better as the season goes on.'

title: Cyclones suffer big loss on Senior Night
author: Alex Martin
description: It didn't take long for the Lewis Central Titan offense to get going, as with just under eight minutes remaining in the first quarter, on a 2nd and goal, Senior Titan Brody Patlan went for a 4-yard touchdown run and dive getting into the end zone, putting his team up 6-0, which was followed by the extra point from Junior Jimmy Scott. However, only minutes later, the Cyclones got right back in the game when on 2nd & 10, Junior Ayden Redmon took off for a 52-yard touchdown run sending the Cyclone fan base into an eruption of applause. Van Baale stopped the Titan offense in a crucial moment in the first quarter when they had a chance to add to their lead but couldn't when Van Baale came up with a tackle on 3rd and 7, forcing the Titans to punt the ball back to the Cyclones.
content:
It didn't take long for the Lewis Central Titan offense to get going, as with just under eight minutes remaining in the first quarter, on a 2nd and goal, Senior Titan Brody Patlan went for a 4-yard touchdown run and dive getting into the end zone, putting his team up 6-0, which was followed by the extra point from Junior Jimmy Scott.
However, only minutes later, the Cyclones got right back in the game when on 2nd & 10, Junior Ayden Redmon took off for a 52-yard touchdown run sending the Cyclone fan base into an eruption of applause. Senior kicker Nolan Schwery tied the game at seven with the extra point.
'Man, he hit it north south and then he ran through a little arm tackle and just took it 52 yards,' said Cyclone Head Coach Todd Bladt. 'Great run and that's what we see. That capability from him. We've just got to keep working on some north south stuff and not a lot of lateral. He's going to be a weapon for us, and that was good to see from him.'
Following Redmon's touchdown, the Cyclones never found paydirt again, but they had some players step up on the defensive side including Bryce Van Baale who came away with 17 tackles on the night. Van Baale stopped the Titan offense in a crucial moment in the first quarter when they had a chance to add to their lead but couldn't when Van Baale came up with a tackle on 3rd and 7, forcing the Titans to punt the ball back to the Cyclones.
'He brings the intensity,' Bladt said of Van Baale's defense. 'He's got high expectations which are fantastic. He's going to be keep improving and producing. He's going to keep being that leader out there on the field.'
In the second quarter when the Cyclones were on offense, it was 3rd and 16 when Junior quarterback Gabe Arkfeld threw an inception to Junior Titan Peyton Phippen who ran for a 16-yard touchdown to put his team back in front. Scott added the extra point to make it 14-7 Titans.
When the Cyclone offense got back on the field, they started their run from the 35-yard line with multiple first downs from Senior running back Lukas Francis and Redmon. Unfortunately, only a few plays later, Arkfeld threw another interception, this time to Junior Titan Leonardo Tatum.
The Titan offense returned to the field with hopes of scoring, but the Cyclones caught a huge break when a fumble was recovered by Junior Cyclone Dallas McDowell at the 8-yard line, giving the Cyclones a great opportunity to score. Unfortunately, they had to settle for a field goal from Schwery to cut the Titan lead to 14-10.
'We had an unfortunate situation where we lost a key player there, and we kind of were struggling with personnel groups,' Bladt said. 'Those are the things that give coaches nightmares. There's a million what if's that you could have. That kind of limited us offensively, but I thought our guys played tough.'
With the second quarter winding down, the Cyclones were hoping to keep the Titans off the scoreboard, but with just over 30 seconds remaining, Senior quarterback Brady Hetzel found Phippen for a 12-yard touchdown pass to expand the Titan lead to 20-10, followed by the extra point from Scott to take an 11-point lead into halftime.
'We were going to focus on what we could do,' Bladt said. 'We had a 3-and-out stop. We marched the ball down the field. If we get that 3-and-out, then march down, we get a touchdown, we're back in the game and it's a ballgame. Instead it flipped the script on us and got away from us in the third quarter.'
The third quarter was quiet when it began, but just under the halfway point, Lewis Central's offense continued to make noise when Hetzel threw a 75-yard touchdown catch and run to Tatum putting his team up 27-10, which was followed by another extra point from Scott.
The rest of the quarter remained quiet. However, not long into the fourth quarter, the Titans were in a position to score once again, getting a 30-yard field goal from Scott to put his team up 31-10. The Cyclones had a few more opportunities to score, but nothing came of it as the clock expired giving them their first loss of the season.
Before the game, it was Senior Night at Merrill Field as Francis, Van Baale, Landen Kaufman, Weston Reisz, Spencer Fink, Jozef Reisz, Caden Bruck, Austin Spray, Kayden Erwin, Nolan Schwery, Alex Heithoff, Jacob Brouse, Masen Shults, Hayden Soma, Thomas Kurtz, Ben Leinen, Brett Heese, and Malcolm McDonald were all honored for their contributions to the program.
'They're great kids,' Bladt said of the Seniors. 'They're fantastic leaders. They've taken on a big leadership role. I'm proud to have them, and I wouldn't want to go to war with anybody else.'
The Cyclones will return to Merrill Field Friday at 7 p.m. for the next opponent, the Denison Monarchs, who are coming off a 41-28 victory in their season opener against Council Bluffs Jefferson. Last season, the Monarchs finished 7-3 making it to the Class 4A – First Round Game losing 42-0 to the ADM Tigers. Offensively, they were led by Senior Luke Wiebers with 1,063 passing yards, Senior Blaine Brodsky 598 rushing yards, and Senior Jake Fink with 455 receiving yards. Defensively, Wiebers led in tackles with 57.5.
'They have a new head coach,' Bladt said. 'Former player in Harlan, Willie Baughman. It'll be interesting to see them on film and what they're trying to do. We're going to have to game plan and see what we can try to exploit and what we think we can do.'

title: Cyclones hand Monarchs their first loss
author: Alex Martin
description: In the fourth set of Thursday's home volleyball match, Cyclone Senior Macy Mueller scored the final point of the night which landed in between two Monarch defenders, winning the set 25-23, and giving the Cyclones their fourth win of the season, along with handing the Monarchs their first loss. In set one, the Cyclones got off to a strong start at one point leading 15-9 before Monarch head coach McKenzie Mich called a timeout. In set two, the Monarch were able to get back in it with a 25-20 victory, evening the match and one win apiece.
content:
In the fourth set of Thursday's home volleyball match, Cyclone Senior Macy Mueller scored the final point of the night which landed in between two Monarch defenders, winning the set 25-23, and giving the Cyclones their fourth win of the season, along with handing the Monarchs their first loss.
'Emercyn Reischl told me it was there, and I saw the blockers on the other side,' Mueller said. 'They were waiting for me to set it either to any of the those big hitters I have up there in Aubrey [Schwieso], Hope [Preston], and Kenzley [Bruck]. I saw it was open, and I took the chance for it.'
In set one, the Cyclones got off to a strong start at one point leading 15-9 before Monarch head coach McKenzie Mich called a timeout. When play resumed, the Monarchs went on an 8-3 run, cutting the Cyclone lead to 18-17. The Cyclones found a way to get turn the tables on the Monachs closing out the set winning 25-21.
In set two, the Monarch were able to get back in it with a 25-20 victory, evening the match and one win apiece.
'I think we were playing really, really good volleyball in the first set, and we kind of just took it for granted,' Mueller added. 'We took a set off, but we came right back.'
The Cyclone bounced back with a strong win in set three at one point leading the Monarchs 16-11 before Mich called a timeout. Following the timeout, the Cyclones closed out the set with a back-and-forth battle, but got some key blocks that prevented potential Monarch points at the net from Schwieso and Addison Wicks.
'I think it's really important for our passers in the back row that we just have a layer before the ball gets to them, especially getting a block touch before it gets back to them, so it doesn't hit the ground right away,' Schwieso said.
Set four was a seesaw battle with the Cyclones leading a majority of the time, but the Monarchs on their tails not going down without a fight. The Monarchs managed to go on a 5-3 run towards the end of the set, cutting the Cyclone lead to 24-23, forcing a timeout from Crees. However, when play resumed, Mueller was able to step in and score the final point.
'She sees the court well. It was a very smart play, especially when we have three power hitters at the net,' Crees said. 'The expectation was thought of the hitters, and she caught them off guard.'
With this win, the Cyclones move to 4-6 on the season. They were be back in action Saturday at 8:30 a.m. for a tournament featuring eight schools at Glenwood High School.
'There's going to be a lot of really talented teams there,' Mueller said. 'I think if we practice good volleyball and keep our energy up, that will be key, and I think we will do really well.'

title: Cyclones football earns first road win over Rams
author: Alex Martin
description: The Cyclones took the early lead when Junior quarterback Gabe Arkfeld handed off to Senior running back Lukas Francis, who managed to bulldoze his way through the Rams defense going for a 36-yard touchdown run on 3 rd and 7. However, the Cyclone offense came alive in the back end of the second quarter when on a 2 nd and 9, Arkfeld threw a missile to Senior Jozef Reisz who caught the ball, got around the Rams defense making his way into the end zone for a touchdown to put his team up 13-0. The Rams punched right back when on a 2 nd & 10, Senior quarterback Cole Staudt threw to Junior Kaden Crouch who caught the ball at and out ran the Cyclone defense get his team right back in the game with a touchdown.
content:
The HCHS Cyclones football team responded to their first road test Friday against the Glenwood Rams winning 38-22 and moved to 2-1 on the season.
The Cyclones took the early lead when Junior quarterback Gabe Arkfeld handed off to Senior running back Lukas Francis, who managed to bulldoze his way through the Rams defense going for a 36-yard touchdown run on 3 rd and 7. Senior Nolan Schwery kicked the extra point to give the Cyclones a 7-0 lead.
'Our guys up front, we ran the ball pretty effectively early, and as the game went on, they kind of started shooting gaps on us and up front, we were not getting our job in the run game, so we had to lean on them a little bit,' said Cyclone Head Coach Todd Bladt.
The remainder of the quarter was quiet. However, the Cyclone offense came alive in the back end of the second quarter when on a 2 nd and 9, Arkfeld threw a missile to Senior Jozef Reisz who caught the ball, got around the Rams defense making his way into the end zone for a touchdown to put his team up 13-0. Schwery kicked the extra point.
The Rams punched right back when on a 2 nd & 10, Senior quarterback Cole Staudt threw to Junior Kaden Crouch who caught the ball at and out ran the Cyclone defense get his team right back in the game with a touchdown. But the Cyclones responded quickly.
With under 45 seconds remaining in the first half on a 3 rd and 13, Arkfeld found Jozef Reisz in the end zone for a 13-yard touchdown pass, as Reisz went up to catch the pass giving his team a 20-7 lead. Schwery kicked the extra point.
'The big thing I told them looking at the close game they [Glenwood] were in the week before, there was no doubt, they were going to try and stay within striking distance,' Bladt said. 'We never really blew it up. They never really got out of it completely because they got it back to 16 there at the end.'
It didn't take long for the Cyclones to score out of the gate in third quarter when on a 1 st & 15, Arkfeld found Reisz once again for a 19-yard touchdown catch and run expanding their lead to 27-7. Schwery kicked the extra point.
The Rams proved they were not going down without a fight and stayed within striking distance of the Cyclones as a few minutes later, approaching the midway point of the quarter on a 3 rd & goal, Sophomore Chase Razor had a 6-yard touchdown run making it a 28-13 game.
Arkfeld and Reisz continued to have great chemistry throughout the game as Arkfeld again found Reisz who was wide open for a touchdown catch and run where Reisz easily got into the end zone expanding the Cyclone lead to 34-14. Schwery kicked the extra point.
'He had a big night,' Bladt said of Arkfeld. 'He's starting to grow and he's starting to see some things a little bit better.
In the fourth quarter with just over eight minutes remaining on the clock, the Cyclones got their final points of the game when they were unable to score a touchdown, but settled for a field goal from Schwery, who put his team up 38-14.
The Rams had one last fight in the them that came on a 1 st & 10, Staudt took matters into his own hands, faking a handoff, going for an 11-yard touchdown run to put his team back within 18 points of the Cyclones. The Rams final points of the night would come on a 2-point conversion from Junior Pierce Dalton following Staudt's touchdown, but the Cyclones hung on for the 38-22 victory.
'At one point we were up 24, but they were able to score and convert a 2-point conversion, and that leaves you within two scores,' Bladt said. 'We were up three scores, possibly four there if they don't convert on that 2-point conversion.'
The Cyclones move to 2-1 on the season and will be back in action on the road Friday night at 7 p.m. taking on the 3-0 Sergeant Bluff-Luton Warriors. Offensively, the Warriors are led by Isaiah Jervik with 204 passing yards, Zayvion Ellington with 274 rushing yards, Gavin Merrill with 70 receiving yards. Defensively, Kaleb Pendergast has 13.5 tackles.
'I don't particularly like the way they play because they play really, really hard,' Bladt added. 'They're going to be a tough team. There's no doubt. They're 3-0, ranked #2 in the state. They get after it offensively. They have a unique offense. When you have the right guys, which they do to run it, it hits pretty well. I look for that to be a tough battle in northern country.'

title: Cyclones and Vikings perform at Cyclone Invite Saturday
content:
Saturday morning, the HCHS Cyclones girls cross country team took another first place finish at the Harlan Golf & Country Club, finishing two points ahead of Lewis Central and three ahead of Glenwood.
'It was awesome,' said Cyclone Head Coach Zach Klaassen. 'We love hosting. We knew going into it, it was going to be a three-team race. Everybody had a job, and I thought everybody did a good job of executing that for the most part. When it comes down to three points separating first and third, a lot of things have to go right, and I thought we did a good job of that.'
On the boys side they took a 13th place finish as a team. Erik Heslink and Jeffrey Gross set the tone with Heslink running 18:30.65 finishing 25th overall, and Gross right behind him at 26th with 18:33.39.
'I think they're getting better each time they go out,' Klaassen said. 'Jeffrey has been battling some injuries too, and Erik with his health, and you can tell they are both getting better with each race, so hopefully in a couple of weeks, they'll be back to about 100%.'
For the girls, Lindsey Sonderman was the fastest Cyclone finishing with 18:27.11, just 11 seconds behind the winner, Lili Denton of St. Albert.
'She [Denton] got out really fast, so that scared me in the beginning,' Sonderman said. 'Eventually I edged up to her a little bit, and I was just trying to not be on her heels because I thought that would make her go even faster. Hopefully I can keep making that gap smaller and smaller.'
With six events into the season, Sonderman has either won or taken second place, finishing second every time behind Denton. She took an opportunity to reflect on how she feels she's performing to this point in the season.
'I'm really thankful for the Harlan program,' she said.
