title: Shelby County man sentenced to 22 years for drug charges
description: COUNCIL BLUFFS – A Shelby County man was sentenced on January 14, 2025 to more than 22 years in federal prison for conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine. Public court documents state on January 2, 2024, law enforcement pursued a vehicle in a high-speed chase through Harlan and Avoca, including on Interstate 80. On January 31, 2024, Gifford engaged in a second high-speed chase with law enforcement and was in possession of over 190 grams of methamphetamine and $29,845.
content:
COUNCIL BLUFFS – A Shelby County man was sentenced on January 14, 2025 to more than 22 years in federal prison for conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine. U.S. Attorney Richard D. Westphal of the Southern District Court of Iowa announced Thursday Sean Patrick Gifford, 41, was sentenced to 270 months in prison.
Public court documents state on January 2, 2024, law enforcement pursued a vehicle in a high-speed chase through Harlan and Avoca, including on Interstate 80. The driver of the vehicle was identified as Gifford. On January 31, 2024, Gifford engaged in a second high-speed chase with law enforcement and was in possession of over 190 grams of methamphetamine and $29,845. Evidence located during a forensic search of Gifford's cell phone corroborated his drug trafficking activities and linked him to the distribution of 4.5 kilograms of methamphetamine.
After completing his term of imprisonment, Gifford will be required to serve a five-year term of supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system.
The case was investigated by the Council Bluffs Police Department, Southwest Iowa Narcotics Enforcement Task Force, and Iowa State Patrol.

title: Cyclones earn win over Spoofhounds
author: Alex Martin
description: Sophomore Spoofhound Claire Walter made the first shot of the game on a free throw, but then the Cyclones went on a 9-0 run forcing a timeout from Spoofhound head coach Del Morley. When play resumed, both teams got locked into a back-and-forth affair until Cyclone Senior Aubrey Schwieso made a layup, followed by an assist to Senior Grace Albertsen who went for a layup, forcing another timeout from Morley. Sophomore Spoofhound Grace Stiens made a layup to cut the Cyclone lead back to single digits.
content:
The HCHS Cyclones girls basketball team continues to stay hot winning their seventh consecutive game 67-55 Thursday night at home against the Maryville Spoofhounds.
'We played well,' said Cyclone Head Coach Zach Klaassen. 'I thought we got out of the gates really well. They [Maryville] were pressing us. We were cutting it up getting easy buckets. We were scoring inside and getting to the hoop as well.'
Sophomore Spoofhound Claire Walter made the first shot of the game on a free throw, but then the Cyclones went on a 9-0 run forcing a timeout from Spoofhound head coach Del Morley.
When play resumed, both teams got locked into a back-and-forth affair until Cyclone Senior Aubrey Schwieso made a layup, followed by an assist to Senior Grace Albertsen who went for a layup, forcing another timeout from Morley.
Sophomore Spoofhound Grace Stiens made a layup to cut the Cyclone lead back to single digits. Following Stiens layup, both teams continued to exchange buckets with the Cyclones leading by six heading into the second quarter.
The Cyclones opened the quarter on a 6-0 Albertsen run where she made three layups, putting the Cyclones up 31-19.
'They [Maryville] didn't really have eyes on me pretty much the whole second quarter,' Albertsen said. 'I was able to find those open spots and my teammates were able to find me.'
The Spoofhound offense managed to get back in the game going on a 10-5 run to close out the half with the Cyclones leading by seven.
'We needed to keep our lead and not let them back in it,' Albertsen added. 'Keep doing what we were doing and finish out the game.'
Schwieso opened the third quarter with a finger roll layup. Junior Spoofhound Payton Kurz answered back with a mid-range jump shot, but Albertsen once again continued her dominance at the basket with another layup.
The Spoofhounds managed to cut the Cyclone lead down to five points when Walter and Kurz scored, but Sophomore Cyclones Kenzley Bruck made a mid-range jump shot, followed by a layup from Schwieso, along with the last shot of the quarter coming from Albertsen on a layup leading by eight points heading into the final quarter.
'I thought we made some good extra passes,' Klaassen said. 'We got a couple of reversals in there where we hit Grace on that backside block. Kenzley was back on, high and soft, so that was good to see. It was working inside.'
Senior Cyclone Molly Swensen assisted the ball to Bruck to open the fourth quarter where Bruck went for the layup. However, Walter got her team back within single digits when she made two free throws, followed by a mid-range shot.
Albertsen and Bruck continued their dominance at the hoop with more baskets to move their lead back to double digits. A few plays later, Schwieso came down court, missed a shot from 3-point range, but Sophomore Brinley Van Baale obtained the rebound and made the layup, which started a 6-0 run.
'That was huge,' Klaassen said of Van Baale's basket. 'We needed a bucket at that point and time. She was right where she needed to be. It seemed like it floated in the air forever. Her shots looks good in practice and we've just got to get it looking good in the game.'
The Cyclones closed out the Spoofhounds for their 14 th win of the season, moving to 14-3 overall. They won't rest for long returning to action Friday at home against the 6-11 Creston Panthers. The Panthers are led by Junior Kadley Bailey averaging 18.5 points, Junior Ella Turner averaging averaging 6.2 rebounds, and Junior Hollynn Rieck averaging 5.8 assists per game.
'I think we'll be good,' Albertsen said. 'We'll go into it like any other game. It's always 0-0 to start, but we'll put in the work, and hopefully come out on top.'

title: Schwery signs LOI at Midland for football
author: Alex Martin
description: HCHS Senior Nolan Schwery has signed a football Letter of Intent at Midland University. During the signing at Midland, Schwery's mom and dad, Joi and Paul, were in attendance, along with his older sister, Tela. With multiple choices in front of him, Schwery talked about what made him settle on Midland University.
content:
HCHS Senior Nolan Schwery has signed a football Letter of Intent at Midland University.
'I'm just really excited and ready to start playing football again,' he said.
During the signing at Midland, Schwery's mom and dad, Joi and Paul, were in attendance, along with his older sister, Tela.
'They give me a lot of support,' Schwery said. 'My parents don't push me as much, but it's mainly my brother who pushes me to be the best person I can. Two of my brothers have been in my shoes going to do college wrestling.'
With multiple choices in front of him, Schwery talked about what made him settle on Midland University.
'I just basically looked at what schools offered what stuff football wise, and Midland felt like home to me,' he said.
This season, Midland finished with a 6-5 overall record with wins against Clarke, Dakota Wesleyan, Waldorf, Briar Cliff, Hastings, and Doane. Schwery plans to major in education during his time there.
During his football career with the Cyclones, Schwery was the punter/kicker his junior and senior season. He credited a former teammate and current Dordt Defender, along with his coaching staff who helped him along the way.
'Some of my teammates, like Stephen Leinen helped me along the way,' Schwery said. 'He basically taught me a lot of the stuff I know how to kick and how to punt. It'll be exciting to kick against him next year this coming fall. All my teammates and coaches have helped me out along the way.'
He talked about fond memories he has from his time playing Cyclone football.
'Mainly it was winning state my freshman and sophomore year, and then kicking the game-winning field goals against Glenwood and Nevada, last year and this year,' Schwery added.
Before his senior season concludes, Schwery will play soccer for the Cyclones. Regardless of how the rest of his high school journey plays out, he will forever be grateful for his time at HCHS.
'I just want to thank everybody that helped me along the way with my teammates, my coaches,' he said. 'What my coaches have taught me throughout my high school career in football and soccer, just helping me be the best I can at that next level.'

title: Cyclones stay hot with ninth consecutive win
author: Alex Martin
description: Despite getting off to a slow start Friday night at home against the Lewis Central Titans trailing 17-5, at the end of the first quarter, the HCHS girls basketball team got going in the second half winning 63-51 for their ninth consecutive victory and 17 th of the season. Senior Grace Albertsen made the first shot via a layup, followed by a free throw from Van Baale, but the Titans got going with a 15-0 run to close out the quarter. Sophomore Titan Ellie Borns opened the second quarter with a 3-pointer, but the Cyclones responded back with a 7-0 run, with a layup from Albertsen, a 3-point shot from Schwieso, and a mid-range jumper from Sophomore Kenzley Bruck.
content:
Despite getting off to a slow start Friday night at home against the Lewis Central Titans trailing 17-5, at the end of the first quarter, the HCHS girls basketball team got going in the second half winning 63-51 for their ninth consecutive victory and 17 th of the season.
'I think our posts are playing really well inside and they're finishing just about everything,' said Cyclone Senior Aubrey Schwieso. 'Brinley [Van Baale] and Molly [Swensen] hit some huge shots, so it's always nice to see those fall. I think we're getting a good mix of hitting shots everywhere.'
Senior Grace Albertsen made the first shot via a layup, followed by a free throw from Van Baale, but the Titans got going with a 15-0 run to close out the quarter.
'I think the first quarter was a lot to take in,' Schwieso said. 'We had quite an atmosphere here. We needed to settle in and the second quarter we did a great job of that.'
Sophomore Titan Ellie Borns opened the second quarter with a 3-pointer, but the Cyclones responded back with a 7-0 run, with a layup from Albertsen, a 3-point shot from Schwieso, and a mid-range jumper from Sophomore Kenzley Bruck. The Cyclones kept their foot on the gas pedal rallying to tie the game at halftime with two 3-pointers from Van Baale to close out the half.
'Her shots are coming,' said Cyclone Head Coach Zach Klaassen of Van Baale. 'She has been shooting it pretty well here for the last 3-5 games. We made a little tweak on her release. It seemed like she wasn't extending all the way out, kind of flaring her elbow, we called it the chicken wing, got that elbow tucked in, and all of a sudden everything is going straight towards the hoop instead of out to the right.'
The third began as a seesaw battle until Schwieso made back-to-back layups forcing a timeout from Titan head coach Coleman Mullenix. Following the timeout, Schwieso banked home another 3-pointer, followed by a mid-ranger from Bruck as the Cyclones led by five heading into the final quarter.
Sophomore Titan Macie Vetter drained a 3-pointer to cut the Cyclones lead to two points to open the quarter, but the Cyclones managed to extend their lead with back-to-back 3's from Swensen, followed later from free throws from her to close out the game.
Following the game, Mia Schwieso, who passed away two years ago was honored by the school.
'If you were an outsider coming to this game tonight, that's what Shelby County is,' Klaassen said. 'That's a great family, and everybody's coming in to support them. If it was another family, this whole family would come back and support them as well. The Schwieso family is very special to this community, very special to me, and we're so proud of what everybody's done to help them. There's no taking away what they've gone through. Like what Chris [Schwieso] said Mia would be very proud of what people are doing for her, this family, and this community. It's a special night.'
The Cyclones return to action Tuesday at Wells Fargo Arena against Hawkeye Ten opponent, the 15-6 Atlantic Trojans, who have won three consecutive games. The Trojans are led by Senior Paytn Harter averaging 17.2 points and 10.5 rebounds per game, along with Junior Zoey Kirchhoff averaging 3.6 assists per game.
'We're excited for that game,' Klaassen added. 'Everybody likes to play on that court. It's a special place to play. I think the last time we played there we left with a bitter taste in our mouths, so hopefully it's a little bit sweeter this time.'

title: Spartans lose Regional Final in heartbreak
author: Alex Martin
description: UNDERWOOD - With 1.2 seconds remaining in regulation trailing by one to the Treynor Cardinals, the Exira-EHK Spartans were hoping for a last second shot to punch their ticket to the state tournament. The Spartans came up empty when Sophomore Taryn Petersen missed a shot attempt, losing 45-44 ending their season. Freshman Spartan Zoey Rasmussen was able to drain a 3-point shot on an open look to give the Spartans a 5-3 lead.
content:
UNDERWOOD - With 1.2 seconds remaining in regulation trailing by one to the Treynor Cardinals, the Exira-EHK Spartans were hoping for a last second shot to punch their ticket to the state tournament. The Spartans came up empty when Sophomore Taryn Petersen missed a shot attempt, losing 45-44 ending their season.
'This one is tough to swallow,' said Spartan Head Coach Tom Petersen. 'Credit to Treynor. They did a great job. I'm so proud of my kids. They found a way to battle tonight and we had a chance almost at the end.'
Taryn opened the game with the first basket on a mid-range floater to give the Spartans an early lead. Junior Cardinal Nora Konz put her team in front soon after with a 3-point shot.
Freshman Spartan Zoey Rasmussen was able to drain a 3-point shot on an open look to give the Spartans a 5-3 lead.
'For a freshman to step in there, she doesn't hesitate,' Petersen said of Rasmussen. 'One of the things I've told her all year is when you're open you're a shooter, shoot the ball, and she does. She could be 0-for-7 or 0-for-8, and she'll shoot the next seven or eight in a row.'
The Cardinal offense got going closing out the quarter on a 7-3 run leading 14-8. Junior Ella Thornton opened the quarter with a layup forcing a timeout from Petersen. When play resumed, the Spartans were able to get back in the game on a layup from Junior Kadence Sporrer along with back-to-back layups from Taryn.
Towards the end of the quarter, Taryn made another shot from the 3-point line, along with another two 3's from Rasmussen as the Spartans led 28-27 at halftime.
'The girls need to stay physical,' Petersen said. 'I thought they were getting second chance opportunities, and I wasn't very happy. Execution on the offensive side wasn't very good.'
The third quarter began with another 3-pointer from Rasmussen, her fourth of the game, putting the Spartans up by four. Konz made another two layups, along with a layup from Freshman Addison Mauer as the Cardinals led 33-31 heading into the final quarter.
Mauer drained a 3-pointer at the start of the fourth quarter. Following Mauer's 3-point shot, both teams continued to exchange shots. A big moment came for the Spartans when Sporrer made a clutch 3-point shot, putting her team down by one, immediately following a timeout from Petersen.
'I told them we were going to get a steal and have an opportunity, and we legit did,' Petersen added. 'We got a steal and we cut it to one.'
The Spartans unfortunately couldn't overcome the Cardinals, closing out their season with an 18-6 record. The Spartans won 16 regular season games against Boyer Valley, Earlham, IKM-Manning, Woodbine, Ar-We-Va, and others, along with two Regional victories against Underwood and MVAOCOU. Seniors Harlee Fahn and Alissa Testroet won't return due to graduating.
'They might be 5'6 and 5'7, but they play like they're 6'0,' Petersen said. 'They wear their hearts on their sleeve. I wish I could've had Alissa all four years. Harlee is a battler. She's a special person.'

title: Cyclones open track season March 14 at ISU Indoor Meet
author: Alex Martin
description: A new season is right around the turn for the HCHS Cyclones girls track and field team and they've been practicing for a week at Merrill Field. 'We aren't looking for times or distances, just a willingness to get out of your comfort zone and push yourself and push each other. In addition to the seniors, Hamilton also has several returners this season, including Ari Daniels, Paige Sonderman, Aubree Wegner, Ava Freund, and Sadie Alberti.
content:
A new season is right around the turn for the HCHS Cyclones girls track and field team and they've been practicing for a week at Merrill Field.
'I'm very excited for this track season,' said Senior Lindsey Sonderman. 'There is something special about our team and some of my favorite high school memories have been on the track with them so I'm very grateful for another season of that.'
During the first week of practice, head coach Jenny Hamilton, along with assistant coach, Jacie Stuerman, have been telling the girls what's key to starting things off on the right foot.
'We have emphasized positive attitudes, open mindedness, and effort,' Hamilton said. 'We aren't looking for times or distances, just a willingness to get out of your comfort zone and push yourself and push each other. We want to create an environment where teammates not only encourage one another, but also challenge and push each other to be their best.'
Hamilton is excited for the current seniors to lead the way; Abby Broeckelman, Jaylee Schmitz, Brylee Schechinger, and Lindsey Sonderman.
'They each bring so many unique strengths to the team, and will certainly be relying on them to use those strengths to lead and set an example daily not only in how they compete, but also in their words and body language,' Hamilton said.
In addition to the seniors, Hamilton also has several returners this season, including Ari Daniels, Paige Sonderman, Aubree Wegner, Ava Freund, and Sadie Alberti.
Last season for the Cyclones, Daniels was the third fastest in 100m hurdles with 18.30, a little over a minute behind the leader, Jaylee Schmitz with 16.93. Paige Sonderman ran the fastest 400m with 1:06.12. Wegner ran the second fastest 100m dash with 13.41, right on the tail of Dani Smith, who ran 13.38. Freund and Alberti were part of multiple relay teams including the 4x200 and 4x400.
Sonderman was one of Hamilton's top runners in 2024. She ran the fastest 800m race with 2:28.17, the fastest 1500m with 4:50.85, and the fastest 3000m run with 10:21.81.
'We are proud of and excited for Lindsey's next adventure in college, but she has always been very committed to this team,' Hamilton said. 'She works extremely hard in the off-season and is coming into this season with big goals. At the same time, she is always all about the team and ready to contribute however she can to push and serve her teammates.'
The Cyclones first event will be March 14 at the IATC Indoor Championships at Iowa State University at the Lied Recreation Center.
'I think many of my teammates and I are looking forward to our first meet and seeing what marks we are starting the season off with,' Sonderman said. 'I think one of the most important things we can do is go into this meet with confidence and not let the nerves get to us.'

title: Pipeline representatives answer questions at Shelby County Supervisors meeting
description: SHELBY COUNTY — Representatives from Summit Carbon Solutions were in attendance at the Shelby County Board of Supervisors meeting Tuesday, March 4, to update the Board and take questions on the proposed carbon capture pipeline project. Lange reported the Iowa Utility Commission approved the proposed construction permit in June, and construction in Iowa is contingent to the approval of the permit in South Dakota. Former Board of Supervisor Chairman and current CO2 pipeline liaison for the Shelby County Supervisors asked, 'If we have a pipeline running through our county, and we have no ethanol plant here, can you explain how this benefits us?' 'It's going to create a larger market, which then increases the value of the corn,' said Lange.
content:
SHELBY COUNTY — Representatives from Summit Carbon Solutions were in attendance at the Shelby County Board of Supervisors meeting Tuesday, March 4, to update the Board and take questions on the proposed carbon capture pipeline project.
Kylie Lange, Iowa Pipeline Manager for Summit was accompanied by company spokesman Riley Gibson. Lange said more than half of the landowners on the proposed pipeline route have signed voluntary easement agreements.
Lange reported the Iowa Utility Commission approved the proposed construction permit in June, and construction in Iowa is contingent to the approval of the permit in South Dakota.
'There's a lot hinging on South Dakota,' Lange said.
Supervisor Mike Kolbe asked if the proposed route could be modified since IUC had approved the permit. Lange said a 'small amount of changes' may be made.
More than 40 were in attendance, and in expectation of a larger crowd, the meeting was moved to the C.G. Therkildsen Activity Center in Harlan.
Former Board of Supervisor Chairman and current CO2 pipeline liaison for the Shelby County Supervisors asked, 'If we have a pipeline running through our county, and we have no ethanol plant here, can you explain how this benefits us?'
'It's going to create a larger market, which then increases the value of the corn,' said Lange.
Shelby County landowners affected by the pipeline route don't agree.
'There's no way somebody is going to put a house on land that has a pipeline in it,' said Sherri Webb.
Webb and her sister, Cindy Hansen, and their siblings inherited Shelby County land from their grandmother.
Webb questioned the damage the pipeline would cause to the soil, terraces, and tiling. 'You can't restore the structure of the land,' Webb said.
'This pipeline is a joke, no offense,' Hansen said.
Other Shelby County landowners questioned the company officials on the use of eminent domain, safety issues, insurance liability and water usage.
Alex Londo, Shelby County Emergency Management Agency Coordinator asked about what training Summit would provide Shelby County's First Responders. 'We have several jurisdictions and they will need equipment.' Londo also asked Lange about a livestock emergency plan, as several feedlots are along the proposed route.
'We will work on it with you,' Lange said.
Additional county and city officials present at the meeting included City of Harlan City Administrator Gervas Mgonja, Harlan Fire Chief Roger Bissen, members of the Shelby County Sheriff's Office, and Shelby County Assessor Tony Buman.
Following the meeting, Webb said, 'When you take care and nurture something for over 125 years, it's not just the land. It's legacy, history, and family.' Grandma and Grandpa treasured this land, and so did our parents. Now, it's ours to take care of and advocate for.'

title: Spartans open golf season with Triangular
author: Alex Martin
description: The Spartans lost some talented golfers from last years boys and girls team including Shay Burmeister, Trey Petersen, Easton Nelson, Derrek Kommes, and Gavin Bengard. Burmeister had 42 strokes on a 9-hole course and 104 strokes on an 18-hole course. On the boys side, Petersen was the top scorer with 39 strokes on a 9-hole course, followed by Bengard and Kommes with 48 strokes.
content:
Despite losing a lot of seniors, the Exira-EHK Spartans golf team is optimistic as it prepares to tee-off March 26 in a triangular with CAM and AHSTW.
'It has been fun so far this year,' said Spartan Head Coach Tom Petersen. 'It's great to have a lot of kids out that will be competing for spots with 16 kids. Hopefully we get some nicer weather so we can get on the course more.'
The Spartans lost some talented golfers from last years boys and girls team including Shay Burmeister, Trey Petersen, Easton Nelson, Derrek Kommes, and Gavin Bengard.
Burmeister had 42 strokes on a 9-hole course and 104 strokes on an 18-hole course. On the boys side, Petersen was the top scorer with 39 strokes on a 9-hole course, followed by Bengard and Kommes with 48 strokes. Nelson came away with 55 strokes per 9-hole course.
There will be no girls on the team this season, but the boys do have one returner, who had 52 strokes during a 9-hole course during his sophomore season.
'We lost a lot from last year and only have one returner in Josh Nelson,' Petersen said. 'He has really improved from last year and has worked at it. We have some new faces that will try to get other spots.'
Some new faces are joining the program during their senior season, including Cole Brabham, Aiden Flathers, Jameson Kilworth, and Quintinn White.
'I really just want them to have fun,' Petersen added. 'It is going to be difficult for them, but I just want to see improvement throughout the season.'
The Spartans will play at multiple courses including Avoca Countryview Golf and Grille, Crestwood Hills Golf Course, Dunlap Golf Club, 5 x 80 Golf Course, and Crestwood Hills Golf Course, while playing multiple schools per competition, each of which Petersen talked about.
'We get to play a lot of courses within our conference and each one presents a challenge,' he said. 'That's what makes golf so much fun for the kids.'
The Spartans will compete in the Rolling Valley Conference against five other schools. Petersen talked about who he feels will be the biggest challenge.
'CAM will be the front runner I think this year in our conference,' he added.

title: Wingert commits to Peru State for cross country
author: Alex Martin
description: Cyclone Senior Lauren Wingert will be continuing her cross country career at the collegiate level following the conclusion of her high school days at Peru State. 'I started running cross country when I was in 7th grade, and just kept running,' Wingert added. Like most students, Wingert had multiple college options in front of her, but talked about what made her choose Peru State.
content:
Cyclone Senior Lauren Wingert will be continuing her cross country career at the collegiate level following the conclusion of her high school days at Peru State.
'I am super excited to get to run with new amazing people at Peru State,' Wingert said. 'Getting to compete at a college level is going to be so much fun and push me to my limits. I am glad I am able to have this opportunity to continue my cross country career.'
The love for running developed at a young age and continued to grow from there.
'I started running cross country when I was in 7th grade, and just kept running,' Wingert added. 'I saw so much improvement throughout the years that I just loved having the opportunity to push myself harder than ever.'
Like most students, Wingert had multiple college options in front of her, but talked about what made her choose Peru State.
'I settled on Peru State when my oldest sister started college,' she said. 'It just became a family tradition. I have two older sisters that have graduated from Peru State and when I join them this fall, my third sister will be starting her fifth and final year down in Peru. I have liked the environment down there. I liked how the school wasn't too big and not too small.'
Wingert comes from a strong family that has supported her every step of the way including three older sister, along with her mom and dad, Laura and Dan.
'My family has made me stronger every day,' she added. 'The support they give me everyday is one of the best feelings you could ever ask for. They just want what is best for me, and their support has made me push myself harder each and every day.'
During her high school cross country career Wingert was coached by Zach Klaassen. Wingert said Klaassen was a great mentor through the years.
'No matter how many coaches I have had or will have, Coach Klaassen has treated everyone equally on the team,' Wingert said. 'He made me a better version of myself. He wants us to push ourselves at every practice to show that we matter and can push through the pain. Coach Klaassen will always be one of the best coaches I could have asked for. I don't think I would be where I am today without his coaching.'

content:
AVOCA - It didn't take long for the Logan-Magnolia Panthers to set the tone Friday night against the AHSTW Vikings girls soccer team as Junior Panther Brooklyn Lally scored in the first two minutes, which would be all the Panthers would need to earn a 3-0 win, handing the Vikings their 5 th loss.
'We've been working really hard in practice, and we try to reflect that in a game,' said Senior Saydi Paulsen. 'We're working as a team, so we're just trying to keep getting better every day. That's what we're focusing on.'
Junior Panther Bella Rosengren added the second goal of the game, her first of the night approaching the 8-minute mark of the first half giving the Panthers a 2-0 lead at halftime.
When the second half began, both teams went quiet on offense, until Rosengren scored another goal 12 minutes into the second half, which would be the final goal of the night, giving the Panthers their second victory of the season.
Following the game, Paulsen and Ella Langer got honored during senior night for their contributions to the soccer program.
'It felt pretty good,' Paulsen said. 'I've been out all four years, so it was nice to have that recognition. We give so much to the community, and just to have them support us was really nice.'
The Vikings will return to action Tuesday at home at 5 p.m. welcoming the 4-3 Tri-Center Trojans to town. The Trojans are led by Quincey Schneckloth eight goals, Alexis Flaharty with six assists, and goalkeeper Macie Schneckloth with 56 saves.
'We just plan to work on getting better everyday,' Paulsen added. 'Working on skills, even if we don't come out on top, we're just working together and getting better as people.'

title: Lewis Central Co-Ed Track Event
author: Alex Martin
description: The HCHS Cyclones girls track and field team earned a fourth place finish at the Lewis Central Co-Ed Track event Wednesday with 64.5 points, finishing 133.5 points behind the winner, Waukee NW. On the track, Lindsey Sonderman finished 2 nd in the 1500 and 3000m run with times of 4:54.59 and 10:30.66, finishing behind Lili Denton of St. Albert in both events. Sonderman also competed in the distance medley event Abby Broeckelman, Wegner, and Dani Smith, helping lead them to a second place finish with 4:27.28, finishing behind Waukee NW, who won the event with 4:25.25.
content:
HCHS Girls
The HCHS Cyclones girls track and field team earned a fourth place finish at the Lewis Central Co-Ed Track event Wednesday with 64.5 points, finishing 133.5 points behind the winner, Waukee NW.
'This was a huge meet with great competition,' said Cyclone Head Coach Jenny Hamilton. 'Overall, a very positive meet for us. We're getting better every time out, and that's the most important thing.'
In field events, Aubree Wegner took a fourth place finish in the high jump event with a jump of 4-06.00. The event was won by Elaina Hesse of Clarinda with a jump of 5-00.00.
On the track, Lindsey Sonderman finished 2 nd in the 1500 and 3000m run with times of 4:54.59 and 10:30.66, finishing behind Lili Denton of St. Albert in both events.
Sonderman also competed in the distance medley event Abby Broeckelman, Wegner, and Dani Smith, helping lead them to a second place finish with 4:27.28, finishing behind Waukee NW, who won the event with 4:25.25.
'Lindsey had a full plate tonight and handled it well,' Hamilton said. 'She keeps chopping away at her 1500 and continues to stay ahead of where she was last year at this point.'
Other Cyclone highlights included Jaylee Schmitz finishing in third place in the 100m hurdles with 17.53, just 1.53 seconds behind Kamryn Vogt of Waukee NW who won the event with 16.00.
In relay races, the 4x400 team which featured Abby Broeckelman, Kami Stork, Paige Sonderman, and Wegner finished second with 4:24.48, finishing 23 seconds behind the winner, Waukee NW with 4:01.30. Broeckelman also ran strong in 400m hurdles with 1:09.59.
'Abby had a really great night,' Hamilton said. 'She gave us a great 400 hurdles run, than was about to turn-around and start the 4x400 off strong. That can be a tough turn around, but it's a challenge she enjoys and embraces.'
HCHS Boys
After an originally scheduled track event for Tuesday, Wednesday night at Lewis Central High School, the HCHS Cyclones boys track and field team earned themselves a fourth place finish with 78 points, 39.5 points behind the winner, Lewis Central.
'You have to be able to pivot, move, and adapt pretty quickly to the weather around you, because it can be nice in the morning and pretty crummy in the afternoon, and vice versa,' said Cyclone Head Coach Sam Brummer. 'Our kids did a great job. The weather was perfect. Much better to compete in on Wednesday. For what we did, a 4 th place finish was a pretty strong performance by the fellas.'
The Cyclones set the tone in the 100m dash event with two seniors taking the top two spots. Cade Sears won the event with 10.88, followed by Matthew Sorfonden finishing right behind him with 11.15.
'Our school record is 10.65, and I think Cade is definitely attainable for that,' Brummer said. 'Sorf can definitely get in the sub 11 range in that 10.80 or 10.70 range on a good day. Cade is still coming back from injury and fine-tuning things that he just missed through injuries. As long as we can keep everyone healthy and on the right track, I think we have a very good squad ready to make some noise in the upcoming weeks in the meets ahead.'
Sears, Sorfonden, Brehden Eggerss, and Lukas Francis turned in some dominant performances in multiple events. In the 4x100 meter relay, they finished first with a time of 42.63, just 1+ second ahead of Treynor, who finished with 44.05. In the 4x200 meter relay, they finished with a time of 1:29.57, 2+ seconds ahead of Treynor with 1:31.81.
'It was nice to get those four guys back in the fold,' Brummer added. 'We haven't had any of them since really the first meet of the year at the Iowa State indoor, which would have been March 7. We're just playing the long game, and making sure we bring them back to run, that they're healthy and able to run up to as close of a standard as they were before injuries, especially with sprinters. We don't want to rush them back before they're ready.'
In 110m hurdles, Franz Reisz took an eighth place finish with 17.40, with Bryce Van Baale right on his tail at 17.76, just a few seconds behind Brady Wallace of Treynor, who won the event with 15.10.
Van Baale also shined in the 400m hurdle event finishing the event in just under one minute with a time of 59.71, taking sixth overall, just 5+ seconds behind the winner Karson Elwood of Treynor with 54.43.
'That 400 lows is a tough race,' Brummer said. 'You talk to anybody who's ran track, that's a race you have to have a little bit different of a mindset for because it just hits different. Each time he [Van Baale] runs it, I think his best is around 58.5 this year, and lastly I think there are like four or five Drake qualifiers in that race, so to finish sixth behind those guys is no slouching task. Bryce is a worker, wants to improve, and is willing to put in the time to get better.'
In field events, the Cyclones took a lot of second place finishes between Dallas McDowell in the high jump with 5-08.00, finishing behind Gavin Ahrendt of Sergeant Bluff-Luton with 5-10.00, Eggerss in long jump with a jump of 21-10.00 finishing behind Mason Boothby of Underwood with 22-00.75, and Reisz in discus with a throw of 154-11, finishing behind Maxwell Tiarks of Underwood with 166-10.
'Field events is something we continue to get better at each week,' Brummer added. 'A lot of track is repetition. All three of them have definitely benefitted from meet reps and going out and competing. Dallas is really starting to hit his stride with high jump, he just needs to continue to get the reps to get at that bar. Eggs is obviously one of the more consistent jumpers in the area with always hovering around that upper 21 and flirting with 22 every now and then. Franz is continuing to PRing. He PR'd last night in discus.'
The Cyclones won't rest for long as they will be back in action Thursday at 4:30 p.m. at the Tigers Relays at Carroll Athletic Stadium where they will be one of 11 schools competing.
'We have most of our guys running tonight that did not run last night, and guys that did run will take most of the night off,' Brummer said. 'Should be relatively fresh, but as mother nature calls, you just adapt and figure out what works best for you. With our team right now and close we are to the end, we don't want to run the risk of losing anybody long term.'
